The EGFR exon 21 K860I mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has not been functionally characterized. However, it has been observed to co-occur with known oncogenic EGFR mutations, including L861Q and L858R, in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 19060236). Three lung adenocarcinoma patients with K860I mutations that co-occurred with other TKI-sensitive alterations (e.g., L858R, L861Q) responded to gefitinib therapy with partial response or stable disease, respectively (PMID: 19060236, 19536777).

The EGFR exon 18 G719S mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 21531810). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitizing to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), erlotinib (PMID: 16187797, 29141884). Preclinical models with a mutation at the EGFR G719 position show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In EGFR TKI-naive patients (N=62), afatinib demonstrated activity against tumors with EGFR G719 mutation (PMID: 31931137). In a clinical study evaluating patients with NSCLC with "uncommon" EGFR mutations, a majority of mutations occurred at position G719 or L861 (45%, 28/62), and both these mutation sites were associated with sensitivity to EGFR TKIs (erlotinib or gefitinib) with a response rate of 57.1%; median PFS, 6.0 months. Specifically, in this study, one patient with the G719S mutation in conjunction with Q701L and I706T had a partial response to EGFR TKIs while another patient with the G719S mutation in conjunction with the L861Q mutation had stable disease (PMID: 21531810). In a Phase II trial of osimertinib in Korean patients with NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations, ten of nineteen patients with a G719 substitution had an objective response, with a median progression-free survival of 8.2 months (PMID: 31825714).

The EGFR exon 19 K745_A750del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR K745_A750del mutation had a partial response to treatment with erlotinib lasting 5.8 months (PMID: 25179728).

The EGFR V834I mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by slightly increased focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR L861P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 22805266). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L861P and EGFR L858R was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 18000506). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L861P was treated with afatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 3.7 months (PMID: 31931137). In a case study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L861P was treated with pembrolizumab,  pemetrexed and carboplatin and demonstrated a progression-free survival of 10 months (Abstract: Vundemodalu et al. Abstract# e21170, ASCO 2021. https://meetings.asco.org/abstracts-presentations/200957).

The EGFR K806E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K806E was treated with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 28717642). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K806E was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 7 months (PMID: 18676761).

The EGFR V300M mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 32406930). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is inactivating as measured by a lower predictive EGFR pathway activation score than wildtype (PMID: 32406930).

The EGFR G652R mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in transitional cell carcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with HEK293T cells expressing EGFR G652R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by ligand-independent EGFR activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 36148499).

The EGFR E746_A750del mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain in exon 19 of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 18508816, 22483783, 16467085, 18325048, 15897572, 25179728, 18261621, 15710947). In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitive to gefitinib (PMID: 16373402, 29141884). Across many clinical studies, patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR E746_A750del have had clinical benefit from treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 18508816, 22483783, 16467085, 18325048, 15897572, 25179728, 18261621, 15710947).

The EGFR P741S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma and colorectal cancer (PMID: 32321774, 27756406). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR P741S demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream activation and transformation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 31314158).

The EGFR L703F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L703F was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 18000506).

The EGFR exon 16 C628Y mutation occurs in EGFR extracellular domain IV. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation did not alter EGFR activity as measured by EGFR autophosphorylation when compared to wildtype (PMID: 24747966).

The EGFR G63R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in glioma (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR G63R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation and phosphorylated EGFR, AKT and STAT5 compared to wildtype (PMID: 31290142). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 and NIH3T3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with erlotinib, cetuximab, panitumumab, afatinib and dacomitinib as measured by decreased cellular viability and inhibition of anchorage-independent growth following treatment (PMID: 31290142).

The EGFR exon 18 E709A mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 20479403, 23242437, 21531810, 15710947, 23566546, 18261621, 21841502, 23749122, 22483783). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and resistant to gefitinib, especially when found in combination with other EGFR-activating alleles (PMID: 19671738, 29141884, 19671738). However, multiple patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E709A mutation as a primary or compound mutation experienced responses to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors neratinib, erlotinib, or gefitinib that met RECIST criteria (PMID: 20479403, 23242437, 21531810, 15710947, 23566546, 18261621, 21841502, 23749122, 22483783). This mutation more commonly occurs in combination with other EGFR mutations, including G719S and L858R (PMID: 18372921).

The EGFR G857R mutation is located in the activation loop of the catalytic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 15863375). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring EGFR G857R was treated with gefitinib and progressed during treatment (PMID: 16012179).

The EGFR exon 20 A767_V769del occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While the explicit function of the EGFR A767_V769del has not been characterized, insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). Consistently, in a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR A767_V769del alteration had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR R222C mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 19 V742A mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitizing to gefitinib, erlotinib and AEE788 (PMID: 19147750, 23605641). The EGFR V742A mutation was identified in two patients with non-small cell lung cancer who experienced stable disease following treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 16152581, 21531810).

The gene S464L mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancers with resistance to the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (PMID: 25623215). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced EGFR autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25623215). An in vitro resistance screen in colorectal cancer cell lines identified EGFR S464L as an extracellular domain mutation that conferred resistance to EGFR antibodies such as cetuximab, and structural modeling showed that the S464L mutation prevents the binding of cetuximab and panitumumab to EGFR (PMID: 25623215). In cfDNA studies of patients with colorectal cancer who progressed on treatment with EGFR-targeted antibodies, the EGFR S464L mutation was identified in 30 patients either as one of many EGFR-pathway mutations (n=27) or as a single EGFR-pathway mutation (n=3) that could explain progression on cetuximab or panitumumab (PMID: 29423521, 29196463).
The exon 21 EGFR E865K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Studies in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that this mutation is likely transforming (PMID: 29141884).

The exon 19 EGFR L747_T751del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and sensitive to erlotinib (PMID: 23387505 ). Across three clinical studies, three patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_T751del mutation alone or in combination with the R776S mutation had a partial response (two of three) or non-progressive disease (one of three) to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 18325048, 15897572, 23242437).

The EGFR Y764_D770dup mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein.  This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26286086). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, in vitro studies of kinase domain duplication mutations have demonstrated that they are activating as measured by constitutive EGFR signaling through the formation of intramolecular dimers (PMID: 23371856, 30255937, 24353160).

The EGFR exon 20 R776G mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, other substitutions at this position (e.g., R776C/H) are activating and relatively resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) erlotinib and gefitinib (PMID: 19147750). One patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR R776G mutation in combination with the known oncogenic and TKI-sensitive EGFR L858R mutation had progressive disease following treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18676761).

The EGFR L718V mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been identified in patients with non-small lung cancer (NSCLC) in conjunction with EGFR L858R following treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 29571986, 31301016, 31757379). Expression of EGFR L718V in combination with L858R in Ba/F3 cells results in enhanced IL-3 independent growth compared to cells expressing EGFR L858R alone. Additionally, these double mutant cells retain sensitivity to afatinib, and a patient with NSCLC harboring EGFR L858R and L718V achieved a partial response following treatment with afatinib (PMID: 29571986, 29568384, 31757379, 32193290). In silico studies demonstrated that EGFR L718V likely introduces structural protein changes that prevent osimertinib binding to EGFR (PMID: 29571986, 29568384). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L718V and EGFR L858R was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 23749122).

The EGFR-SEPT14 fusion protein is a fusion between the N terminus of the EGFR protein through exon 24 and the C-terminal coiled-coil domain of the SEPT14 protein from exon 10 (PMID: 23917401). This fusion has been found recurrently in glioblastoma and is often associated with concurrent chromosomal amplification (PMID: 23917401, PMID: 26762204)(Abstract: Di Stefano et al. Abstract# 06.07. FGFR3-TACC3 AND EGFR-SEPT14 GENE FUSIONS IN ADULT GLIOMAS. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4185815/pdf/nou174.48.pdf.). Expression of this alteration in glioma cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased proliferation, migration, and activation of the STAT3 pathway compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 23917401). In vitro studies also demonstrate that this alteration is sensitive to EGFR inhibition with erlotinib or lapatinib (PMID: 23917401).

The EGFR A743V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 26873401, 24040454). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A743V was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23749122). In silico analysis suggests that EGFR A743V confers resistance to treatment with EGFR inhibitors due to reduced binding affinity (PMID: 29369805).

The EGFR exon 23 I941R mutation occurs in the EGFR autophosphorylation domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation impairs EGFR activation and prevents colony formation in soft agar (PMID: 24063894)

The EGFR P589L mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR R98Q mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in BA/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR V592I mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is likely neutral as colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF when expressed in NIH3T3 cells was similar to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28979142).

The EGFR exon 20 V769_D770insASV mutation lies in the loop following the EGFR C helix. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24353160). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and resistant to erlotinib (PMID: 24353160). Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). Consistently, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR V769_D770insASV mutation had progressive disease in response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR exon 15 C620Y mutation occurs in Domain IV of the EGFR extracellular domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitizing to lapatinib and to low doses of the pan-ErbB inhibitor, dacomitinib (PMID: 24747966).

The EGFR exon 20 C797S mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this variant has not been functionally characterized per se, across multiple studies cells transformed with EGFR containing the L858R, T790M and C797S mutations in cis were resistant to growth inhibition by osimertinib (AZD9291) and rociletinib (CO-1686) compared to cells transformed with EGFR containing only L858R and T790M in cis, suggesting this mutation confers resistance to osimertinib and rociletinib in cell lines (PMID: 25939061, 25964297). Multiple patients with EGFR T790M+ non-small cell lung cancer who progressed on osimertinib after initially responding to the drug have shown acquisition of an EGFR C797S mutation in their post-treatment samples (PMID: 25939061, 26181354, 26749488, 28625641, 30073261). Preclinical studies suggest that the EGFR C797S mutation may be sensitive to the combination of an allosteric EGFR inhibitor (EAI045) with an anti-EGFR antibody such as cetuximab (PMID: 27251290). Preclinical models with classical EGFR activating mutations together with the T790M and C797S mutations show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, but moderate sensitivity to PKC and ALK inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Preclinical models with the C797S mutation alone show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Additionally, in vitro studies suggest that the C797 residue may be crucial for EGFR dimerization (PMID: 26378037). Preclinical studies with mobocertinib-resistant Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations identified EGFR C797S as a secondary resistance mutation (PMID: 37666482).

The EGFR L862V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L862V was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 2.0 months (PMID: 21841502).

The exon 19 EGFR K745_E746insIPVAIK mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Although not functionally characterized per se, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing in-frame deletion and insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 19 of EGFR demonstrate that they are activating, suggesting that EGFR K745_E746insIPVAIK is likely activating (PMID: 15329413, 15118073, 21841502, 15118125). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR K745_E746insIPVAIK demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with erlotinib, afatinib, osimertinib and mobocertinib as measured by reduced cell viability following treatment (PMID: 37196448). In a clinical analysis, patients with lung adenocarcinoma harboring this mutation were treated with erlotinib (n=3), afatinib (n=1) and osimertinib (n=1) and demonstrated partial response and stable disease (PMID: 37196448).

The EGFR Q181H mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is likely neutral as colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF when expressed in NIH3T3 cells was similar to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28979142).

The EGFR K129E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in hepatocellular carcinoma (PMID: 25159915). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is tolerated and benign (PMID: 30093630).

The EGFR exon 20 L792F mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this variant has not been functionally validated as a single alteration, Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR L792F in conjunction with exon 19 deletion and T790M were resistant to osimertinib in vitro (PMID: 29506987). Four patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L792F mutations in combination with other EGFR mutations (T790M, G796S/R, L792F/H, C797S/G, V802F) progressed on treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 28625641, 28093244, 27913578).

The EGFR P753Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P753Q, EGFR L747_S752del and EGFR T790M was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated slow progressive disease (PMID: 26857779).

The EGFR exon 21 L833V mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 25130612, 20808254, 21422421). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3, MCF10A and NIH3T3 cell lines demonstrated that this mutation is activating as demonstrated by IL-3 independent growth, EGF and insulin-independent growth and increased foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785, 29141884). Preclinical models with the L833V mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR L833V demonstrate resistance to treatment with gefitinib as measured by sustained cell viability following treatment (PMID: 29141884). Across three studies, patients with NSCLC harboring the EGFR L833V mutation in combination with the TKI-sensitizing EGFR L858R, G719A or H835L mutations had a partial response (two of five), complete response (one of five) or stable disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 25130612, 20808254, 21422421). Further, in an analysis of 860 patients with lung adenocarcinoma who were prospectively tested for actionable mutations, one patient (100%) with an EGFR L833V mutation in conjunction with an EGFR L858R substitution mutation who received EGFR TKI therapy and chemotherapy had clinical benefit (PMID: 28336552).

The EGFR exon 21 E884K mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation exhibits constitutive activity (PMID: 19015641). Cell line and clinical data suggests this mutation confers resistance to erlotinib but sensitivity to gefitinib in lung cancer patients harboring a double EGFR mutation of L858R + E884K (PMID: 19015641, 16407879). One patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring L858R + E884K EGFR mutations in cis responded to gefitinib after progressing on erlotinib (PMID: 16407879)

The EGFR exon 19 E746_T751delinsL mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_T751delinsL mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18261621).

The EGFR exon 20 L814P mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized it was identified in combination with several other EGFR mutations of unknown function (V765M, L798H, K806E) in two patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Both patients achieved a partial response following treatment with gefitnib (PMID: 16870303).

The EGFR F712S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 22026926). Although not functionally validated per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR F712S, EGFR E868G and EGFR D855G was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 16870303).
The EGFR R977C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is deleterious and affects dimer stability (PMID: 20049516).

The gene T725M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancers, among others (PMID: 24743239, 31931137). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased gene autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24743239). The gene T725M mutation has been identified as a possible sensitizing mutation to the kinase inhibitor afatinib and preclinical models with the T725M mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 31931137, 34526717).

The EGFR E707K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E707K and EGFR L858R was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 14.7 months and an overall survival of 26.5+ months (PMID: 23912954).

EGFR C-terminal deletion or truncating variants (EGFR CTD) are the result of intragenic deletions in the carboxyl-terminal domain of the gene. This mutation accounts for approximately 5 to 7% of the EGFR mutations in glioblastoma (PMID: 24292886, 24120142, 23007009). Deletions resulting in the EGFR CTD mutant may be in exons 25-26, 25-27 or 25-28, immediately downstream of the kinase domain (PMID: 23007009, 20676128, 24292886). These deletions are associated with constitutive activation of EGFR due to constitutive dimerization of the receptor (PMID: 23007009). Additionally, expression of EGFR CTD in mouse hematopoietic cells was associated with ligand-independent increased cell growth and sensitivity to EGFR TKI erlotinib and EGFR monoclonal antibody cetuximab (PMID: 22001862).

The EGFR exon 21 R841K mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as it did not respond to ligand stimulation and did not alter cell proliferation or downstream pathway activation (PMID: 18193092).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_P753delinsS alteration occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413) and this is true of L747_P753delinsS which is found to be activating, transforming and sensitizing to EGFR TKIs (PMID: 19147750, 15118073).  Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR L747_P753delinsS demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with erlotinib, afatinib, osimertinib and mobocertinib as measured by reduced cell viability following treatment (PMID: 37196448). Across five clinical studies, eight patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_P753delinsS mutation derived clinical benefit from treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib, with six patients having a partial response, one patient having stable disease, and one patient exhibiting tumor marker decrease (PMID: 18508816, 15897572, 25179728, 15710947, 15118073).

The EGFR Q105H mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 21 E866K mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domian (PMID: 19147750). Expression of EGFR E866K results in a kinase-dead EGF-receptor that is associated with absence of EGFR autophosphorylation upon ligand exposure and this mutation is unable to transform cells (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR A289V mutation occurs in the EGFR extracellular domain in exon 7 and is often associated with increased EGFR copy number (PMID: 17177598, 24120142). This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 17177598). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is an activating and transforming mutation (PMID: 17177598, 29141884). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) erlotinib, gefitinib and lapatinib (PMID: 17177598, 22588883).

The EGFR E746_L747delinsIP mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 generally result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). A patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR E746_L747delinsIP was treated with afatinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 35712479).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_A750del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_A750del mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 16467085).

The EGFR V148M mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 21 L861R mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 17177598, 24743239). Cell line experiments demonstrate that his mutation is activating (PMID: 24743239). While transforming ability of EGFR L861R has not been described, other amino acid substitutions at this residue (such as L861Q) are transforming (PMID: 17177598, 21252719). Preclinical models with the L861Q mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, thirgeneration, and ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717), and in two clinical studies, patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L861R mutation alone or in combination with the EGFR R831C mutation had partial response (two of three) or progressive disease (one of three) in response to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 21531810, 21841502).

The EGFR exon 8 R324L mutation occurs in the EGFR extracellular domain (ECD). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming. Molecular modeling of this mutation suggests that the mechanism of its activity involves stabilizing EGFR dimerization (PMID: 24212795, 17177598) and thereby promoting EGFR activation.

The EGFR A611T mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines was inconclusive, as it led to decreased cell viability in Ba/F3 cells but increased cell viability in MCF10A cells compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The gene G719C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancers (PMID: 21531810, 15118073). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased clonogenic growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 29141884). Drug efficacy studies in cell lines and murine models demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to gene tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 29141884, 31931137).  The gene G719C mutation has also been identified as broadly sensitive to kinase inhibitors, including osimertinib, in a Phase II clinical trial (PMID: 15118073, 21531810, 21841502, 18261621, 31825714, Abstract: Chen et al. JCO Precision Oncology 2024 Vol 8, Number 8. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.23.00454).

The EGFR A871V is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 16152581, 26164066). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A871V and an EGFR exon 19 deletion was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_A750delinsQ mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_A750delinsQ mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 19.2 months (PMID: 17192902).

The EGFR E282K mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR A750T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and gastric cancer (PMID: 26373574, 29307989). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A750T was treated with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 23749122).

The EGFR exon 21 L838V mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming and resistant to erlotinib, gefitinib and AEE788 (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR exon 3 R108K mutation occurs in the ligand binding region of the EGFR extracellular domain (PMID: 17177598). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming, and sensitive to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 17177598). The R108K mutation of EGFR is often associated with increased EGFR copy number (PMID: 24120142, 17177598). The EGFR R108K mutation is activating, occurs in the extracellular domain of EGFR and has been found in multiple glioblastoma samples (PMID: 17177598). The FDA-approved EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor erlotinib was demonstrated to induce dose-dependent cell death in cells engineered to express this mutation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 17177598).

The EGFR A763V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 25589618). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A763V and an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation was treated with bevacizumab and achieved a complete response with an overall survival of 827 days and a progression-free survival of 689 days (PMID: 26773740). In a clinical analysis, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A763V was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 1.9 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR R803W mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 26214590). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R803W and mutated ALK was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 0.7 months (PMID: 27086595). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R803W and EGFR delE746_T751insVA was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated non-progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 7.7 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR H773_V774insNPH mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717). Expression of this mutation in cell lines demonstrated it was likely activating as measured by increased transformation potential in vitro compared to wildtype (PMID: 31108249). Preclinical models with the H773_V774insNPH mutation show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and moderate sensitivity to Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). A patient-derived xenograft model with the EGFR H773_V774insNPH mutation showed high sensitivity to poziotinib (PMID: 29686424).

The EGFR K806A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K806A was treated with gefitinib followed by a second-line therapy and demonstrated progressive disease to both treatments (PMID: 19536777).

The HMGA2-EGFR fusion protein involves exons 1 through 3 of HMGA2, which contain the three DNA-binding domains, fused to the transmembrane and kinase domains of EGFR. This fusion protein has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 29193056). Expression of the HMGA2-EGFR fusion in U87MG human glioma cell lines demonstrated that the alteration is activating as measured by increased tumor formation (PMID: 29193056). Treatment with the EGFR kinase inhibitor erlotinib in TGS-01 cells expressing the fusion protein demonstrated sensitivity and inhibited tumor growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 29193056).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insD mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR D770_N771insD mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18676761).

The EGFR V765A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 14.7 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR Y891D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 30922578). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR Y891D demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by phosphorylation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 38182677). Preclinical studies of Ba/F3 cells expressing both EGFR L858R and EGFR Y891D demonstrate that EGFR Y891D is associated with resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors through destabilization of the EGFR L858R protein as measured by increased cellular viability following treatment compared to the EGFR L858R-mutant control (PMID: 38182677). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L858R acquired EGFR Y891D as a secondary resistance mutation following treatment with erlotinib (PMID: 30922578). In a second case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L858R and EGFR A859S acquired EGFR Y891D as a secondary resistance mutation following treatment with icotinib and conferred resistance to osimertinib (PMID: 33324543).

The EGFR D770_N771insNPG mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung carcinomas (PMID: 34526717). Expression of this mutation in cell lines demonstrated it was likely activating as measured by increased transformation potential in vitro compared to wildtype (PMID: 31108249), and expression in a genetically engineered mouse model resulted in the formation of lung tumors that were sensitive to poziotinib (PMID: 29686424). Preclinical models with the D770_N771insNPG mutation show resistance to first- and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR H850D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was identified in myelodysplastic syndrome (PMID: 24030381). Although not functionally characterized per se, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR H850D and EGFR L858R were treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease and progressive disease, respectively (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR exon 20 H773Y mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, other substitutions at this position (e.g., H773L) have been shown to be activating and oncogenic (PMID: 17974985). Two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring a compound H773Y mutation and EGFR exon 20 insertion failed to respond to gefitinib treatment (PMID: 19536777, 18676761).

The EGFR exon 19 I744_K745delinsKIPVAI mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR I744_K745delinsKIPVAI mutation had a partial response to treatment with erlotinib lasting 7 months (PMID: 21841502).

The EGFR K754E mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Xenograft experiments using an immortalized human lung epithelial cell line expressing this mutation demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 27478040). Preclinical models with the K754E mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717)

EGFR amplification results from the gain of extra copies of the EGFR gene on chromosome 7p11. Often, this leads to the overexpression of EGFR protein and hyperactivation of downstream signaling through the MAPK pathway (PMID: 24120142, 10728703). EGFR amplification is found across various cancers, including lung adenocarcinoma, esophageal carcinoma and glioma (PMID: 25079552, 28052061, 24120142). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that EGFR amplification in primary glioma sphere-forming cell samples results in sensitivity to the PARP inhibitor talazoparib as measured by decreased viability and reduced tumor growth in a xenograft model upon drug treatment (PMID: 31852834). Patients with non-small cell lung cancer who harbor amplification of wildtype or tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-sensitive mutant EGFR have shown clinical benefit in response to EGFR TKIs (PMID: 30622811, 30284706). Additionally, EGFR amplification has been associated with sensitivity to HER2 inhibition with afatinib in HER2+ esophagogastric cancer (PMID: 30463996). A patient with salivary gland cancer harboring high-level EGFR amplification had a durable, near-complete response to treatment with afatinib (Abstract: Lai et al. JCO PO, 2019. https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.19.00186).

In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Preclinical models with exon 19 deletions show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation and ex20ins-active inhibitors (PMID: 34526717), and based on 119 patients across ten clinical studies, the clinical benefit rate of gefitinib or erlotinib in patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions is 89% (PMID: 17192902, 18000506, 18458038, 19536777, 22019513, 22760226, 23559152, 23566546, 23749122, 24457318). The drugs afatinib, erlotinib and gefitinib are FDA-approved for treatment of patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR exon 19 deletions.

The EGFR exon 21 N826S mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming and resistant to erlotinib, gefitinib and AEE788 (PMID: 19147750). However, in one study of 33 patients with non-small cell lung cancer, one patient with an N826S EGFR mutation had stable disease in response to gefitinib treatment lasting 6.7 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR exon 20 L792H mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this variant has not been functionally validated as a single alteration, Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR L792H in conjunction with exon 19 deletion and T790M were resistant to osimertinib in vitro, and preclinical models with the L792H mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 29506987, 29857056, 34526717). Fourteen patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L792H mutation in combination with other EGFR mutations (L858R, T790M) progressed on treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 29857056, 28625641, 28093244, 29506987).

The EGFR L747V mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR P596L mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 20 S768I mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 23912954, 23242437, 19536777, 25179728, 25130612, 18676761, 25521406, 25521405). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating (PMID: 16205628), and transforming (PMID: 19147750, 29141884). In vitro studies demonstrate that EGFR S768I confers resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) relative to other EGFR TKI sensitizing mutations such as L858R (PMID:19147750, 16205628). Preclinical models with the S768I mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Preclinical models with the S768I and T790M mutations show resistance to first- and second-generation EGFR inhibitors, high sensitivity to third-generation EGFR inhibitors and moderate sensitivity to PKC and ALK inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Reports of clinical sensitivity to TKIs in patients harboring the mutation have been varied (PMID: 23912954, 23242437, 19536777, 25179728, 25130612, 18676761, 25521406, 25521405). Across eight clinical studies, thirteen patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR S768I mutation alone or in combination with erlotinib- and gefitinib-sensitive EGFR L858R, G719A or exon 19 deletion mutations had partial response (eight of thirteen), stable disease (two of thirteen) or progressive disease (three of thirteen), respectively, in response to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 23912954, 23242437, 19536777, 25179728, 25130612, 18676761, 25521406, 25521405). In a Phase II trial of osimertinib in Korean patients with NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations, three of eight patients with an S768I substitution had an objective response, with a median progression-free survival of 12.3 months (PMID: 31825714).

The gene G863D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung and gastric cancers, among others (PMID: 16204011, 21436633). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely activating as measured by increased EGFR levels and enhanced downstream signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 17376509). The gene G863D mutation has been identified in patients as a potential sensitizing mutation to the EGFR inhibitor gefitinib (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_T751delinsVA mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In two studies, patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_T751delinsVA mutation alone or in combination had partial response or non-progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 18508816, 15897572).

The EGFR exon 21 E868G mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and sensitive to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 20942962). The EGFR E868G mutation was found in combination with the EGFR F712S and D855G mutations in a patient with non small cell lung (NSCLC) cancer who experienced a partial response to gefitnib treatment defined by RECIST criteria. A second patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR E868G and L838P mutations experienced progressive disease (PMID: 16870303).

The EGFR N826Y mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR N826Y was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 3.3 months and an overall survival of 13.9 months (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR exon 20 D770_N771insVDSVDNP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 21841502). Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR D770_N771insVDSVDNP mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 21841502).

The EGFR L747F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L747F was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 122 days and overall survival of 211 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EGFR G874S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (PMID: 21070477). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G874S was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 18000506). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G847S and EGFR I706T was treated with combination erlotinib plus bevacizumab and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of 423 days and an overall survival of 444 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EGFR G428D mutation occurs in the extracellular domain of the protein. Homozygous mutations in EGFR G428D have been reported in a lethal neonatal syndrome with epithelial dysfunction. Patient-derived EGFR G428D fibroblasts were unable to bind to EGF and underwent early senescence, pointing to a loss-of-function effect (PMID:26436111).

EGFR R252C mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. While expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR, other substitutions at this position are considered likely oncogenic, and this mutation is a statistically significant hotspot in glioma (PMID: 29533785, 26619011).

The EGFR exon 21 L858R mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming, and sensitizing to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) (PMID: 15118073, 15118125). Preclinical models with the L858R mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second- and third-generation inhibitors, and to Ex20ins-active inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Patients with lung cancers harboring the L858R mutation responded to EGFR TKIs with overall survival ranging from 3.5-17+ months after starting treatment (PMID: 15329413).

The EGFR G598A mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 20 S784F mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming and mildly sensitive to erlotinib, gefitinib and AEE788 (PMID: 19147750, 20522446). In two clinical studies, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR S784F mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 21531810, 21841502).

The EGFR E758G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 16152581). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with lung cancer harboring EGFR E758G was treated with afatinib and demonstrated a median progression-free survival of 34.9 months (PMID: 35263633). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E758G and EGFR L858R was treated with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810). Another patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E758G and EGFR L858R was treated with gefitinib and responded to treatment (PMID: 19536777).

The EGFR P753S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 25148578). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma harboring EGFR P753S was treated with a combination therapy of cetuximab plus sirolimus and demonstrated a dramatic and sustained response to treatment (PMID: 24934779). In clinical studies, patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P753S in combination with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor-sensitive EGFR L858R or EGFR exon 19 deletion mutations treated with gefitinib demonstrated stable disease or partial response (PMID: 16467085, 25130612).

The EGFR exon 20 S768T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 22810696). In a Phase II clinical trial, a patient with neuroendocrine carcinoma harboring the EGFR G719C and S768T mutations was treated with osimertinib and demonstrated partial response (Abstract: Chen et al. JCO Precision Oncology 2024 Vol 8, Number 8. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.23.00454).

The EGFR exon 7 M277E mutation occurs within the EGFR extracellular domain. This mutation has been found in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Expression of this mutation in cell line and xenograft experiments demonstrated that it is activating and transforming as shown by increased proliferation compared to cells expressing wildtype EGFR. In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to growth inhibition by the EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor erlotinib and EGFR monoclonal antibody cetuximab (PMID: 28979142).

The EGFR E709G mutation lies in the kinase of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR G873E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was identified in non-small cell lung cancer and biliary tract cancer (PMID: 16567021, 24372748). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR G873E demonstrate resistance to treatment with gefitinib as measured by sustained cell viability following treatment (PMID: 29141884). In a case report, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G873E and EGFR L858R were treated with erlotinib and gefitinib and both demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 146 days and 120 days, respectively (PMID: 30990107). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G873E, EGFR L858R and PIK3CA E542K was treated with combination therapy bevacizumab, cetuximab plus erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 23435217). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G873E and an EGFR exon 19 deletion was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 1.3 months and an overall survival of 5.3 months (PMID: 23912954).

Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). An important exception is EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA, which does appear to be sensitive to standard EGFR TKIs (PMID: 24353160). While afatinib, erlotinib and gefitinib are FDA-approved for the treatment of patients with lung cancer harboring exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R substitution mutations, most exon 20 mutations including 762_823ins mutation appear to confer resistance to EGFR TKIs erlotinib and gefinitinib. Exon 20 insertion mutations may be more reliant on Hsp90 than other forms of EGFR and may be sensitive to Hsp90 inhibition (PMID: 30154228).

The EGFR exon 20 R776C mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and relatively resistant to treatment with erlotinib, gefitinib or AEE788 in vitro (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR exon 20 A767_V769dup mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain in exon 20 of the protein. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). Across four clinical studies, six patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR A767_V769dup mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 23749122, 23912954, 19536777, 18676761).

The EGFR exon 20 P772_V774dup mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR P772_V774dup mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 25179728).

The EGFR V742I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in ovarian cancer, large-cell lung carcinoma and nasopharyngeal carcinoma (PMID: 33947352, 26317919, 28581676). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V742I was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23749122). EGFR V742I was identified as a potentially druggable mutation in patients with lung adenocarcinoma with erlotinib, gefitinib and lapatinib (PMID: 31749831).

The EGFR V802I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V802I and EGFR K852R was treated with vandetanib and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of 2.6 months and overall survival of 6.3 months (PMID: 23584298). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V802I was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 17062680).

The EGFR T783A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T783A was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 20 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR exon 21 P848L mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell lines experiments demonstrate that this mutation is not activating beyond wildtype EGFR (PMID: 22848293, 17877814). It has been hypothesized that this alteration can mask the EGFR inhibitor sensitizing mutation L858R (PMID: 23897956). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and brain metastases with this variant (germline) had progressive disease on chemotherapy and erlotinib-based therapy regimens (PMID: 25176975). However, a patient with the EGFR P848L mutation in combination with an erlotinib- and gefitinib-sensitive EGFR exon 19 deletion had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 6.9+ months (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR exon 21 F856V mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical studies with mobocertinib-resistant Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations identified EGFR F856V as a secondary resistance mutation (PMID: 37666482).

The EGFR L760P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in prostate cancer (PMID: 28481359, 28825054). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma with brain metastases harboring EGFR L760P was treated with icotinib and demonstrated a favorable response (PMID: 26767025).

The EGFR A1118S mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 28573640).

The EGFR E711_F712del mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E711_F712del was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 1.4 months and overall survival of over 44.8 months (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR S229C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR P596S mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR D247Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 26960396). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with glioblastoma harboring EGFR D247Y, EGFR P596L and EGFR G598V was treated with afatinib plus temozolomide and demonstrated significant disease regression (PMID: 26423602).

The EGFR A508V mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is likely neutral as colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF when expressed in NIH3T3 cells was similar to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28979142).

The EGFR exon 21 A859T mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain and is adjacent to the gefitinib-sensitive L858 mutation. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation does not result in increased downstream signaling and does not confer sensitivity to erlotinib (PMID: 17877814). However, this mutation was observed in a single patient with non-small cell lunger cancer (NSCLC) who had a partial response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 21317745), a single patient with NSCLC who demonstrated progressive disease following gefitnib treatment (PMID: 15710947), and a single patient with NSCLC also harboring the L858R mutation who had stable disease following gefitinib treatment (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR exon 19 A750_E758del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR A750_E758del mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18325048).

The EGFR D855G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR D855G, EGFR F712S and EGFR E868G was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 16870303). In silico analysis suggests that EGFR D855G confers resistance to treatment with erlotinib, gefitinib and neratinib (PMID: 29369805).

The EGFR M178I mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR T363I mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

EGFR exon 19 insertions occur in the kinase domain of EGFR. In vitro expression of exon 19 insertions (including 744_K745insKIPVAI and K745_E746insTPVAIK) demonstrate that they are transforming (PMID: 17133113 ) and sensitive to the EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) gefitnib and afatnib, as shown by decreased cell proliferation and decreased EGFR phosphorylation similar to TKI-treated cells expressing EGFR exon 19 deletion mutations (PMID: 22190593). Preclinical models with exon 19 deletions show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation and ex20ins-active inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In a retrospective study of patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), five of six patients with tumors harboring EGFR exon 19 insertions (2 of 2 patients in the neoadjuvant setting and 3 of 4 patients with advanced disease) had partial responses to EGFR TKIs, including one patient who achieved a 14 month-partial response upon treatment with afatinib (PMID: 22190593). Further, in an analysis of 860 patients with lung adenocarcinoma who were prospectively tested for actionable mutations, one patient with an EGFR exon 19 insertion who received EGFR TKI therapy had clinical benefit (PMID: 28336552). In a separate retrospective study of 2664 patients with NSCLC, 2 patients with EGFR exon 19 insertions received TKI therapy; one patient treated with erlotinib had a partial response and one patient treated with gefitnib had stable disease (PMID: 29340050). Additional studies have reported clinical responses to TKI therapy in patients with lung cancer harboring exon 19 insertion alterations (PMID: 24389445, 25279299, 20075572, 21841502).

The EGFR E709Q mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 19 K745M occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation is inactivating as it abolishes the kinase activity of EGFR, as demonstrated by decreased autophosphorylation of EGFR in in vitro experiments (PMID: 21081186).

The EGFR V726M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V726M was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 18000506). EGFR V726M was identified as an acquired secondary resistance mutation in patients with non-small cell lung cancer treated with osimertinib (Abstract: Lim et al. Abstract# P76.18, Journal of Thoracic Oncology Vol. 16 No. 3S. https://www.jto.org/article/S1556-0864%2821%2901117-5/fulltext).

The EGFR exon 20 G810S mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming and mildly sensitive to erlotinib, gefitinib and AEE788 (PMID: 19147750).

The exon 20 EGFR P772_H773dup mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR P772_H773dup is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR exon 22 E931G mutation occurs in the kinase domain of the protein. Cells engineered to express EGFR E931G mutation showed that this mutation confers resistance to EGFR inhibitors, suggesting that alternative treatment strategies, such as the use of CDK4 inhibitors, could be more adequate in this genetic context (PMID: 17974985).

The EGFR H835L mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR I706T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 17575133, 23912954, 25521408). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR I706T was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated a progression-free survival of 7.9 months (PMID: 25215536). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR I706T and EGFR G719A was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 25521408). In a second case report, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR I706T was treated with afatinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 29290256).

The EGFR exon 18 E709K mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 15710947, 25179728, 23566546, 18000506, 23749122, 25130612). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming and mildly sensitizing to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), gefitinib and erlotinib, with greater sensitivity to second-generation inhibitors such as afatinib and neratinib (PMID: 19726454, 29141884, 26206867). Patients with NSCLC harboring the EGFR E709K mutation in combination with other TKI-sensitizing mutations derived clinical benefit from treatment with erlotinib or gefitinib (PMID: 15710947, 25179728, 18000506, 23749122, 25130612).

The EGFR exon 20 D770_P772dup mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 23749122). Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR D770_P772dup mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 23749122).

The EGFR P691S mutation is located in exon 18 of the gene. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and prostate cancer (PMID: 22483783, 24595526). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P691S was treated with erlotinib and then osimertinib and demonstrated a partial response to both with a progression-free survival of 18 months and 15+ months, respectively (PMID: 29123416). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P691S was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 18000506). In a second case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P691S and EGFR E709A was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 22483783).

The EGFR E746V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 31534501). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746V was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 18000506). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746V and EGFR L747_S752del was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 16467085).

The EGFR S511Y mutation is located in domain IV of the protein. This mutation has been identified in transitional cell carcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is pathogenic (PMID: 36561320).

The EGFR-RAD51 fusion combines exons 1-24 of EGFR, including the kinase domain, with exons 4-10 of RAD51, including the ATPase domain (PMID: 27102076). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitive to erlotinib, afatinib and osimertinib (PMID: 27102076). Three patients with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR-RAD51 had sustained partial responses to treatment with erlotinib (PMID: 27102076)

The EGFR A289T mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in 3T3 and Ba/F3 cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation and cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884, 29533785).

The EGFR exon 19 G742S mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in lung and colorectal cancer (PMID: 30796031, 28838405, 16166444). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming (PMID: 24894453, 24743239) and sensitive to cetuximab (PMID: 24894453). Preclinical models with the G724S mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In a clinical study of 31 patients with colorectal cancer, one individual with the G724S EGFR mutation had stable disease as assessed by RECIST criteria following gefitinib treatment (PMID: 16166444). EGFR G742S has been identified as an acquired resistance mutation following treatment with osimertinib in two cases of EGFR mutant lung cancer (PMID: 28838405). Five additional patients with EGFR G724S-mutant lung adenocarcinoma had progression on osimertinib (PMID: 30405134, 30228210), with loss of the T790M allele accompanying progression in these patients (PMID: 30228210). Expression of the EGFR G724S mutation in combination with either the EGFR Ex19Del or the EGFR L858R mutations in HEK293 cells demonstrated that the G724S mutation significantly reduced osimertinib affinity for the EGFR Ex19Del allele while not affecting the ability of osimertinib to bind to or inhibit the EGFR L858R mutation (PMID: 30796031).

The EGFR R831H mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by levels of phosphorylated EGFR comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 20 G779F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in patients with lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15788655, 33183013, 28676220, 31175009). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring this mutation had a complete response to treatment with chemotherapy plus durvalumab (PMID: 33183013). Another patient with this mutation had a partial response to erlotinib (PMID: 28676220). In silico analysis suggests that this mutation is probably damaging (PMID: 31175009).

The EGFR S220P mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).
The EGFR exon 20 E804G mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming (PMID: 18193092).

The EGFR exon 20 G796R mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this variant has not been functionally validated as a single alteration, Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR G796R in conjunction with L858R and T790M were resistant to osimertinib in vitro (PMID: 29857056). Three patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G796R mutation progressed on treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 29857056, 28625641).

The gene L747S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancers, among others (PMID: 18645621, 17973572). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating when expressed together with the gene L858R mutation as measured by downstream signaling compared to the L858R mutation alone (PMID: 28424065). Structural modeling shows that the gene L747S mutation disrupts the formation of a hydrophobic core, which is important for the stabilization of inactive EGFR (PMID: 22190593, 28424065). The gene L747S mutation, in combination with the L858R mutation, has been identified as a potential resistance mutation to first-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors, such as gefitinib, and a sensitizing mutation to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, such as osimertinib (PMID: 28424065). Preclinical models with the L747S mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors. (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_E749del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain.
