In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In two clinical studies, patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_E749del mutation in combination with A750P or L746Q mutations had partial responses to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 25179728, 16467085).

The EGFR T854I mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the EGFR T854I mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR P373Q mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 21 L833F mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has yet to be functionally characterized. Patients with lung cancer harboring the L833F mutation have had mixed responses to targeted therapies. Preclinical models with the L833F mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). One patient had a partial response to chemotherapy but had progressive disease to an EGFR TKI (PMID: 23922984). Another patient had progressive disease despite being treated with erlotinib (PMID: 26773740). Another patient with G719A and L833F mutations had severe adverse effects in response to gefitinib (PMID: 25130612). One patient with the L833F mutation and an L858R mutation had clinical benefit in response to erlotinib (PMID: 28336552).

The EGFR R932C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 32321774). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation has a high functional impact on the protein (PMID: 24339735).

The EGFR V765M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and chronic lymphocytic leukemia (PMID: 16870303, 24127483). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V765M and an EGFR exon 19 deletion was treated with afatinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 31931137). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V765M was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 16870303). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V765M was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a 10% tumor shrinkage and progression-free survival of 4.1 months (PMID: 26462025).

The EGFR exon 12 S492R mutation occurs in the EGFR extracellular domain. This mutation was detected in a colorectal cancer cell line that was chronically exposed to cetuximab and experimental evaluation of this mutation determined that it interferes with the binding of the extracellular domain targeted antibody cetuximab but not panitumumab (PMID: 22270724). Colorectal cells expressing S492R EGFR had equivalent EGFR activity to those expressing wildtype EGFR (PMID: 22270724). In vitro and in vivo experiments with colorectal cancer cells expressing EGFR S492R demonstrated the mutation is activating as measured by accelerated cell growth as compared to wildtype (PMID: 30671888). Tumor biopsies from two of ten patients with metastatic colorectal cancer who experienced disease progression after a prior response to cetuximab harbored the S492R mutation in post- but not pre-treatment specimens (PMID: 22270724, 24025416). One of these patients was further treated with panitumumab monotherapy and showed 50% tumor reduction in his liver metastases within two months of treatment (PMID: 22270724). Treatment of EGFR S492R-mutant colorectal cancer xenografts with the monoclonal antibody CH12 demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive as measured by inhibited tumor growth following treatment  (PMID: 30671888).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insG mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 15788655). Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR D770_N771insG is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR exon 20 H773R mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has not yet been functionally characterized; however, other substitutions at this position (e.g., H773L) have been shown to be activating and oncogenic (PMID: 17974985). It has been found to co-occur with other EGFR mutations of unknown function (PMID: 18676761, 28676220). Two patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring compound H773R mutations had progressive disease after gefitinib treatment (PMID: 18676761, 16870303, 15623594). In the MSK-IMPACT clinical series, one patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR H773R mutation was treated with chemotherapy and EGFR TKIs and documented to achieve clinical benefit (PMID: 28336552).

The EGFR A289I mutation is located in the furin-like domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in glioblastoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 36044040). In vivo studies with mice expressing EGFR A289I demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by tumor growth and increased expression of transcripts related to lipid metabolism compared to wildtype (PMID: 36044040).

The EGFR G721D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G721D was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 0.7 months and an overall survival of 8.0 months (PMID: 17192902). In silico analysis suggests that EGFR G721D is sensitive to treatment with gefitinib, erlotinib, lapatinib, dacomitinib, afatinib, vandetanib and neratinib (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR K754_I759del mutation is located in exon 19 in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein.  This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 15118125). While this deletion has not been functionally characterized per se, in vitro studies of exon 19 deletions have demonstrated that they are generally activating as measured by increased EGFR autophosphorylation and activation of AKT and STAT pathways to promote cell survival (PMID: 15118125, 15284455, 17877814). Exon 19 deletions are sensitive to treatment with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors as measured by diminished phosphorylation in tumors expressing EGFR exon 19 deletions (PMID: 15329413, 15118073, 15118125, 18261621).

The EGFR H145R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in prostate cancer (PMID: 31874108). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is likely neutral and benign (PMID: 28843361).

The EGFR exon 19 G735S mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming potentially by increasing dimerization and kinase activity (PMID: 18193092, 25435280).

EGFRvV is a truncating mutation in the intracellular region of EGFR at amino acid 958, leading to increased ligand-dependent kinase activity (PMID: 17189397). In vitro assays have demonstrated that this mutation results in decreased EGFR receptor internalization and degradation, likely leading to enhanced EGFR activation and signaling (PMID: 1730638, 2790960).

The EGFR exon 21 L858Q mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation did not significantly alter ligand-independent EGFR activation. However, expression of L858Q showed elevated levels of AKT phosphorylation in the presence of EGF compared to WT and other mutants (PMID: 24743239). The oncogenic potential of this mutation has yet to be characterized.
The EGFR H988P mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation disrupts protein function and reduces protein stability (PMID: 20049516).

The EGFR D770delinsGY mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the Ba/F3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability under IL-3 deprived conditions compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28363995). Preclinical models with the D770delinsGY mutation show resistance to first- and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

EGFRvIII (variant three) is a mutation resulting in an in-frame deletion of exons 2 through 7 of the extracellular domain of the EGFR receptor (PMID: 17189397), resulting in a truncated 145 kDalton protein, which is constitutively active (PMID: 19324552). This alteration abrogates binding of EGFR to any ligand, including EGF, resulting in unrestricted activation (PMID: 23777544). EGFRvIII expressing cell lines have increased proliferation and invasion in addition to reduced apoptosis. Expression of EGFRvIII results in enhanced EGFR phosphorylation and activation of downstream signaling, including AKT, MAPK (mitogen activated protein kinase), and STAT (signal transducer and activator of transcription) pathways. EGFRvIII expressing-murine xenograft models also have increased tumor formation compared to controls, which confirms that this alteration is oncogenic (PMID: 8052651, 8895767, 12438278).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_A750delinsP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Across two clinical studies, four patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_A750delinsP mutation had a partial response (three of four) and a complete response (one of four), respectively, to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib, lasting a range of 6-36 months (PMID: 18508816, 17192902). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this alteration may be more responsive to afatinib than to erlotinib or osimertinib (PMID: 31182434).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_S752delinsV mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Across three clinical studies, six patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_S752delinsV mutation had a complete response (1/6), partial response (4/6) or stable disease (1/6), respectively, to treatment with gefitinib lasting a range of 18.9 to 75.2 months (PMID: 22483783, 25179728, 15710947).

The EGFR exon 19 W731L mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in malignant peritoneal mesothelioma (PMID: 20942962). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and sensitive to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 20942962).

The EGFR V441G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized per se, EGFR V441G was identified as an acquired mutation in patients with colorectal cancer who progressed cetuximab or panitumumab (PMID: 29423521, 29196463).

The EGFR exon 21 V843I mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been identified as a germline variant that predisposes patients to lung cancer (PMID: 23380224, 21172876, 18355544)(Abstract: Ohtsuka et al. JCO PO, 2019. https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.19.00104). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) (PMID: 25057940, 23380224, 21172876, 18355544). Despite cell line data demonstrating that V843I confers resistance to EGFR TKIs (PMID: 25057940, 23380224, 21172876, 18355544), in two clinical studies, three patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR V843I mutation alone or in combination with the erlotinib- and gefitinib-sensitive EGFR L858R mutation had a partial response (one of three) or stable disease (two of three) upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18000506, 19536777).

The EGFR L692F mutation is located in exon 18 of the gene. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 23912954). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L692F was treated with first- and second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors and demonstrated a progression-free survival of over two years (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR D837N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in biliary tract cancer, breast cancer and urinary tract cancer (PMID: 24372748, 31340200, 28481359). In vitro studies with YAMC cells expressing EGFR D837N and an EGFR kinase domain duplication mutation demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of kinase domain activity and decreased cellular proliferation compared to EGFR kinase domain duplication mutation (PMID: 33654076). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR D837N was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 23749122). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR D837N was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival and overall survival of 52 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EGFR S899N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR S899N, EGFR G719A and EGFR D1083V was treated with dacomitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 35770100).

The EGFR exon 21 L838P mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR L838P mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR exon 7 T263P mutation occurs in the cysteine-rich region of the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in multiple glioblastoma samples (PMID: 17177598). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming, and sensitive to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 17177598). The FDA-approved EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitor erlotinib was demonstrated to induce dose-dependent cell death in cells engineered to express this mutation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 17177598).

The EGFR K714N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 21057810, 31386689). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K714N was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 0.6 months and an overall survival of over 4.7 months (PMID: 23912954). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K714N and EGFR G719C was treated with erlotinib plus a placebo and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of 359 days and an overall survival of 973 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EGFR exon 18 L718Q mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation is of inconclusive function (PMID: 25948633). However, co-expression of EGFR L718Q with an EGFR mutation that is sensitive to EGFR inhibition led to drug resistance, suggesting that this mutation is likely a secondary resistance mutation (PMID: 25948633). A patient with T790M+ non-small cell lung cancer harboring the L718Q mutation progressed after treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 27257132, 25948633)

The EGFR L38V mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR V689M mutation lies in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation mediates constitutive actitvity in vitro and has transforming potential both in cell-line experiments and when injected in mice (PMID: 19560417).

The EGFR exon 20 P772_H773insYNP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). Across two clinical studies, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR P772_H773insYNP mutation in combination with the H773Y mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 19536777, 18676761)

The EGFRvII mutation is an in-frame deletion of exons 14 and 15 (amino acids 521-603) in the cystine-rich portion of the extracellular domain of the receptor (PMID: 17189397). This mutation results in constitutive activation of the kinase and no longer requires binding of the EGF ligand. Cells lines engineered to express this mutation had increased EGFR phosphorylation and downstream signaling, including enhanced MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase) and AKT signaling. Expression of this alteration leads to transformation in vitro and modest tumor growth in murine xenograft models (PMID: 24893890).

The EGFR Q787R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR L692V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, EGFR L692V was identified as an acquired resistance mutation in a patient with non-small cell lung cancer following treatment with rociletinib (PMID: 27283993).

The EGFR K708R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in ovarian cancer (PMID: 21057220). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR K708R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation and phosphorylated EGFR, AKT and STAT5 compared to wildtype (PMID: 31290142). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 and NIH3T3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with erlotinib, cetuximab, panitumumab, afatinib and dacomitinib as measured by decreased cellular viability and inhibition of anchorage-independent growth following treatment (PMID: 31290142).

The EGFR D1009N mutation lies in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR Y727H mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 19812598). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR Y727H was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 18000506). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR Y727H and KRAS G13D was treated with panitumumab plus carboplatin/paclitaxel and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 24389433).

The EGFR T710A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 22026926). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T710A and EGFR P649S was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR R377S mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation confers resistance to panitumumab through decreased binding affinity (PMID: 31228284).

The gene H773L mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancers, among others (PMID: 17974985, 32093862). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation, reduced apoptosis, and enhanced downstream signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 17974985). The gene H773L mutation has also been identified as a potential sensitizing mutation to the third-generation EGFR inhibitor osmertinib in patients (PMID: 32093862, 29858019).

The EGFR M793L mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 29434916). In silico analysis suggests that EGFR M793L confers resistance to gefitinib due to the importance of the EGFR M793 residue in gefitinib binding (PMID: 28436422).

The EGFR R831C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrioid carcinoma, pancreatic cancer and osteosarcoma (PMID: 29876005, 21573507, 17509661). In vitro studies with NIH-3T3 cells expressing EGFR R831C demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by constitutive activation and increased ligand-dependent phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 32190291). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L831C and EGFR L861R was treated with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR D1188N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with YAMC cells expressing EGFR D1188N and an EGFR kinase domain duplication mutation demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of kinase domain activity and decreased cellular proliferation compared to EGFR kinase domain duplication mutation (PMID: 33654076).

The EGFR G588S mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR M137V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR M137V and EGFR A1165V was treated with adjuvant radiotherapy and combination cisplatin plus navelbine and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 36629526).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_P753del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_P753del mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 20.17 months (PMID: 25179728).

The exon 20 EGFR N771_P772insH mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23371856). Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR N771_P772insH is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR exon 21 V851A mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 19147750). In vitro experiments have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as demonstrated by the abolishment of EGFR phosphorylation and the inability to transform cells or promote cellular proliferation (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR R836C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in choroid plexus papilloma (PMID: 31612017). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R836C was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of 2.1 months and an overall survival over 10.8 months (PMID: 23912954). In a case report, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR R836C was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23486275).

The gene I491M mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancers with resistance to the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (PMID: 25623215). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased ligand-dependent EGFR autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25623215). Structural modeling shows that the I491M mutation prevents binding to cetuximab and another EGFR targeting antibody panitumumab, suggesting that this mutation may be a treatment-associated resistance mutation.

The EGFR R165Q mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma and colorectal cancer (PMID: 32321774, 22895193). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR R165Q demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by IL-3 independent growth and increased phosphorylation of EGFR, AKT and STAT5 compared to wildtype (PMID: 31290142). Preclinical studies with NIH-3T3 cells and mouse xenograft models expressing EGFR R165Q demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with cetuximab and panitumumab as measured by decreased colony growth and tumor size following treatment (PMID: 31290142).

The EGFR A647T mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with advanced pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma acquired EGFR A647T as a secondary resistance mutation following treatment with erlotinib and conferred resistance to treatment with osimertinib as measured by patient disease progression (PMID: 32930150).

The exon 23 EGFR S921R mutation occurs in the EGFR autophosphorylation domain. This mutation has yet to be functionally characterized. In a clinical trial of 32 non-small cell lung cancer patients, one patient with the EGFR S921R mutation had stable disease after gefitinib therapy as determined by RECIST criteria (PMID: 19020901)

The exon 7 EGFR A289D mutation occurs in the EGFR extracellular domain. Cell lines with EGFR A289D mutations were more dependent on EGFR for survival compared to cell lines with wildtype EGFR as measured by cell death upon administration of EGFR inhibitors or knockdown of EGFR with shRNA (PMID: 22588883, 17177598). This mutation has been identified as a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011).

The EGFR exon 18 E709_T710delinsD mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in patients with lung cancer (PMID: 21531810, 26206867). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming, highly sensitive to afatinib, and moderately sensitive to gefitinib (PMID: 26206867). Preclinical models with the E709_T710delinsD mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In a clinical study, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E709_T710delinsD mutation had stable or progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 21531810). Additionally, a single case report documents a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring the EGFR E709_T710delinsD mutation who responded to afatinib after initially progressing on chemotherapy and erlotinib (PMID: 26206867). In the MSK-IMPACT clinical series, two of five patients with NSCLC harboring the EGFR E709_T710delinsD alteration responded to EGFR TKIs treatment, either alone or in combination with chemotherapy (PMID: 28336552).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_T751delinsP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_T751delinsP mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 27 months (PMID: 15710947). In a case report, a patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR L747_T751delinsP mutation was treated with osimertinib and demonstrated partial response lasting approximately 21 months and then subsequently was treated with combination osimertinib and sotorasib after acquiring the secondary resistance mutation KRAS G12C (PMID: 38096473).

The EGFR I744M mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in 3T3 cells demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by focus-formation comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR S306L mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in 3T3 cells demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by focus-formation comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884). In vitro studies suggest that this mutation is sensitive to gefitinib and erlotinib as measured by cell viablility (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR H773_V774insH mutation lies in the loop following the C helix in exon 20 of the protein. This mutation is found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24353160, 34526717). Expression of this variant in Ba/F3 cells led to pathway activation and factor-independent growth, demonstrating that EGFR H773_V774insH is activating (PMID: 24353160). In vitro studies of EGFR H773_V774insH suggest that it is resistant to erlotinib, as demonstrated by sustained growth upon erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160), and further preclinical models with the H773_V774insH mutation show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors and moderate sensitivity to Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR H773_V774insH mutation had progressive disease in response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR A767T mutation is detected in patients with colorectal cancer (PMID: 15746034, 26046796). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, expression of this mutation shows resistance to the EGFR inhibitor gefitinib (PMID: 18497962).

The EGFR S768_V769insSVD mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717, 29686424). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the S768_V769insSVD mutation show resistance to first- and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). Patients with the EGFR S768_V769insSVD mutation have shown robust radiological response to treatment with poziotinib (PMID: 29686424).

The EGFR exon 21 V834L mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation is found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 29705137, 32953862, 23912954). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR V834L mutation in combination with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor-sensitive EGFR exon 19 deletion had partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 45.2+ months (PMID: 23912954). The mutation has also been observed in patients with NSCLC with L858R-mutated EGFR but no functional effect has been described (PMID: 16533793, 19060236). This mutation has also been identified in the germline of a patient with familial lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: van der Leest et al, JCO PO, 2018). One patient with NSCLC harboring a somatic compound mutation of EGFR L858R/V834L was treated with icotinib hydrochloride, a small anticancer drug, and achieved stable disease for at least one year (PMID: 32953862).

The EGFR L777G mutation is located in the kinase domain. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L777G was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 1.0 month and an overall survival of 2.6 months (PMID: 17192902).

The gene K467T mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancers with resistance to the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (PMID: 25623215). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely neutral as measured by EGFR autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25623215). Structural modeling shows that the K467T mutation prevents binding to cetuximab, but maintains binding to another EGFR targeting antibody panitumumab via a rotated protein conformation, suggesting that this mutation may confer resistance to some EGFR targeting antibodies (PMID: 25623215, 27658254).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_S752delinsA mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_S752delinsA mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 5+ months (PMID: 15710947).

The EGFR exon 21 T854A mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation does not lead to increased EGFR activation. This mutation displayed resistance to erlotinib but demonstrated sensitivity to afatinib in cell lines (PMID: 19010870). The EGFR T854A mutation was found in a patient with EGFR L858R-mutant lung adenocarcinoma that developed resistance to the EGFR-TKI erlotinib. The mechanism of resistance for EGFR T854A is suggested to be similar to that of the EGFR T790M mutation and cause loss of contact and binding affinity to first-generation EGFR TKI treatment (PMID: 35045945). EGFR T854A has been identified to co-occur with the EGFR-TKI sensitive EGFR L858R mutation (PMID: 19010870, 35045945). Molecular dynamics simulations and PCA analysis comparing wildtype EGFR to EGFR mutant T854A predicts that the mutant would be resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors erlotinib and gefitinib (PMID: 26041145).

The EGFR exon 19 A750_E758delinsP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR A750_E758delinsP mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18261621).

The EGFR P772R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR L692P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L692P was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 19238633). In a separate clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L692P was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID 18000506).

The EGFR exon 19 E734Q mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in patients with peritoneal mesothelioma (PMID: 20942962). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitive to erlotinib (PMID: 20942962).

The EGFR G779S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and gastric cancer (PMID: 17626639, 31620276). Although not functionally characterized per se, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G779S and EGFR L858R were treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 18676761, 19536777).

The EGFR V774_C775insAV mutation occurs in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the V774_C775insAV mutation show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and moderate sensitivity to Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR V774M mutation occurs in exon 20 in the tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation is found in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 21531810, 31007929, 32093862, 29858019). A patient with NSCLC harboring the EGFR V774M mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib, while a patient with compound EGFR H773L/V774M mutation progressed on gefitinib but responded to treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 21531810, 29858019). Structural analysis demonstrated that the EGFR H773L/V774M compound mutation imposes a direct steric conflict to the αE helix compared to wild-type, potentially weakening the stability of the inactive state leading to constitutive activation of EGFR as well as drug resistance (PMID: 29858019).

The EGFR E709V mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR G729R is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 23749122). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G729R was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 18000506).

The EGFR E685K mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. In vitro studies with HCT116 cells expressing EGFR E685K demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced AKT phosphorylation and interaction with the transactivation domain of TP53 compared to wildtype (PMID: 36977662).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_S752delinsI mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_S752delinsI mutation had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib lasting 37.4 months (PMID: 17192902).

The EGFR L747_K754delinsATSPE mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung carcinomas (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the L747_K754delinsATSPE mutation show resistance to first- and second-generation EGFR inhibitors, high sensitivity to third- generation EGFR inhibitors and moderate sensitivity to PKC and ALK inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR S720F mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by focus formation comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR exon 20 G796D mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer in a patient who responded to and subsequently progressed on osimertinib (PMID: 28572531). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells shows that is it likely activating and oncogenic as demonstrated by moderate factor-independent growth, and further in vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to osimertinib as measured by sustained cell proliferation and kinase activity upon drug treatment (PMID: 28572531).

The EGFR G873Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR G873Q and EGFR L858R was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of over 1.4 months and an overall survival of over 1.8 months (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR G719D mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785). Preclinical models with a mutation at the EGFR G719 position show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In EGFR TKI-naive patients (N=62), afatinib demonstrated activity against tumors with EGFR G719 mutation (PMID: 31931137). Clinical studies have shown that patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR G719D mutation had clinical benefit with gefitinib or erlotinib treatment (PMID: 21531810, 18000506).

The EGFR N700D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 21057810). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR N700D was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 7.9 months and overall survival of 15.9 months (PMID: 15897572).

The EGFR E45Q mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR S198R mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR R776S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24040454). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R776S and EGFR L747_T751del was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 20 months and overall survival of over 40 months (PMID 23242437). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R77S and EGFR L858R was treated with afatinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 34512058).

The EGFR L688P mutation is found in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer. Expression of this mutation in HEK293T cells demonstrates that it is inactivating and may not contribute to tumor progression, as shown by decreased kinase activity and the inability to confer growth factor independence (PMID: 19147750).

The EGFR exon 20 A763_Y764insFQEA insertion mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 24353160). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming (PMID: 24353160, 29533785). Unlike other EGFR exon 20 insertions, this mutation is sensitizing to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) erlotinib, gefitinib and afatinib (PMID: 24353160). Preclinical models with A763insFQEA insertion show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717, 37196448). Structural analysis suggests the inserted residues result in a conformational change in the C-helix of EGFR that mirrors the change accompanying the EGFR L858R mutation (PMID: 24353160). Three patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the A763_Y764insFQEA mutation had either partial response (2 of 3) or stable disease (1 of 3), respectively, as best response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160), suggesting that this alteration is likely sensitive to EGFR inhibitors. (PMID: 23969006). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR A763_Y764insFQEA suggest the mutation is highly sensitive to erlotinib, afatinib, osimertinib and poziotinib as measured by decreased cell viability following treatment compared to wildtype (PMID: 34104899).

The EGFR exon 20 R776H mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found to be a germline variant that may predispose patients to lung cancer (PMID: 23358982, 34555730). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and sensitizing to erlotinib and gefitinib treatment (PMID: 23358982). Two patients with R776H mutations in conjunction with other EGFR mutations (L858R and delL747_T751) had a partial response to erlotinib (PMID: 20512075, 23242437). An additional study identified a patient with somatic EGFR R776H and L861Q mutations who had a partial response to afatinib (PMID: 34555730).

The EGFR exon 20 V769M mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 21764376), and corresponds to the region just after the C-helix of the EGFR kinase domain. This mutation was identified as a germline variant in a patient with five synchronous lung cancers, each of which also harbored a co-occurring EGFR G719A/C/S somatic mutation. In silico method predicted this to be a functionally damaging alteration (PMID: 20354512). V769 interacts directly with F856 of the DFG loop, a key structural element crucial for EGFR kinase activation. V769M substitution disrupts its molecular interactions in the hydrophobic core of the protein, resulting in structural rearrangements that facilitate the penetration and stabilization of ATP, potentially leading to constitutive activation of EGFR kinase. When expressed in 293T cells, the EGFR V769M mutant hyper-activated the signaling pathway, resulting in increased phospho-AKT, and phospho-ERK levels in an EGF ligand-dependent setting. Cells expressing the EGFR V769M mutant were sensitive to the EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) erlotinib, although less responsive than cells expressing the sensitizing allele L858R (IC50 0.4μM for V769M, compared to 0.01 μM for L858R mutant). Introduction of an additional EGFR G719C mutation into the V769M mutant and expression of this double mutant into 293T cells increased both the pathway activation and erlotinib sensitivity to a greater extent compared V769M alone (Abstract: Hellmann et al., JCO- PO, 2017. http://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.16.00019). Two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring this mutation in combination with a TKI-sensitive EGFR exon 19 insertion had progressive disease or partial response, respectively, to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 21531810, 23749122).

The EGFR R108G mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The exon 20 EGFR N771_P772insHH mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR N771_P772insHH is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR exon 20 V786M mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with bronchioloalveolar carcinoma harboring an EGFR V786M mutation in combination with the known to be oncogenic EGFR S784F mutation (PMID: 19147750), had a complete response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 18379371). In a separate study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR V786M mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 22760226). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR T786M mutation progressed on gefitinib but later had a partial response to third-generation EGFR TKI almonertinib (PMID: 35664749). Structural studies suggest that this mutation increases EGFR dimerization and likely activates the protein (PMID: 35664749).

The EGFR R222H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 30205045). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is pathogenic (PMID: 36561320).

The EGFR L861F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 19536777). In vivo studies with mice expressing EGFR L861F demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with afatinib and afatinib plus osimertinib, as measured by reduced tumor volume, and resistance to treatment with osimertinib, as measured by sustained tumor volume (PMID: 35304574). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L861F and EGFR L858R was treated with EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810). Another patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L861F and EGFR L858R was treated with gefitinib and responded to treatment (PMID: 19536777).

The EGFR exon 20 V769_D770insGVV mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR V769_D770insGVV mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 17192902).

The EGFR V441D mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 31924740). Although not functionally characterized per se, EGFR V441D was identified as an acquired mutation in patients with colorectal cancer who progressed cetuximab or panitumumab (PMID: 29423521, 29196463).

The EGFR exon 21 H870R mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is not activating (PMID: 19671738). This mutation is likely a passenger event as it has been observed to co-occur with the known oncogenic EGFR mutation L858R (PMID: 19671738, 21841502). In vitro studies showed that the single H870R mutation and the double H870R/L858R mutation had higher resistance to gefitnib treatment compared to the single L858R mutation (PMID: 19671738). Two lung adenocarcinoma patients with co-occuring L858R + H870R EGFR mutations had stable disease followed by rapid progression after treatment with erlotinib or gefitinib (PMID: 21841502, 19671738)

The exon 19 EGFR K745_E746insVPVAIK mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 18176089).  Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing in-frame deletion and insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 19 of EGFR suggests that EGFR K745_E746insVPVAIK is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 19 in-frame mutations constitutively activating the protein compared to wildtype (PMID: 15329413, 15118073, 21841502, 15118125).

The EGFR P694S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma and non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 28481359, 16014883). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR P694S and EGFR T710A was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 1.2 months and overall survival of 16.2 months (PMID: 23912954).

The EGFR R669Q mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR A750V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 32314446). Although not functionally characterized per se, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A750V were treated with afatinib and demonstrated stable disease in one patient and no clinical response in the other patient (PMID: 26354527).

The EGFR-PURB fusion results from a fusion between the N-terminus of EGFR and the C-terminus of PURB. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring the EGFR-PURB fusion was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 27102076).

The EGFR V774L mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR L703P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in ovarian cancer (PMID: 21057220). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L703P was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease with an overall survival of 15.7 months (PMID: 19020901).

The EGFR H47Y mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely inactivating as measured by decreased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR P272L mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely inactivating as measured by decreased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 20 H773insLGNP mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR H773insLGNP mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 23749122).

The EGFR P794R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation may confer resistance to osimertinib through reduced binding affinity (PMID: 33294282).

The EGFR exon 21 G857E mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR G857E mutation had stable disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 19238633, 18000506). The mutation has also been observed in patients with breast cancer (PMID: 23139256, 25435280).

The EGFR exon 26 T1041A mutation occurs in the C-terminal region of the protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased EGFR phosphorylation levels at this site and altered receptor trafficking compared to wildtype (PMID: 24797263).

The EGFR P596R mutation is located in the growth factor receptor domain IV of the protein. This mutation has been identified in glioblastoma (PMID: 23917401). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is damaging and deleterious (PMID: 35977996).

The EGFR A767_S768insASV mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung carcinomas (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the A767_S768insASV mutation show resistance to first- and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, including poziotinib (PMID: 34526717, 29686424).

The EGFR L704N mutation is located in exon 18. In vitro studies, using NIH3T3 cells have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as it acts as a dominant negative and prevents colony formation in soft agar (PMID: 24063894).

The EGFR exon 21 L861Q mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain (PMID: 17177598). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and oncogenic (PMID: 17177598, 21252719, 19147750, 29141884), but not as sensitizing to EGFR TKIs as L858R (PMID: 21252719) consistent with patient data demonstrating that while patients with the L861Q mutation do respond to gefitinib and erlotinib, their clinical benefit is to a lesser degree than that observed with more common EGFR mutations such as L858R (PMID: 24285021, 25668120). Preclinical models with the L861Q mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In a clinical trial of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), evaluation of patients with "uncommon" EGFR mutations demonstrated that a majority of these were G719 or L861 (45%, 28/ 62), and both these mutations were associated with sensitivity to EGFR TKIs (erlotinib or gefitinib) with a response rate, 57.1%; median progression-free survival, 6.0 months (PMID: 21531810). In patients treated with afatinib across the LUX-2/LUX-3/LUX-6 studies, the PFS in EGFR L861Q mutants was 8 months (PMID: 26051236). Across thirteen clinical studies, 22 patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L861Q mutation alone or in combination with other EGFR mutations (G719S, G719D, E756G, R776H or exon 19 deletion) had partial response (thirteen of 22), stable disease (five of 22), or progressive disease (4 of twenty-two), respectively, in response to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 15897572, 16467085, 18325048, 18508816, 18676761, 19536777, 20808254, 21531810, 21841502, 22760226, 23749122, 23912954, 24457318). In a Phase II trial of osimertinib in Korean patients with NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations, seven of nine patients with an L861Q substitution had an objective response, with a median progression-free survival of 15.2 months (PMID: 31825714).

The EGFR H773_V774insH mutation lies in the loop following the C helix in exon 20 of the protein. This mutation is found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24353160, 34526717). Expression of this variant in Ba/F3 cells led to pathway activation and factor-independent growth, demonstrating that EGFR H773_V774insH is activating (PMID: 24353160). In vitro studies of EGFR H773_V774insH suggest that it is resistant to erlotinib, as demonstrated by sustained growth upon erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160), and further preclinical models with the H773_V774insH mutation show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors and moderate sensitivity to Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR H773_V774insH mutation had progressive disease in response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR S752_I759del mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 28744312). In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 generally result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR S752_I759del was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 24.2 months and an overall survival of 11.7 months (PMID: 17192902). In a second clinical study, nineteen patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR S752_I759del were treated with gefitinib, erlotinib, icotinib and gefitinib plus erlotinib and demonstrated a range of clinical responses with progression-free survival of over a year (PMID: 32492620).

The exon 20 EGFR P772_H773insTPNP mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23371856).  Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR P772_H773insTPNP is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insGL mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 18948947). Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR D770_N771insGL is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR F712L mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR R252P mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR N528D mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is likely neutral as colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF when expressed in NIH3T3 cells was similar to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28979142).

The EGFR exon 19 D761N mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 19147750). Expression of EGFR D761N in Ba/F3 cells led to IL-3 independent growth, suggesting that this mutation is activating and transforming (PMID: 19147750). This mutation showed mild sensitivity to gefitinib and erlotinib in vitro compared to EGFR L858R and T790M, as measured by cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 19147750) but this mutation remained highly sensitive to AEE788 (PMID: 26870223).

The EGFR exon 20 N771_H773dup mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a Phase II study, three patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR N771_H773dup were treated with osimertinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 35777160).

The EGFR T847I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and breast cancer (PMID: 20811949, 21457545). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T847I and PIK3CA E545K was treated with combination erlotinib plus dasatinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23800712). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR T847I was treated with either erlotinib or gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR A871G mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by a slight increase in phosphorylated EGFR and focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 26146591, 29141884).

The gene G598V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastomas (PMID: 17177598). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased clonogenic growth and enhanced tumor formation in mouse models compared to wildtype  (PMID: 17177598, 29141884, 22588883). Drug efficacy studies in cell lines demonstrated that this mutation might be sensitive to the EGFR inhibitor erlotinib (PMID: 17177598,  22588883).

The EGFR Q701L mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 29434916). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR Q701L, EGFR G719S and EGFR I706T was treated with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810).

The EGFR G983R mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 19 A750P mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 15737014, 19625781, 25179728). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming (PMID: 19625781). This mutation typically co-occurs with known EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor sensitizing EGFR mutations. Expression of the A750P mutation in cis with L747_E749del resulted in increased downstream signaling as measured by increased autophosphorylation as well as increased phosphorylation of downstream targets including STAT3 and AKT (PMID: 16187797). Two patients with lung cancer who responded to erlotinib or gefitinib had an EGFR A750P mutation in combination with the L747_E749del mutation with or without an EGFR L746Q mutation, the former of which is known to be oncogenic and sensitive to erlotinib (PMID: 15737014, 19625781, 25179728).

The EGFR S116F mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR exon 20 C797G mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. While this variant was shown in a single study to decrease EGFR activity in vitro when expressed as a single alteration (PMID: 26378037), multiple patients with EGFR T790M+ non-small cell lung cancer who progressed on osimertinib after initially responding to the drug have showed acquisition of an EGFR C797G mutation in their post-treatment samples suggesting it is an important mediator for drug resistance (PMID: 27086175, 29713646).

The EGFR A839T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 16567021). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR A839T demonstrate resistance to treatment with gefitinib as measured by sustained cell viability following treatment (PMID: 29141884). In a clinical study, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR A839T was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with an overall survival of 13.4 months (PMID: 15623594).

The EGFR exon 21 L844V mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation is of inconclusive function (PMID: 25948633). However, co-expression of EGFR L844V with an EGFR mutation that was previously sensitive to EGFR inhibition led to drug resistance, suggesting that this mutation is likely a secondary resistance mutation (PMID: 25948633).

The EGFR E711K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lymphoepithelioma-like carcinoma (PMID: 21070477). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E711K was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 18000506).

The EGFR V774A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V774A was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR H773_V774insAH was treated with poziotinib and acquired EGFR V774A following progression (PMID: 35820397). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR H773_V774insAH and EGFR V774A demonstrated that EGFR V774A does not confer resistance to poziotinib as measured by cell viability levels comparable to treated single mutated EGFR H773_V774insAH cells (PMID: 35820397).

The EGFR G465E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 31924740). In vitro studies with NCI-H508 cells expressing EGFR G465E demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased downstream signaling activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26416732). Preclinical studies with NCI-H508 cells and patient-derived tumor grafts expressing EGFR G465E demonstrated that the mutation confers resistance to treatment with cetuximab and panitumumab, as measured by sustained cell viability and tumor growth following treatment compared to vector controls, and sensitivity to treatment with afatinib, as measured by decreased cell growth following treatment (PMID: 26416732). EGFR G465E was identified in next-generation sequencing data of patients with colorectal cancer and is suggested to confer resistance to cetuximab and panitumumab through blocking binding (PMID: 29196463).

The EGFR R521K mutation (formerly referred to as R497K) occurs in exon 13 in the extracellular domain of EGFR. This mutant is a germline polymorphism that has been predictive of familial colorectal cancer risk (PMID: 21896992). In a retrospective analysis of 32 patients with metastatic colorectal cancer treated with cetuximab, eleven of the twelve patients with the EGFR R521K mutation achieved an objective response or stable disease (PMID: 18544172). In squamous cell carcinoma patients, this variant has been associated with skin rash after gefitinib treatment, which is indicative of response, and decreased tumor progression (PMID: 20028750).

The EGFR L858M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 22836650). Although not functionally characterized per se, an erlotinib-resistant patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L858M and EGFR L861Q was treated with afatinib and demonstrated tumor regression (PMID: 28088511). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 and NIH-3T3 cells expressing EGFR L858M and EGFR L861Q demonstrated decreased sensitivity to first- and third-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors as measured by sustained cellular proliferation following treatment (PMID: 28088511, 25232377).
The EGFR exon 8 E330K mutation occurs in the EGFR extracellular domain (ECD) of EGFR. Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and transforming (PMID: 24212795).

The EGFR exon 19 L747_S752del mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). Across two clinical studies, four patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR L747_S752del mutation alone or in combination with another EGFR mutation (E746V, P753S, A755G) had a partial response to treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 17192902, 16467085).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insSVD mutation is an insertion located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24353160). Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating, transforming and resistant to erlotinib (PMID: 24353160). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR D770_N771insSVD mutation had progressive disease in response to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 24353160). In a Phase II clinical trial, a patient with epithelial carcinoma of the paranasal sinus harboring the EGFR D770_N771insSVD mutation was treated with osimertinib and demonstrated partial response (Abstract: Chen et al. JCO Precision Oncology 2024 Vol 8, Number 8. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/PO.23.00454).

The EGFR T363N mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is likely neutral as colony formation in the presence or absence of EGF when expressed in NIH3T3 cells was similar to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 28979142).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insY mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23371856). Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR D770_N771insY is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR K860E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K860E mutation was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 18000506). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K860E was treated with combination erlotinib plus bevacizumab and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 39 days and an overall survival of 127 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EGFR N842S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24002608). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR N842S was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 0.9 months and an overall survival of 9.7 months (PMID: 21531810).

This EGFR L798H mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L798H, EGFR V765M, EGFR L814P and EGFR K806E and three patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR L798H, EGFR V765M, EGFR L798H and EGFR K806E were treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 19060236, 16870303).

The EGFR exon 20 T785A mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in malignant peritoneal mesothelioma (PMID: 20942962). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating and sensitive to erlotinib treatment (PMID: 20942962).

The EGFR exon 18 G719A EGFR mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) (PMID: 21531810). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is transforming (PMID: 26206867, 27294619). Preclinical models with a mutation at the EGFR G719 position show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717). In EGFR TKI-naive patients (N=62), afatinib demonstrated activity against tumors with EGFR G719 mutation (PMID: 31931137). Approximately 50-60% of patients with lung cancer harboring a mutation at the EGFR G719 position experience clinical benefit in response to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) erlotinib or gefitinib. Specifically, in a study cohort of 62 patients with lung cancer harboring uncommon EGFR mutations; 3/6 patients with G719A mutant NSCLC had a partial response to EGFR TKIs while 3/6 experienced progressive disease. Additionally, two patients with the G719A mutation coincident with either the S720F or S768I EGFR mutations experienced partial response and progressive disease, respectively, in response to EGFR TKIs (PMID: 21531810). In a Phase II trial of osimertinib in Korean patients with NSCLC harboring uncommon EGFR mutations, ten of nineteen patients with a G719 substitution had an objective response, with a median progression-free survival of 8.2 months (PMID: 31825714).

The gene I853T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced gene phosphorylation, inability to transform cells, and similar proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19147750).

The exon 20 EGFR D770_N771insGF mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23026641).
