Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing insertion mutations of variable lengths and positions in exon 20 of EGFR suggests that EGFR D770_N771insGF is likely activating as measured by EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations increasing transforming activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24353160).

The EGFR A755D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 17908804). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A755D and an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of over 53.5 months and an overall survival of over 56.3 months (PMID: 23912954). In a clinical study, EGFR A755D was identified as an acquired resistance mutation in a patient with non-small cell lung cancer following disease progression after treatment with either first-generation or second-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 33931014).

The EGFR R705K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer and papillary thyroid carcinoma (PMID: 22805266, 28062544). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR R705K was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 23749122).

The EGFR G465R mutation is in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been observed in patients who developed resistance to treatment with EGFR-inhibitor treatment and has been shown to impede drug binding and decrease drug sensitivity in vitro (PMID: 25623215). Functionally, G465R mediates constitutive activation in cell lines (PMID: 25623215, 26059438, 26888827).

The EGFR L62R mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in 3T3 and Ba/F3 cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation and cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884, 29533785).

The EGFR E746Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746Q, EGFR L747_E749del and EGFR A750P was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 16467085). In a separate clinical study, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR E746Q, EGFR L747_T751del and EGFR T790M was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 14.7 months and an overall survival of 62.2 months (PMID: 32843903).

The EGFR exon 15 D587H mutation is located in the EGF binding domain. This mutation has been found in adenocarcinoma of unknown primary origin (PMID: 27245685). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is activating (PMID: 27245685). EGFR D587H may interfere with auto-inhibition by disrupting a salt bridge with EGFR Y270 and K609 (PMID: 26571394).

The EGFR exon 19 D761Y mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in combination with EGFR L858R in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) both before and after treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 17085664, 17545553, 19632948, 28424065, 22052230). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, cell line experiments demonstrate that co-expression of EGFR D761Y with L858R is less sensitive to gefitinib and erlotinib than EGFR L858R alone but does not confer complete resistance to gefitinib and erlotinib (PMID: 17973572). In clinical studies, patients with NSCLC harboring the EGFR D761Y mutation in combination with the erlotinib- and gefitinib-sensitive EGFR L858R mutation had stable or progressive disease in response to gefitinib (PMID: 17192902, 28424065, 17085664, 22052230).

The EGFR exon 20 S768_D770dup mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In two clinical studies, five patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR S768_D770dup mutation had progressive disease (four of five) or partial response (one of five), respectively, to treatment with gefitinib or erlotinib (PMID: 23749122, 18676761).

The EGFR H304Y mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR T751I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer, plasma cell myeloma and prostate cancer (PMID: 20811949, 18006781, 24595526). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with ovarian cancer and a patient with sarcoma harboring EGFR T751I were treated with erlotinib, cetuximab and bevacizumab and single agent erlotinib, respectively, and both patients did not respond to treatments (PMID: 23139256). In silico analysis suggests that EGFR T751I confers resistance to treatment with osimertinib (PMID: 31393074).

The EGFR exon 19 E746_T751delinsA mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. In-frame deletions of EGFR exon 19 result in constitutive activation of EGFR tyrosine kinase activity and confer sensitivity to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) including gefitinib, erlotinib and afatinib in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 15118073, 15118125, 15329413). In two clinical studies, two patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR E746_T751delinsA mutation had non-progressive disease or a minor response upon treatment with gefitinib lasting 5-13.5 months (PMID: 15897572, 15710947).

The EGFR E114K mutation is located in the EDC1 domain of the protein. In vitro studies in Ba/F3 cells have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased downstream signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 31290142). This mutation is sensitive to EGFR-targeted monoclonal antibodies cetuximab and panitumumab as measured by decreased cell viability and downstream signaling compared to wildtype Ba/F3 cells (PMID: 31290142).

The gene A755G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the gene protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancers, among others (PMID: 16467085, 28336552). The gene A755G mutation has been identified in patients who are partially sensitive to gene tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 16467085); however, patients with secondary EGFR mutations (such as A755G) in combination with gene T790M mutations have reduced progression-free survival in response to the EGFR inhibitor osimertinib (PMID: 32387812).

The EGFR V769L mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the V769L mutation show resistance to third-generation EGFR inhibitors, moderate sensitivity to first-generation and Ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors, and high sensitivity to second-generation EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EGFR A871E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in penile squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 30446465). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A871E and EGFR L858R was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 21531810). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR A871E and EGFR L858R was treated with icotinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 240 days (PMID: 30990107).

The EGFR D191N mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell viability comparable to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR V292M mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR V834C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V834C, EGFR G719A and EGFR L833V was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated complete response with a progression-free survival of over 16 months and an overall survival of over 29 months (PMID: 25130612).

The EGFR A871T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 21057810). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR A871T demonstrate resistance to treatment with gefitinib as measured by sustained cell viability following treatment (PMID: 29141884). In a clinical study, a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring EGFR A871T was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with an overall survival of 10.7 months (PMID: 16870303).

The EGFR V851I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer, prostate cancer and biliary tract cancer (PMID: 16152581, 21266046, 24372748). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing EGFR V851I demonstrate resistance to treatment with gefitinib as measured by sustained cell viability following treatment (PMID: 29141884). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR V851I was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 15870435).

The EGFR exon 20 S768_V769insVAS mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. Insertions of variable length and position in exon 20 of EGFR tend to be activating and transforming but resistant to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 18676761, 15897572, 17686547, 24353160, 19536777, 23371856, 21764376, 23371856). In a clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring the EGFR S768_V769insVAS mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with gefitinib (PMID: 21841502).

The EGFR V292L mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the NIH3T3 cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29141884).

The EGFR D256Y mutation lies in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in the MCF10A cell line demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785).

The EGFR E746G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 29075127). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746G and EGFR L861Q mutations was treated with either gefitinib or erlotinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 21531810). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746G was treated with erlotinib plus a placebo and achieved a progression-free survival of 415 days and an overall survival of 462 days (PMID: 26773740). In a second clinical study, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR E746G and EGFR L747P was treated with first-line EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors and demonstrated stable disease (Abstract: Bonomi et al. Abstract# A20, Annals of Oncology 27. https://www.annalsofoncology.org/article/S0923-7534%2819%2956588-7/pdf).

The EGFR exon 20 T790M mutation occurs in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain and is considered a "gatekeeper" mutation. This mutation is found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 15737014). Studies show that this mutation is oncogenic and increases the affinity of EGFR for ATP (PMID: 18227510). EGFR T790M generally occurs as an acquired secondary mutation upon prolonged exposure to first- and second-generation EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) such as erlotinib, gefinitib or afatinib, and is recognized by the NCCN to confer clinical resistance to these inhibitors (PMID: 15728811, 15737014, 18227510). The third-generation EGFR TKI, osimertinib, is associated with clinical benefit in patients with the EGFR T790M mutation and is FDA-approved for patients with EGFR T790M-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 29151359). Preclinical models with EGFR exon 19 deletion and the T790M and L792H mutations show resistance to first-, second-, and third-generation EGFR inhibitors, and moderate sensitivity to PKC and ALK inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

EGFR-KDD is an exon 18-25 or 18-26 kinase domain duplication (PMID: 26286086). This alteration has been found in lung cancer and glioma (PMID: 26286086, 9692551, 10698499). In vitro and Ba/F3 cell line experiments demonstrate that the EGFR-KDD is activating and transforming as measured by increased basal receptor phosphorylation and IL-3 independent growth (PMID: 26286086, 10698499, 19915609). A patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring the EGFR-KDD alteration had a partial response to afatinib that lasted for seven cycles of therapy, and other patients with the EGFR-KDD alteration have had clinical benefit in response to EGFR TKIs (PMID: 26286086, 30255937).

The EGFR S811F mutation is located in the EGFR tyrosine kinase domain. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 34526717). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, preclinical models with the S811F mutation show high sensitivity to first-, second-, third-generation, and ex20ins-active EGFR inhibitors (PMID: 34526717).

The EP300 Y1414C mutation is located in the protein's HAT domain and likely leads to loss of acetyltransferase activity (PMID: 25151357). Y1414C-mutant EP300 failed to rescue EP300-knockdown of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells in vitro (PMID: 25151357) suggesting that this mutation is inactivating.

EP300 truncating mutations result in EP300 proteins that lack some (or all) of the key enzymatic domains: the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) domain, the bromodomain and transcription factor binding domains (PMID: 10700188, 15156177, 12402157). Functional studies have shown that deletion of these domains result in decreased acetyltransferase and tumor suppressive activity (PMID: 12237408). These truncations are loss-of-function alterations, highlighted by the finding that truncation of one allele is highly associated with loss of the second EP300 allele (PMID: 10700188). Truncation of EP300 leads to disruption of signaling cascades such as the TGFβ pathway (PMID: 12237408).

The EP300 P1502L mutation is located in the protein's HAT domain and likely leads to loss of acetyltransferase activity (PMID: 25151357). P1502L-mutant EP300 failed to rescue EP300-knockdown of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells in vitro (PMID: 25151357) suggesting that this mutation is inactivating.

The EGFR F723L mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR F723L was treated with erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 0.47 months and an overall survival of 4.47 months (PMID: 22760226). In a clinical trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR F723L was treated with bevacizumab plus erlotinib and demonstrated progressive disease with a progression-free survival of 81 days and an overall survival of 311 days (PMID: 26773740).

The EP300 D1399N mutation is located in the protein's histone acetyltransferase domain. In three separate cancer cell lines, the transient expression of H1451L decreased histone H3 K27 acetylation, as compared to the wildtype protein. This residue is predicted to form hydrogen bonds at the active site of the protein, and the mutation could thus lead to functional loss due to disruption of these bonds (PMID: 28970362).

The EGFR K737T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring EGFR K737T and an EGFR exon 19 deletion mutation was treated with gefitinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 10.6 months and overall survival of 42.4 months (PMID: 23912954).

The EP300 H1451L mutation is located in the protein's histone acetyltransferase domain. In three separate cancer cell lines, the transient expression of H1451L decreased histone H3 K27 acetylation, as compared to the wildtype protein. This residue is predicted to form hydrogen bonds at the active site of the protein, and the mutation could thus lead to functional loss due to disruption of these bonds (PMID: 28970362).

The MLL-EP300 fusion results from the (11;22)(q23;q13) chromosomal translocation between MLL and EP300, and retains the HAT domain and bromodomain of EP300. This fusion protein has been observed in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 20980053, 9389684,18778367). Although not functionally characterized, the MLL-EP300 fusion is suggested to be activating based on the inclusion of both EP300's HAT domain and bromodomain that could cause aberrant epigenetic modifications in hematopoietic cells to promote tumorigenesis (PMID: 31662917).

The EP300 R1627W mutation occurs in the EP300 HAT domain. Structural modeling predicts that this mutation inactivates HAT activity of the protein resulting in dysregulation of gene expression (PMID: 28970362).

The EP300 D1399Y mutation is located in the protein's HAT domain and likely leads to loss of acetyltransferase activity. Human cell lines expressing the EP300 D1399Y mutant showed reduced transactivation of target genes compared to cells with wildtype EP300 (PMID: 12586840). Additionally, D1399Y-mutant EP300 failed to rescue EP300-knockdown of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma cells in vitro (PMID: 25151357), suggesting that this mutation is inactivating.

The MOZ-EP300 fusion results from translocation of the monocytic leukemia zinc finger protein (MOZ) with EP300 (and CBP) t(8;22)(p11;q13) and has been reported in acute leukemias (PMID:11243405, 10824998). The MOZ-EP300 fusion generates a protein with two acetyltransferase domains, which leads to aberrant histone modifications and altered gene regulation (review PMID: 23307074).

Fusions of EP300 have been identified in patients with hematological malignancies (PMID: 25943178, 26293203). The EP300 histone acetyltransferase (HAT) domain is commonly retained in fusion proteins leading to aberrant histone modifications and altered gene regulation (PMID: 23307074).

EP300 truncating mutations result in EP300 proteins that lack some or all of the key enzymatic domains: the histone acetyltransferase (HAT) domain, the bromodomain and transcription factor binding domains (PMID: 12402157). Functional studies have shown that deletion of these domains result in decreased acetyltransferase and tumor suppressive activity (PMID: 12237408). Deletion of one EP300 allele is highly associated with loss of the second EP300 allele (PMID: 10700188) and can lead to disruption of signaling cascades such as the TGFβ pathway (PMID: 12237408).

The EP300 R1627Q mutation occurs in the EP300 HAT domain. Structural modeling predicts that this mutation inactivates HAT activity of the protein resulting in dysregulation of gene expression (PMID: 28970362).

The ERBB2 E698del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized per se, ERBB2 E698del was identified as an acquired mutation in a patient with breast cancer harboring ERBB2 V777L after progression on neratinib (Abstract: Marin et al. Abstract# P4-01-02, AACR 2022. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/82/4_Supplement/P4-01-02/681020/Abstract-P4-01-02-A-spectrum-of-secondary).

The ERBB2 E930D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 29718453). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 V664F mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 V308M mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colon cancer (PMID: 27149842). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated it is likely inactivating as measured by decreased cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 R143Q mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder and lung cancer (PMID: 24971884, 26647728). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, bladder cancer, murine fibroblast and B-cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein activation, cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24971884, 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 T216S mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890, 18772396). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in colony formation and protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 V773A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 22046346). There is conflicting data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in downstream signaling and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346). In vitro studies suggest that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug administration (PMID: 22046346). One patient with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma harboring this mutation had a partial response to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor gefitinib (PMID: 16299242).

The ERBB2 C311R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, increased downstream signaling and increased colony formation in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 E1079K mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in esophageal cancer (PMID: 23525077). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in murine B-cells as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 D769N mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung, breast, colorectal and cervical cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 D1058A mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 27077364). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 D1058A suggest that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in murine B-cells as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 P650S mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in uterine cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 A644F mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 E914K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioma (PMID: 15457249, 16618716). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R1006C mutation is located in the cytoplasmic C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 27406316). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 N302K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is oncogenic (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 L755S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 22046346). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, murine breast, murine fibroblast and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, colony formation and cytokine-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346, 18413839, 23220880). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitors lapatinib, gefitinib and trastuzumab when expressed in breast or murine B-cell cell lines as measured by sustained proliferation and colony formation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22046346, 23220880). In vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, fulvestrant and aromatase inhibition, and to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib, but is sensitive to the combination of neratinib with fulvestrant when expressed in breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and pathway activation (PMID: 30531871, 30314968). Eight patients with cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial had various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to complete response (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 G660R mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 27903463, 31849493, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by protein activation and increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab, but is resistant to pertuzumab when expressed in murine B-cells as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 30449325). One patient with lung cancer harboring this mutation along with the ERBB2 V659E mutation demonstrated a partial response to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor afatinib (PMID: 27903463).

The ERBB2 S792F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 29464843). Expression of this mutation in a cervical cancer cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29464843).

The ERBB2 V1128I mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in intestinal, liver and pancreatic cancer (PMID: 28481359, 27149842, 25159915, 28481359). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R897Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in intestinal cancer (PMID: 23700467, 27149842). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 P1199T mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioma (PMID: 23917401). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 V842I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in colorectal and endometrial cancer (PMID: 28572459).  Expression of this mutation in breast, breast cancer or murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation and increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). However, expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in vivo tumor formation in a xenograft mouse model compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, and neratinib when expressed in a breast epithelial cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment; however, other in vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to trastuzumab, sapitinib and lapatinib but sensitive to afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880, 29967253). Five patients with cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial had various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to stable disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 V839G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 L651W mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 V659G mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 Q680H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 N319D mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890,18772396). Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in colony formation and protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 18772890, 23389443). One patient with ovarian cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial demonstrated progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 L663P mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in soft tissue sarcoma (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased foci formation and increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab and pertuzumab when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 R217C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 30371878). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). However, expression in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 R34Q suggest that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

This mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 20 of ERBB2. Expression of exon 20 insertions or indels in cell lines results in constitutive phosphorylation and activation of ERBB2 as measured by increased phosphorylation and binding of dimerization partners such as EGFR and ERBB3, and increased phosphorylation of downstream targets such as AKT and MAPK (PMID: 16843263). Stable expression of exon 20 mutant ERBB2 MCF10A cells results in increased proliferation and foci formation in matrigel compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 16843263). Cancer cells engineered to express ERBB2 exon 20 mutations have been found to be sensitive to lapatinib, neratinib, and trastuzumab (PMID: 23220880). Clinical studies of patients with lung cancer have demonstrated sensitivities of some patients with ERBB2 exon 20 mutations to afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, neratinib and poziotinib (PMID: 23610105, 22325357, 22649146, 23610105, 16775247, 21353324, 34550757) (Abstract: Ann Oncol 2014; 25: suppl 4, abstract LB39_PR). Clinical studies have also shown that four patients with lung cancer harboring ERBB2 exon 20 mutations achieved partial responses after treatment with dacomitinib (PMID: 25899785).

The ERBB2 I654V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in familial breast cancer (PMID:15550452,19336545). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation or growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (Abstract: Kancha et. al, AACR Annual Meeting 2009, Abstract # 1766. http://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/69/9_Supplement/1766). However, computational analysis of this mutation in combination with ERBB2 I655V demonstrated that together both mutations may increase protein activity (PMID: 15550452). This mutation is associated with an increased risk for breast cancer (odds ratio= 2.56), particularly in women over the age of forty (odds ratio= 2.86) (PMID: 15550452).

The ERBB2 C334S mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, increased downstream signaling and increased colony formation in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 S656C mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in esophageal cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 P489L mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 29902295). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 V777A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and is a hotspot residue (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772396, 18772890). Expression of this mutation in a mouse fibroblast cell line suggested that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in colony formation and protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 23389443).

The ERBB2 L755P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 22046346). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, HEK293, murine breast, murine fibroblast and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased levels of protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346, 29967253). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, neratinib and osimertinib but sensitive to afatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22046346, 29967253). In a neratinib basket trial, one patient with lung cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (14.7 months) upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 V794M mutation is located in the N-terminal lobe of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 25435280). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in breast epithelial and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, cellular invasion and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25435280). In silico structural modeling predicts this mutation would be activating (PMID: 25435280).

The ERBB2 S760A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial, breast cancer or murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein and pathway activation compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 23220880).

The ERBB2 E401G mutation is located in the extracellular domain III of the protein. This mutation has been found in cancer of unknown primary (CUP) (PMID: 34997908). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a lung cancer cell line and a mouse fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased protein phosphorylation, activation of downstream targets, and motility, in comparison to wildtype (PMID:34997908). However, cellular growth was not enhanced by this mutation in vitro, and in vivo experiments in a mouse model of cancer demonstrated only a modest increase in tumor size in comparison to wildtype (PMID: 34997908).

The ERBB2 A648L mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in urinary cancers (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 D769Y mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder and gastroesophageal cancer (PMID: 29420467). This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial, breast cancer and murine B-cell and fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation, colony formation in soft agar, and transformation of mammary cell lines compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors afatinib, lapatinib, neratinib, osimertinib, and sapitinib, but resistant to trastuzumab as measured by growth on matrigel (PMID: 23220880, 29967253). Two patients with either bladder or gastroesophageal cancer harboring this mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467)

The ERBB2 E717D mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in pancreatic cancer (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with human pancreatic epithelial cells expressing ERBB2 E717D demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by cellular transformation, increased ERBB2 signaling and anchorage-independent cell growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 31046123). In vivo studies with xenograft mouse models expressing ERBB2 E717D also demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by tumor growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 31046123).

The ERBB2 L866M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 26243861). Expression of this mutation in immortalized colon epithelial cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein activation and growth in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 26243863). In vitro studies of ERBB2 L866M demonstrate that it is sensitive to neratinib and afatinib when expressed in colon epithelial cells as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 26243863).

The ERBB2 L785F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).
The ERBB2 E719K mutation is located in between the transmembrane and kinase domains of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 A440T mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in prostate cancer (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).
The ERBB2 Q396K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 L15F mutation is found in the N-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in urothelial bladder cancer (PMID: 24971884). In vitro experiments with cancer cell lines expressing this mutation demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no significant changes in colony formation or protein activation in comparison to wildtype (PMID: 24971884).

The ERRB2 P1074L mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation was identified in a metastatic tumor biopsy from 1 of 168 patients with ER+ breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 G776_V777insYVMA mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is found in lung cancer (PMID: 16843263). Expression of this mutation in lung and breast epithelial cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by constitutive protein and pathway activation and increased cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 16843263). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to erlotinib and gefitinib but sensitive to lapatinib and trastuzumab as measured by colony formation and ERBB2 phosphorylation upon drug treatment (PMID: 16843263).

The ERBB2 P1170A mutation is located in the C-terminal tail of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in familial breast cancer (PMID: 19336545). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 L755_T759del mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 22722193, 27284958). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway phosphorylation, cell proliferation and colony formation on matrigel compared to wildtype (PMID: 15118125, 15118073, 15329413, 23220880). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to treatment with the ERBB2 inhibitors gefitinib and neratinib when expressed in a breast epithelial cell line as measured by decreased proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880).

The ERBB2 R677T mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 L755_E757delinsS mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, one patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation had a partial response (9 months) upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 Y772_A775dup insertion/duplication is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial, bronchial epithelial, murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation, colony formation, invasion in cell lines, tumor formation in xenograft models and cytokine-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 16843263). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, and neratinib but is resistant to gefitinib and erlotinib when expressed in breast and murine B-cell cell lines as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275, 23220880, 16843263). Seventeen patients with cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial had various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to complete response (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 S633F mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial and colorectal cancer (PMID: 28481359, 27852700). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R188C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 R188C demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by IL-3-independent growth and increased ERBB2 receptor phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 32366937). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 R188C demonstrated sensitivity to lapatinib, pelitinib, canertinib and trastuzumab as measured by decreased cell viability with IC50 values, and demonstrated resistance to gefitinib and erlotinib as measured by sustained cell viability with IC50 values (PMID: 32366937).

The ERBB2 V665D mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 H878Y mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in liver cancer (PMID: 17150109). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that is it activating as measured by increased pathway activation and modestly increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25853726, 22046346). However, expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines in a large functional screen demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In silico models predict this mutation to be probably damaging (PMID: 30023006). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrated that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, afatinib, sapitinib, osimertinib and neratinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell signaling and cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22046346, 25853726, 29967253,18199554).

The ERBB2 E265K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in gallbladder cancer (PMID: 24997986). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and gallbladder cell lines demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cell growth in the context of ERBB3 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 24997986). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is partially sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab, and sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 G778A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, preclinical studies with gastroesophageal cancer patient-derived xenograft models harboring ERBB2 G778 and CCNE1 amplification demonstrated sensitivity to trastuzumab deruxtecan plus adavosertib (Abstract: DiPeri et al. Abstract# 327, AACR 2022. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/82/12_Supplement/327/703319).

The ERBB2 V777M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal, breast and lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 27284958, 16397024, 28481359, 26619011). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25720673). However, expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25720673). In vitro studies of ERBB2 V777M demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 K753A mutation is located within the ATP-binding pocket of the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in murine B-cells demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by loss of protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 22393464, 23680147, 11071886).

The ERBB2 N857S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in ovarian cancer (PMID: 15457249). In a paper with limited controls or statistical analysis, expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by modest pathway activation and cytokine independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but is sensitive to the tyrosine kinase inhibitors lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in breast and murine B-cell cell lines as measured by decreased proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22046346, 29967253).

The ERBB2 Q680F mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 K676T mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 S305F mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 Y1248F mutation is located in the intracellular autophosphorylation domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 1671296).

The ERBB2 L915M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to ERBB2 V659E alone. (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 L869R mutation is located in the activation loop of the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011).This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, growth factor-independent cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wildtype; coexpression of this mutation with ERBB3 E928G resulted in increased pathway activation compared to expression of either mutant alone (PMID: 28274957). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor neratinib but not lapatinib when expressed in a breast epithelial cell line as measured by cell proliferation (PMID: 28274957). One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation had a partial response (3.6 months) upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial and one patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring this mutation had a partial response to lapatinib but no response to trastuzumab alone (PMID: 29420467, 26305917). In vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, fulvestrant and aromatase inhibition, and to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib, but is sensitive to the combination of neratinib with fulvestrant when expressed in breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and pathway activation (PMID: 30531871, 30314968).

The ERBB2 Q711H mutation lies in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 L841V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28572459, 34380637). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro and in vivo xenograft studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in murine fibroblast and B-cells as measured by decreased cell proliferation and tumor growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype EGFR (PMID: 29533785). In a neratinib basket trial, One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation and one patient with colorectal cancer harboring this mutation both had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib in a basket trial (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 L313V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder and cervical cancer (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated it is likely inactivating as measured by decreased cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 E717K mutation is located in between the transmembrane and kinase domains of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 30641862). This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib  (PMID: 18413839). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 R677L mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The SHC1-ERBB2 fusion protein results from exon 2 of SHC1 fusing with exon 25 of ERBB2. In vitro studies with H3122 cells expressing the SHC1-ERBB2 fusion demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation compared to the control vector (PMID: 37168365). In vitro studies with HeLa cells expressing the SHC1-ERBB2 fusion also demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by increased fluorescently tagged signaling pathway activity compared to wildtype (Abstract: Liu et al. Abstract# e24316, ASCO 2018. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2018.36.15_suppl.e24316). Preclinical studies with H3122 cells expressing the SHC1-ERBB2 fusion demonstrate sensitivity to afatinib, lapatinib and tarloxotinib as measured by reduced cellular viability following treatment (PMID: 37168365).

The GRB7-ERBB2 fusion protein results from fusing of exon 5 of GRB7 with exon 10 of ERBB2, retaining the kinase domain of ERBB2. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with colorectal cancer harboring the GRB7-ERBB2 fusion was treated with combination cetuximab plus irinotecan and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 26660078). In a clinical trial, a patient with colorectal cancer harboring the GRB7-ERBB2 fusion was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 G778_S779insG mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Exon 20 indel mutations have been found in lung cancer (PMID: 25899785, 23610105, 22325357, 21353324,16775247). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 I675M mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and genitourinary cancer (PMID: 28215721, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 R340P mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 R138W mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute lymphoblastic T-cell leukemia (PMID: 28157215). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERRB2 R1153L mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 30531871). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation was identified in a metastatic tumor biopsy from 1 of 168 patients with ER+ breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 I263T mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype. In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 G776delinsVC mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is found in lung cancer (PMID: 26545934). Expression of this mutation in normal bronchial, breast epithelial, murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26545934, 29967253, 29533785). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to lapatinib, trastuzumab and erlotinib, but is sensitive to afatinib, neratinib and osimertinib when expressed in lung cancer and murine B-cell cell lines as measured by protein activation and proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 26545934, 29967253). In a neratinib basket trial, one patient with lung cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (8.5 months) upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 R896G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 31849493). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, a patient with squamous lung carcinoma harboring this mutation responded to treatment with the ERBB2 inhibitor afatinib (PMID: 31849493).

The ERBB2 Y343C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 25957691). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 V773M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal, breast and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 A241V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer (PMID: 24121792). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrates that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R896C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Overexpression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity and enhanced colony growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). However, expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). Expression in MCF10A cells at physiological levels did not transform the cells, though neither did the positive control ERBB2 V777L (PMID: 26508629). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, afatinib, osimertinib, sapitinib and neratinib when expressed in breast and murine B-cell cell lines as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880, 29967253).

The ERBB2 S779_P780insVGS mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 S779_P780insVGS suggest that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib but sensitive to sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 G660D mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in familial lung adenocarcinoma and in various sporadic cancers (PMID: 24317180, 26545934, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in lung epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, growth factor-independent proliferation and decreased survival in a transplanted leukemic mouse model compared to wildtype (PMID: 26545934, 30449325). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to neratinib, afatinib, lapatinib and trastuzumab but is stimulated by pertuzumab when expressed in lung epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines as measured by protein and pathway activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 26545934, 30449325). One patient with familial lung cancer harboring this mutation in the germline responded to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor afatinib (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 A1039T mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in stomach cancer (PMID: 23525077). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 G58R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 30200630). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 G58R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35503682).

The ERBB2 T306M mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 29718453). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

This mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 20 of ERBB2. Expression of exon 20 insertions or indels in cell lines results in constitutive phosphorylation and activation of ERBB2 as measured by increased phosphorylation and binding of dimerization partners such as EGFR and ERBB3, and increased phosphorylation of downstream targets such as AKT and MAPK (PMID: 16843263). Stable expression of exon 20 mutant ERBB2 MCF10A cells results in increased proliferation and foci formation in matrigel compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 16843263). Cancer cells engineered to express ERBB2 exon 20 mutations have been found to be sensitive to lapatinib, neratinib, and trastuzumab (PMID: 23220880). Clinical studies of patients with lung cancer have demonstrated sensitivities of some patients with ERBB2 exon 20 mutations to afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, neratinib and poziotinib (PMID: 23610105, 22325357, 22649146, 23610105, 16775247, 21353324, 34550757) (Abstract: Ann Oncol 2014; 25: suppl 4, abstract LB39_PR). Clinical studies have also shown that four patients with lung cancer harboring ERBB2 exon 20 mutations achieved partial responses after treatment with dacomitinib (PMID: 25899785).

The ERBB2 L726I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 17638894). Endogenous expression of this mutation in a gefitinib-resistant breast cancer cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation compared to the parental cell line (PMID: 17638894).

The ERBB2 K200N mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 D326H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In vitro studies with HeLa cells expressing ERBB2 D326H demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased fluorescently tagged signaling pathway activity compared to wildtype (Abstract: Liu et al. Abstract# e24316, ASCO 2018. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2018.36.15_suppl.e24316).

The ERBB2 R34Q mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 30325992). Expression of this mutation in murine B-cell and fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 G309A mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28572459). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Overexpression of this mutation in human mammary epithelial or murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation, invasion, colony formation in soft agar, tumor growth in xenograft models and growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 23220880). However, expression of this mutation at physiologic levels demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by cell proliferation, colonization and tumor formation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 26508629). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERRB2 inhibitors afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, and neratinib as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 S783P mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in MCF-7 or HEK293T cells demonstrated it is likely neutral as measured by autophosphorylation and downstream pathway activation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 28164408). This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to ERBB2 V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 L786V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with lung cancer harboring ERBB2 L786V was treated with neratinib and demonstrated stable disease with a progression-free survival of 3.6 months (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 R678Q mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein and is a hotspot residue. This mutation has been found in various cancers including biliary, breast, and lung, among others (PMID: 23220880, 30449325). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in breast, bladder cancer and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, growth-factor independent cell proliferation, and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24971884, 30449325). However, expression of this mutation in breast and murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrate that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activity, cell proliferation or colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880, 29967253). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, pertuzumab, lapatinib, afatinib, sapitinib, osimertinib and neratinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by moderately decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880, 29967253, 30449325). Two patients with colorectal and gastroesophageal cancer harboring this mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib, and a patient with endometrial cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (5.5 months) upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 X633_splice mutation is located at the splice acceptor site in intron 15 and results in the skipping of exon 16. In vitro studies with RLE-6TN and MCF10A cells expressing an exon 16 skipping ERBB2 transcript (ERBB2ΔEx16) demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased ERBB2 signaling, cellular proliferation and anchorage-independent growth compared to full-length ERBB2 (PMID: 32727899). Preclinical studies with RLE-6TN cells expressing ERBB2ΔEx16 demonstrate resistance to afatinib as measured by decreased markers of cell death compared to treatment of full-length ERBB2-expressing cells (PMID: 32727899).

The ERBB2 T798I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28274957). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, breast and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrate that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in pathway activation or colony formation compared to wildtype and failure to induce growth-factor independent proliferation (PMID: 18413839). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitors neratinib and osimertinib but sensitive to afatinib and AZ5104 when expressed in ERBB2 L869R-expressing breast cells (PMID: 28274957).
