One patient with breast cancer who acquired the ERBB2 L869R mutation developed resistance to neratinib (PMID: 28274957).

The ERBB2 L755A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 L755A demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by IL-3-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 34584864). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 L755A demonstrated sensitivity to poziotinib and tarloxotinib-E, as measured by reduced cell viability at lower IC50 values, and resistance to osimertinib and tarloxotinib, as measured by sustained cell viability at higher IC50 values (PMID: 34584864). In a clinical trial, a patient with lung cancer harboring ERBB2 L755A was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).
The ERBB2 S1002R mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 I655V mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in rhabdomyosarcoma and colon and lung cancer (PMID: 28978093, 26647728, 24793135). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial, breast cancer and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in cell viability, downstream signaling, acini structure and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785, 27697991).

The ERBB2 V659E mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in glioma as well as lung, breast, biliary and colorectal cancer (PMID: 28572459, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, growth-factor independent cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 1671296, 7821711, 30449325). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to trastuzumab but is stimulated by pertuzumab when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by cell viability in the presence of the drug (PMID: 30449325). Four patients with cancers harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial had stable disease in response to neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 T798M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by moderately increased colony formation on soft agar and cytokine-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346). This mutation is analogous to the EGFR T790M gatekeeper mutation and was found in a random mutagenesis screen for resistance to lapatinib (PMID: 25238247). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by persistent cell growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 22046346, 23948973).

The ERBB2 I682G mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 E645K mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 G776delinsLC mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is found in lung cancer (PMID: 26545934). Expression of this mutation in normal bronchial epithelial and murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26545934, 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrated that it is resistant to erlotinib and trastuzumab but sensitive to afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 26545934).

The ERBB2 E645F mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 S653C mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast, liver, colorectal, and bladder cancer (PMID: 28572459, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and bladder, breast cancer and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24971884, 30449325, 30531871). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to lapatinib and afatinib when expressed in bladder cancer cell lines as measured by decreased protein activation and foci formation upon drug treatment (PMID: 24971884). In vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to endocrine therapy and to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib, but is sensitive to the combination of neratinib with fulvestrant when expressed in breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and pathway activation analysis (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 A710V mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 R678W mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in pancreatic cancer and glioma (PMID: 31676785, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 L726F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cell invasion, colony formation, growth factor-independent and anchorage-independent growth and tumor growth in xenograft mouse models compared to wildtype (PMID: 25435280, 18413839). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib but sensitive to the EGFR/ERBB2/VEGF inhibitor EXEL-7647 when expressed in either murine fibroblast or breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and tumor growth (PMID: 25435280, 18413839).

The ERBB2 G222C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 29718453). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 G135E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in intestinal cancer (PMID: 27852700). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 L755W mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot.  Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with MCF10A cells expressing ERBB2 L755W demonstrated sensitivity to irreversible kinase inhibitor neratinib as measured by inhibition of colony growth in a matrigel colony forming assay (PMID: 23220880).

The ERBB2 P761del mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with metastatic breast cancer harboring ERBB2 P761del and ERBB2 L755S was treated with neratinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 36627899). In a clinical trial, a patient with endometrial cancer harboring ERBB2 P761del was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 V272G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In vitro studies with HeLa cells expressing ERBB2 V272G demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased fluorescently tagged signaling pathway activity compared to wildtype (Abstract: Liu et al. Abstract# e24316, ASCO 2018. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2018.36.15_suppl.e24316).

The ERBB2 E812K mutation is located in the kinase domain of ERBB2. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib  (PMID: 18413839). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 R683Q mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in pancreatic, endometrial, bone and colorectal cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 V750E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772396, 18772890). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in colony formation and protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 23389443).

The ERBB2 G776V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and breast cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 Q709L mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and gastrointestinal cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, pertuzumab, neratinib, afatinib, and lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 I661V mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 P36S mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and brain cancer (PMID: 27406316, 28481359). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 D845A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 30531871). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating, as measured by abolished protein activity and decreased colony formation in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 V480A mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 25344691, 27149842). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it may be activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). However, expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it was neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 V480A suggest that it is sensitive to trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 A644V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 28162959). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R456C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 27149842). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with breast cancer harboring ERBB2 R456C was treated with neratinib and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 30301790).

The ERBB2 G776delinsVV mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is sensitive to treatment with afatinib and pyrotinib (PMID: 35330827).

The ERBB2 G292R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in gallbladder cancer (PMID: 24997986). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and gallbladder cell lines demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cell growth in the context of ERBB3 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 24997986). However, expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERRB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, and osimertinib but not neratinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253). One patient with bladder cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 K753E mutation is located within the ATP-binding pocket of the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 27697991). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial, breast cancer and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activity or cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 27697991). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab and lapatinib but is sensitive to neratinib when expressed in a breast epithelial cell line as measured by colony formation upon drug treatment (PMID: 27697991).

The ERBB2 Y803N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 L755M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 27602491). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 E693K mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma, breast and ovarian cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 L674V mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 G1015E mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in meningioma and prostate cancer (PMID: 28713588, 31874108). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is benign (PMID: 32291971).

The ERBB2 A775G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 24222160). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 D277H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 24971884, 26619011). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in bladder cancer, murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by lack of change in protein and pathway activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24971884, 29967253). However, coexpression of this mutation with ERBB2 S310F in a bladder cancer cell line demonstrated that it may be activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation compared to S310F alone (PMID: 24971884).

The ERBB2 R849W mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastric cancer (PMID: 31620276). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with ovarian cancer harboring ERBB2 R849W was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERRB2 R143G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein (PMID: 30531871). This mutation has been found in breast cancer. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation was identified in a metastatic tumor biopsy from 1 of 168 patients with ER+ breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 G727A mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation coexpressed with ERBB2 V777L is resistant to endocrine therapy including tamoxifen, fulvestrant and aromatase inhibition when expressed in a breast cancer cell line as measured by decreased cell viability upon drug treatment; however, as V777L is known to be activating and is sufficient to promote resistance independently, the contribution of G727A remains inconclusive. This mutation was identified in a metastatic tumor biopsy from 1 of 168 patients with ER+ breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy and also expressed the ERBB2 V777L mutation (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 S310Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and gallbladder cancer (PMID: 22908275, 24997986). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast or B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, colony formation in soft agar and cytokine-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 24997986, 29967253). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to other ERBB2 inhibitors neratinib, afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275, 29967253). Seven patients with cancers harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial demonstrated various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to stable disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 F671N mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 G309E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 22908275). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased colony formation in soft agar and cytokine-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275). However, while this mutation increases proliferation via protein dimerization when overexpressed, it does not increase protein autophosphorylation (PMID: 23220880, 31635022). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors afatinib, lapatinib, trastuzumab, and neratinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 D769H mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 29420467). This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial, breast cancer and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrate that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, colony formation in soft agar, transformation of mammary cell lines, and tumor growth in xenograft models compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880, 23843458). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253). One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (3.5 months) and one patient with colorectal cancer harboring this mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467)

The ERBB2 T862A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, murine breast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, cell proliferation, colony formation on soft agar and cytokine-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to the tyrosine kinase inhibitors lapatinib, afatinib, neratinib, sapitinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line (PMID: 22046346). In a neratinib basket trial, one patient with a solid tumor harboring this mutation had stable disease (3.5 months) upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 K831N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with colorectal cancer harboring ERBB2 K831N was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 G776_V777insVGC mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. ERBB2 exon 20 inframe insertion mutations are considered likely oncogenic. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 29420467). While this particular exon 20 mutation has not been functionally characterized, two patients with lung cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (5.3 and 5.4 months) and one patient with lung cancer harboring this mutation had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 V777L mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, normal breast epithelial, breast cancer, and murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, colony formation, tumor growth in xenograft models and cytokine-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22046346, 23220880). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, and neratinib when expressed in a breast epithelial cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment; however, other in vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to trastuzumab but sensitive to afatinib, neratinib, osimertinib and lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880, 29967253). In vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to endocrine therapy, including tamoxifen, fulvestrant and aromatase inhibition, and to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib, but is sensitive to the combination of neratinib with fulvestrant when expressed in breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and pathway activation analysis (PMID: 30531871, 30314968). One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation demonstrated a clinical response to the ERBB2 inhibitor combination therapy lapatinib + trastuzumab (PMID: 24516025). Thirteen patients with cancer harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial demonstrated various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to partial response (PMID: 29420467). Two patients with compound ERBB2 mutations including V777L had progressive disease (PMID: 29420467). One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation who showed intrinsic resistance to the combination of palbociclib and letrozole had a subsequent partial response to the combination of fulvestrant and neratinib (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 G776S mutation lies in the catalytic kinase domain of the protein (PMID: 18039657). This mutation has been found in stomach cancer (PMID: 15457249, 24816253). Expression of this mutation in murine bone, fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18039657). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrated that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib and trastuzumab but sensitive to sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 L651V mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and cervical cancer (PMID: 30449325). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 T733I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in gastric cancer (PMID: 16397024). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by slightly increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18413839). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation may be resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib when expressed in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines as measured by sustained cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 18413839). However, in vitro studies have also demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, neratinib, afatinib, sapitinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by decreased cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253). One patient with biliary tract cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease (3.7 months) upon treatment with neratinib in a neratinib basket trial (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 V697L mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and lung adenocarcinoma (PMID: 28481359, 27923066). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with endometrial cancer harboring ERBB2 V697L was treated with neratinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 G641S mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325)

The ERBB2 P780L mutation is located in the kinase domain of ERBB2. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 P780_Y781insGSP mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Exon 20 indel mutations have been found in lung cancer (PMID: 25899785, 23610105, 22325357, 21353324,16775247). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro and in vivo xenograft studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab, but sensitive to lapatinib, osimertinib, sapitinib, afatinib, and neratinib when expressed in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines as measured by cell proliferation and tumor growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 Y835F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity and cell proliferation compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 23220880).

The ERBB2 L49H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioma (PMID: 23243055). Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in colony formation and protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 18772890, 23389443, 18772396).

The ERBB2 G815R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and lung squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 27149842, 33796225). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing ERBB2 G815R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by IL-3-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 34741886). In a clinical trial, a patient with metastatic lung squamous cell carcinoma harboring ERBB2 G815R was treated with afatinib and achieved a progression-free survival of six months (PMID: 34741886).

The ERBB2 D808N mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in vitro and in breast epithelial and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, cellular invasion and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25435280).

The ERBB2 A775_G776insYVMA mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this variant in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by growth factor-independent proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 17311002, 29967253). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitors erlotinib, lapatinib, osimertinib and trastuzumab but sensitive to neratinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by in vitro cell proliferation and tumor burden in xenograft models (PMID: 17311002, 29967253).

The ERBB2 D277Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein and is at a hotspot residue. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer (PMID: 24121792, 28481359). Expression of this mutation in a cervical cancer cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased nuclear translocation compared to wildtype (Abstract: Liu, et al. Abstract# e24316, ASCO, 2018. https://ascopubs.org/doi/10.1200/JCO.2018.36.15_suppl.e24316). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib but not lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 E321G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, increased downstream signaling, growth factor-independent proliferation and increased colony formation in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 34997908). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors neratinib, afatinib and lapatinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275, 24971884).

The ERBB2 E719G mutation is located in between the transmembrane and kinase domains of the protein. This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib  (PMID: 18413839). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized per se, when expressed in Ba/F3 cells with the known oncogenic ERBB2 V659E mutation, this mutation conferred resistance to lapatinib as measured by sustained growth in the presence of lapatinib compared to V659E alone (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 R487W mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma and breast cancer (PMID: 30312528, 33008833). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 R677Q mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in liver, pancreas, neuroendocrine, urinary and colorectal cancer (PMID: 30371878, 30449325). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 R677Q suggest that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 D962N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype ERBB2 (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of ERBB2 D962N suggest that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 D326G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275).

The ERBB2 C630Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (Abstract: Xu et al. Abstract # 02-046, IASLC 2017. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1556086417315149?via%3Dihub). This mutation was found in a mutagenesis assay to confer resistance to lapatinib (PMID: 18413839).

The IKZF3-ERBB2 fusion protein results from exon 19 of ERBB2 fusing with IKZF3, resulting in only partially retaining the kinase domain of ERBB2. Although not functionally characterized per se, two patients with breast cancer harboring the IKZF3-ERBB2 fusion were treated with trastuzumab combined with chemotherapy and did not achieve pathologic complete response (PMID: 28453704).

ERBB2 amplification results in overexpression of the protein. Overexpression of ERBB2 in murine fibroblasts and in the mammary glands of genetically engineered mouse models have demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation and tumor growth (PMID: 23204226, 12124352, 11571643, 10716706, 2885917). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to trastuzumab when expressed in biliary tract cancer cell lines as measured by decreased proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 30659304). One patient with biliary tract cancer overexpressing ERBB2 had a partial response to an ERBB2-targeting antibody linked to a cytotoxic agent, ado-trastuzumab emtansine (Abstract: Mondaca et al. JCO PO, 2019. https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.19.00223). The therapeutic agents trastuzumab, ado-trastuzumab emtansine, lapatinib and pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab are FDA-approved drugs for the treatment of patients with ERBB2 amplified breast cancer. Trastuzumab is also FDA-approved for the treatment of patients with ERBB2-amplified gastric cancer.

The ERBB2 G778_P780dup mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880). Expression of this mutation in a breast epithelial cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation and increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitors lapatinib and trastuzumab but is sensitive to neratinib as measured by growth in soft agar upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880). In a neratinib basket trial, four patients with cancer harboring this mutation had stable disease or partial response upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 R647T mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 D769A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and is a hotspot reside. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 23843458).

The ERBB2 V659D mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lung adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 33587347). Although not functionally characterized, a patient with advanced lung adenocarcinoma harboring ERBB2 V659D was treated with afatinib, an irreversible tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) targeting HER2 family members, in combination with apatinib, a TKI targeting VEGFR2, and achieved good efficacy and tolerable adverse reactions (PMID: 33587347).

The ERBB2 D821N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating, as measured by moderate colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18413839). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib when expressed in a murine B-cell cell line as measured by sustained cell proliferation in the presence of the drug (PMID: 18413839).

The ERBB2 S649T mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in kidney cancer (PMID: 30371878). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 L674H mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 I767M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23220880, 25994018). Expression of this mutation in normal breast epithelial, murine fibroblast and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, cellular proliferation, and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25994018, 29967253). However, there is conflicting data for this mutation. Expression in MCF-10A cells demonstrated that this protein is likely neutral as measured by in vitro kinase assays, western blots for downstream activity, and growth in matrigel that was comparable to wildtype (PMID: 23220880). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, afatinib, sapitinib, osimertinib and neratinib when expressed in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines as measured by decreased colony growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 23220880, 29967253).

The ERRB2 I628M mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 30531871). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation was identified in a metastatic tumor biopsy from 1 of 168 patients with ER+ breast cancer who had received prior endocrine therapy (PMID: 30531871).

The ERBB2 S335C mutation is located in the extracellular subdomain II of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 26305917). While publications have mentioned that this mutation is activating, there is no data demonstrating functional characterization of the protein (PMID: 23630663).

The ERBB2 V659K mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation in the presence of wildtype ERBB2 compared to wildtype ERBB2 alone (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 F1030C mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in liver cancer (PMID: 30371878). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 S310F mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein (PMID: 22908275, 24997986). This mutation has been found in bladder, lung, breast and colon cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, colony formation in soft agar and cytokine-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 22908275, 24997986). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors osimertinib, neratinib, afatinib, lapatinib and trastuzumab when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22908275, 29967253). Single patients with breast cancer harboring this mutation have demonstrated clinical responses to ERBB2 inhibitor combination therapies, trastuzumab + pertuzumab and lapatinib + trastuzumab (PMID: 26358791, 24516025). Twenty-two patients with cancers harboring this mutation in a neratinib basket trial demonstrated various clinical responses to neratinib, ranging from progressive disease to complete response (PMID: 29420467).

The ERBB2 E770_A771insAYVM mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 26559459). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro and in vivo xenograft studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib and osimertinib but sensitive to afatinib and neratinib when expressed in murine fibroblast and B-cells as measured by decreased cell proliferation and tumor burden upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 L663H mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by sustained growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325).

The ERBB2 T686A mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer (PMID: 30449325). There is conflicting data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 30449325). However, in vitro studies demonstrated that this threonine is required for phosphorylation and protein activation (PMID: 18799465).

The ERBB2 M774_A775insAYVM mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been expressed in colon cancer. Expression of this mutation in murine B-cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by cytokine-independent proliferation compared to wildtype. In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrated that it is resistant to erlotinib in colon epithelial cells as measured by sustained cell proliferation upon treatment with erlotinib (PMID: 17311002).

The ERBB2 A1232fs mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 25344691, 27149842). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it may be activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). However, expression in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor trastuzumab, but sensitive to lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 K753M mutation is located within the ATP-binding pocket of the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a breast cancer cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by abolished protein activation (PMID: 16489002).

The ERBB2 A293T mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal and ovarian cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The ERBB2 R138Q mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in head and neck cancer (PMID: 25303977). Expression of this mutation in murine B-cell and fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no change in proliferation or foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon treatment (PMID: 29967253).

The ERBB2 D277G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast and B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253). One patient with bladder cancer harboring this mutation along with ERBB2 S310F had progressive disease upon treatment with neratinib (PMID: 29420467).

The EZH2 Y646C mutation is located in the enzymatic SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lymphoma (PMID: 21275949, 28419429, 20081860). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in lymphoma cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by preferential modification of dimethylated H3K27 residues instead of un- or monomethylated residues compared to wildtype (PMID: 21078963, 21190999, 25402979).

The ERBB2 R784C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 26320869). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it may be activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). However, expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it was neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29967253). In vitro studies of this mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to the ERBB2 inhibitors trastuzumab, lapatinib, sapitinib, afatinib, neratinib, and osimertinib when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29967253).

biomark_group: Oncogenic Mutations (excluding Y646S, Y646H, Y646C, Y646F, Y646N, A682G and A692V)
var_description: The EZH2 K665E mutation is located in the SET domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. In silico analysis of EZH2 K665E suggests that the mutation is inactivating (PMID: 28561778).

biomark_group: Oncogenic Mutations (excluding Y646S, Y646H, Y646C, Y646F, Y646N, A682G and A692V)
var_description: The EZH2 T683I mutation is located in the SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (PMID: 24030381). In vitro studies with patient-derived cells expressing EZH2 T683I demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by complete loss of methyltransferase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 38072134). Preclinical studies of cells expressing EZH2 T683I and C538Y demonstrate sensitivity to the EZH2 inhibitor EPZ-6438 and EED inhibitor A-395 as measured by lower IC50 values compared to wildtype (PMID: 38072134).

EZH2 amplification results in overexpression of the protein. This alteration has been found in several tumor types and has been implicated as a marker of poor prognosis in various solid tumors (PMID: 12374981, 14500907, 21837672, 16330673, 16330673). EZH2 overexpression in natural killer and natural killer T-cell lymphoma cell lines resulted in a growth advantage compared to wildtype (PMID: 23529930).

biomark_group: Oncogenic Mutations (excluding Y646S, Y646H, Y646C, Y646F, Y646N, A682G and A692V)
var_description: The EZH2 R690C mutation is located in the enzymatic SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lymphoma (PMID: 20601953). Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased H3K27 methylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20601953).

The ERBB2 D742H mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation in breast epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in cell viability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

biomark_group: Oncogenic Mutations (excluding Y646S, Y646H, Y646C, Y646F, Y646N, A682G and A692V)
var_description: The EZH2 C552R mutation is located in the CXC domain of the protein. In vitro studies with patient-derived cells expressing EZH2 C552R demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by complete loss of methyltransferase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 38072134). Preclinical studies of cells expressing EZH2 C552R and P527H demonstrate sensitivity to the EZH2 inhibitor EPZ-6438 and EED inhibitor A-395 as measured by lower IC50 values compared to wildtype (PMID: 38072134).

The EZH2 A692V mutation (also cited as EZH2 A687V) is located in the SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lymphoma and multiple myeloma (PMID: 30555699, 24052547, 21796119, 28572459). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased H3K27 trimethylation and preferential modification of di- and monomethylated residues instead of unmethylated residues compared to wildtype (PMID: 22850114, 25402979, 25671303). Patients with follicular lymphoma harboring this mutation respond to treatment with tazemetostat, and patients with A692V-mutant follicular lymphoma are included in the tazemetostat FDA-approval (Abstract: Morschhauser et al. Abstract# 123, ASH 2019. https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/134/Supplement_1/123/426294/Phase-2-Multicenter-Study-of-Tazemetostat-an-EZH2).

The EZH2 R502Q mutation is located in the non-SET region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 34070172). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation has possible impact on protein function (PMID: 25079552).

The EZH2 Y646F mutation is located in the enzymatic SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lymphoma (PMID: 21796119, 20081860). Expression of this mutation in vitro, in human embryonic kidney and lymphoma cell lines, and in transgenic mouse models demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein stability, preferential modification of dimethylated H3K27 residues instead of un- or monomethylated residues, increased levels of H3K27 trimethylation compared to wildtype and the formation of lymphoma and melanoma in vivo (PMID: 21078963, 21190999, 25402979, 24469040, 25671303). In addition, a mouse model of B-cell lymphoma expressing this mutation had reduced levels of T-cell infiltrates compared to models expressing wildtype (PMID: 30705065).

Preclinical studies of cells expressing EZH2 R690H and C576Y demonstrate sensitivity to the EZH2 inhibitor EPZ-6438 and EED inhibitor A-395 as measured by lower IC50 values compared to wildtype (PMID: 38072134).

var_description: EZH2 overexpression has been observed in several tumor types and has been implicated as a marker of poor prognosis in various solid tumors (PMID: 12374981, 14500907, 21837672, 16330673, 16330673). EZH2 overexpression in natural killer and natural killer T-cell lymphoma cell lines resulted in a growth advantage compared to wildtype (PMID: 23529930).

The EZH2 Y646H mutation is located in the enzymatic SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lymphoma and Ewing's sarcoma (PMID: 25223734, 28481359, 21796119, 20081860). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in lymphoma cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by preferential modification of dimethylated H3K27 residues instead of un- or monomethylated residues compared to wildtype (PMID: 21078963, 21190999, 25402979).

The EZH2 P577L mutation is located in the enzymatic SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute lymphoblastic T-cell leukemia (PMID: 25595890). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation has a structurally destabilizing effect on the second zinc-binding domain of the protein (PMID: 24367637).

var_description: EZH2 truncating mutations can produce several forms of C-terminally truncated proteins. These mutations have been found in myelodysplastic syndromes (PMID: 20601954). EZH2 loss in hematopoietic stem cells results in defective differentiation (PMID: 27926872). Patients harboring EZH2 truncating mutations have exhibited biallelic mutation or loss of heterozygosity at the EZH2 locus (PMID: 20601954).
