Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of NIH3T3 cells expressing FGFR2-CLIP1 have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with FGFR inhibitors INCB054828, AZD4547, BGJ398, JNJ-42756493 and ponatinib as measured by inhibition of cell viability following treatment (PMID: 31371345). In a case report, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-CLIP1 was treated with INCB054828 and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 31371345).

The FGFR2-LZTFL1 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement fusing intron 17 of FGFR2 and intron 7 of LZTFL1, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a case report, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring FGFR2-LZTFL1 was treated with JNJ-42756493 and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 11 months (PMID: 30267839).

The FGFR2 V754I mutation is located in the second kinase domain of the FGFR2 protein. Expression of this mutation in mouse fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by cell transformation, proliferation and colony formation in soft agar comparable to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 26048680).

The FGFR2 K659M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a patient with FGFR2-fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma following progression on the FGFR kinase inhibitor BGJ398 (PMID: 28034880). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, in silico structural modeling of this mutation suggests that it confers resistance to BGJ398 by destabilizing the inactive conformation of the kinase to which BGJ398 binds (PMID: 28034880)

The FGFR2-KIAA1967 fusion contains the extracellular, transmembrane and kinase domains of FGFR2 fused to the full KIAA1967 protein (PMID: 23558953). This fusion has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 23558953). Expression of this fusion in in vitro assays demonstrates that it is likely activating as measured by increased factor-independent dimerization compared to wildtype (PMID: 23558953).

The FGFR2 D101Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 18552176). Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrared that it is activating as measured by increased anchorage-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 18552176).

The FGFR2 R678G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro kinase assays have demonstrated that this mutation is likely activating as measured by increased auto- and effector-phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 17803937).

The FGFR2-CIT fusion contains the extracellular, transmembrane and kinase domains of FGFR2 fused to the coiled-coil domain of CIT. Expression of this mutation in cell lines demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased dimerization in cells in the absence of ligand compared to wildtype cells (PMID: 23558953).

The FGFR2-DDX21 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal DDX21, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a Phase I clinical trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma expressing FGFR2-DDX21 was treated with debio-1347 and demonstrated stable disease (PMID: 30745300).

The FGFR2 I547V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells suggests that it is activating, as measured by increased FGFR2 phosphorylation and proliferation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 23908597). In vitro experiments suggest that this variant is resistant to dovitinib but sensitive to ponatinib, as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23908597).

The FGFR2 T729S mutation is located in the second kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in mouse fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by cell transformation, proliferation and colony formation in soft agar comparable to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 26048680).

The FGFR2 D471N mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 D471N demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by wildtype comparable transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 E565G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in Ba/F3 cells suggested that it is activating, as measured by increased kinase activity and proliferation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 23908597). In vitro studies of FGFR2 E565G suggest that it is resistant to dovitinib, as measured by sustained growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 23908597).

The FGFR2 E596K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 E596K demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 P303L mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 25148578). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 P303L demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2-AHCYL1 fusion joins exon 19 of FGFR2 with exon 5 of AHCYL1, resulting in a fusion protein retaining the immunoglobulin-like, transmembrane and kinase domains of FGFR and the coiled-coil domain of AHCYL1. Expression of this fusion protein in NIH-3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased FGFR2 pathway activation, colony formation and in vivo tumor formation compared to kinase-dead versions of the fusion protein (PMID: 24122810).

The FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion contains the extracellular, transmembrane, and kinase domains of FGFR2 fused to the C-terminus of PPHLN1. Expression of the FGFR2-PPHLN1 fusion in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by increased colony formation in soft agar assays compared to wildtype (PMID: 25608663). Cell lines expressing this mutation were found to be sensitive to small molecule inhibitors of FGFR (PMID: 25608663).

The FGFR2 L770V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 19147536). Structural modeling suggests that this mutation would impair the ability of FGFR2 to activate the downstream phospholipase C-gamma pathway (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 E718K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 E718K demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 Y328N mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 Y328N demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity and proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 E160A mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type domain 2 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 19147536). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation disrupts the heparan sulfate interaction of the protein and negatively impacts dimerization (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2-FAM76A fusion contains the extracellular, transmembrane and kinase domains of FGFR2 fused to the FAM76A protein beginning at exon 2 (PMID: 24563622). Expression of this fusion in CP70 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation and anchorage independent growth compared to a LacZ control (PMID: 24563622).

The FGFR2 A67V mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in epithelioid trophoblastic tumors (PMID: 31954539). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 A67V demonstrate this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2-TTC28 fusion is a fusion of the N-terminus of FGFR2, including the kinase domain, with the C-terminus of TNS1. In vivo studies with patient-derived mouse models expressing FGFR2-TTC28 demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by tumor growth (PMID: 37270847). Preclinical studies of the fusion demonstrate sensitivity to RLY-4008 as measured by tumor regression in xenograft models following treatment (PMID: 37270847). In a Phase I trial, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-TTC28 was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 24.1 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2 C382R mutation (also known as C383R) is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein (PMID: 17525745). This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 33926920). Expression of this mutation in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased autophosphorylation in the absence of ligand and increased cell transformation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 9136983). In vitro studies with 3T3 cells expressing the mutation demonstrated resistance to clinical multikinase FGFR inhibitor dovitinib as measured by low efficacy in reducing cell growth as compared to treatment with FGFR-selective inhibitors (PMID: 34272467). In a Phase I trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 C382R was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 35176457). In another Phase I trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 C382R was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 9.2 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2 L617M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells suggests that it is activating, as measured by increased FGFR2 phosphorylation and proliferation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 23908597). In vitro experiments suggest that this variant is resistant to dovitinib but sensitive to ponatinib, as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23908597).

The FGFR2 F276C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 33926920). Expression of this mutation in a hepatobiliary cell line demonstrated that this mutation is likely activating as measured by increased activation of downstream effectors, such as ERK, compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 30761385). This mutation results in altered subcellular localization of FGFR2 from the plasma membrane to the endoplasmic reticulum (PMID: 30761385). A patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring the FGFR2 F276C mutation had a partial response to treatment with the FGFR-inhibitor BGJ398 (PMID: 30761385, 33926920).

The FGFR2-ATE1 fusion protein results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma, among others (PMID: 35948633). Expression of this fusion in mice demonstrated that it is activating as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice with orthotopically transplanted tumors expressing this fusion demonstrated sensitivity to clinical FGFR inhibitor AZD4547 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 G227E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in HEK293 cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by impaired receptor processing, impaired trafficking to the cell membrane and reduced ability to stimulate cell proliferation upon ligand stimulation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 E219K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Structural modeling of the FGFR2 E219K mutation suggests that it may prevent ligand-dependent dimerization of FGFR (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 S792fs*4 mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice expressing the corresponding mouse isoform FGFR2 S697fs*4 demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and of patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 G701S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. The FGFR2 G701S mutation is found in melanoma (PMID: 19147536). Mapping of this mutation to the FGFR2 crystal structure suggests that this mutation would impair the kinase activity of the protein, likely leading to loss of function (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 G305R mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 19147536). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 G305R demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 R399* mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 R399* demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 H167_N173del mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 33926920). Expression of this mutation in NIH-3T3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by oncogenic cell transformation and tumor formation in xenograft mice compared to wildtype (PMID: 33926920). In vitro studies suggest that this mutation is sensitive to inhibition with Debio1347 and futibatinib (PMID: 33926920). Two patients with cholangiocarcinoma harboring this mutation had durable partial responses to the FGFR-inhibitor Debio1347 (PMID: 33926920) while one patient who developed a second FGFR2 mutation (L618F) and acquired resistance to Debio1347 went on to have a partial response to futibatinib (PMID: 33926920).

The FGFR2 R664W mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 R664W demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 S252W mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 18552176). Expression of this mutation in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased anchorage-independent growth and downstream signaling compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 18552176, 17525745). This mutation activates FGFR2 downstream signaling by increasing receptor affinity for FGF9 which is commonly deregulated in endometrial cancer (PMID: 17525745).

The FGFR2 S372C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, it has been found recurrently as a germline mutation in patients with Syndromic Craniosynostosis and Beare-Stevenson syndrome (PMID: 8696350, 10425034, 11781872, 17525745), is paralogous to the activating FGFR3 G370C mutation (PMID: 12009017).

The FGFR2-NRAP fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal NRAP, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a case report, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-NRAP was treated with BGJ398 and TAS-120 and demonstrated a partial response with a progression-free survival of 7.1 months and 17.2 months, respectively (PMID: 31109923). In a second case report, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-NRAP was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated a progression-free survival of 17.2 months (PMID: 36190545). In a Phase I trial, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-NRAP was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 21.7 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2 V248D mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation is found in melanoma (PMID: 19147536). Mapping of this mutation to the FGFR2 crystal structure suggests that this mutation may impair the tertiary folding of the protein (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 S789* mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice expressing the corresponding mouse isoform FGFR2 S694* demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and of patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 K526E mutation is located at the cleft between the two portions of the FGFR2 tyrosine kinase domain. In vitro kinase assays demonstrated that this mutation is likely activating as measured by increased kinase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 17803937). Molecular analysis studies predicted that the K526E mutation may stabilize the activation loop in an active conformation (PMID: 16061565).

The FGFR2-ZMYM4 fusion combines the N-terminus of FGFR2 up to exon 17 with the C-terminus of ZMYM4 starting from exon 10, resulting in a fusion protein containing an intact FGFR2 kinase domain (PMID: 28034880). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, other FGFR2 fusions have been shown to be oncogenic and therefore this fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 26048680, 23558953). This mutation was found in a patient with cholangiocarcinoma who responded to the FGFR inhibitor BGJ398, though with limited durability due to the eventual emergence of acquired FGFR2 resistance mutations (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR2-WDHD1 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal WDHD1, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a Phase II clinical trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-WDHD1 was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 8.8 months (PMID: 33218975).

The FGFR2-USP33 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal USP33, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a Phase I/II trial, a patient with pancreatic cancer harboring FGFR2-USP33 was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 10.7 months (PMID: 33106918).

Fusions of FGFR2 arise from chromosomal translocations that generally fuse the N-terminal kinase-domain-containing portion of FGFR2 with the C-terminal portion of a partner protein; however, fusions involving the C-terminus of FGFR2 have also been described. FGFR2 fusions have been detected in a variety of human cancers, including gastric, breast cancers and CNS tumors (PMID: 28430863, 26254407, 34551969). These fusions often result in overexpression of the FGFR2 protein and constitutive activation of FGFR2 tyrosine kinase activity, which has been demonstrated to be transforming as shown by increased colony growth (PMID: 23558953, 25608663). In vitro and xenograft assays with FGFR2-amplified cell lines demonstrate increased sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor regorafenib compared to cell lines without FGFR2 amplification (PMID: 29573334). Patients with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma carrying FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements demonstrated an objective response rate of 25.4% to the highly selective, irreversible FGFR1–4 inhibitor futibatinib (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2-TACC3 fusion contains the extracellular, transmembrane and kinase domains of FGFR2 fused to the coiled-coil domain of TACC3 (PMID: 26048680). This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 26048680). Expression of this fusion in NIH-3T3 cells demonstrated that this fusion is activating, as measured by increased factor-independent dimerization, proliferation and colony formation in soft agar compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 26048680). In vitro studies suggest that this fusion is sensitive to small molecule inhibitors of FGFR2, such as BGJ398, as measured by decreased colony formation upon drug treatment (PMID: 26048680).

The FGFR2 Y812* mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice expressing the corresponding mouse isoform FGFR2 Y717* demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and of patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 I642V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased levels of downstream MAPK pathway activation and decreased kinase activity compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2 Y381D mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation is found in bent bone dysplasia syndrome (BBDS). Expression of this mutation in growth plate cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased nucleolar localization, increased MAPK pathway signaling and mitotic activity and decreased cell differentiation (PMID: 24908667).

The FGFR2-TACC2 fusion protein is a fusion between exons 1-17 of FGFR2 and exons 7-17 TACC2 and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma and poorly cohesive gastric carcinoma (PMID: 35948633, 34551773). Expression of this fusion in mice demonstrated that it is activating as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies of mice with orthotopically transplanted tumors expressing this fusion demonstrated sensitivity to clinical FGFR2 inhibitor AZD4547 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In vitro studies with the MKN-45 and NUGC4 cell lines expressing this fusion demonstrated sensitivity to clinical FGFR2 inhibitors BGJ398, AZD4547 and erdafitinib as measured by suppressed cell growth (PMID: 34551773). In a case report, a patient with gastrointestinal stromal tumors harboring a KIT exon 11 in-frame deletion acquired the FGFR2-TACC2 fusion after several rounds of various tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatments (PMID: 35170141).

The FGFR2 R399Q mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 R399Q demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 E475K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in HEK293 or Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as it has kinase activity similar to wildtype FGFR2 and decreased proliferation compared wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 19147536).

The FGFR2-CCDC147 fusions results from an out-of-strand rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal CCDC147, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (Abstract: Vaslin et al. Abstract# 689, AACR 2015. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/75/15_Supplement/689/604865/Abstract-689-Characterization-of-two-novel). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with NMRI nude mice expressing FGFR2-CCDC147 demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by increased tumor growth compared to vehicle control (Abstract: Vaslin et al. Abstract# 689, AACR 2015. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/75/15_Supplement/689/604865/Abstract-689-Characterization-of-two-novel). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and Rat-2 cells expressing FGFR2-CCDC147 have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with debio-1347 as measured by inhibition of cellular proliferation and tumor growth (Abstract: Vaslin et al. Abstract# 689, AACR 2015. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/75/15_Supplement/689/604865/Abstract-689-Characterization-of-two-novel).

The FGFR2 Y375C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the FGFR2 protein. This mutation is found in Beare-Stevenson cutis gyrata syndrome (BSS) and cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 22585574, 33926920). Expression of this mutation in a mouse model of BSS demonstrated it is likely activating as measured by ligand-independent phosphorylation of FGFR2 and downstream activation of p38 signaling, as well as abnormal cell proliferation and differentiation, as evidenced by immunohistological staining (PMID: 22585574). Expression of this mutation in rat chondrosarcoma chondrocytes resulted in increased downstream pathway activation as measured by increased phosphorylated ERK and LRP6 compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 22558232). In a Phase I trial, a patient with a primary unknown cancer harboring FGFR2 Y375C was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 19.2 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2 N549S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein (PMID: 23908597). Expression of this mutation in hematopoietic cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased kinase activity of FGFR2, increased cell proliferation and moderate resistance to FGFR inhibitors such as dovitinib in cell culture (PMID: 23908597).

The FGFR2 L560F mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 L560F demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The KLK2-FGFR2 fusion involves the N-terminus of KLK2 fused to the C-terminus of FGFR2. This fusion has been identified in prostate cancer (PMID: 31043681). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing KLK2-FGFR2 demonstrated this fusion is likely activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467). Other in vitro studies with NIH3T3 cells expressing the fusion also demonstrate KLK2-FGFR2 is activating as measured by enhanced migration and signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 31043681). KLK2-FGFR2 is suggested to be sensitive to treatment with FGFR inhibitors AZD-4547, BGJ398, JNJ-42756943, TAS-120 and Ponatinib as measured by decreased cell viability compared to control cells (PMID: 31043681).

The FGFR2 H544Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 H544Q demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The deletion of exon 18 in FGFR2 involves various FGFR2 alterations that cause truncation of the C-terminus of FGFR2. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma, among others (PMID: 35948633). Expression of Fgfr2ΔE18 variants in mice demonstrated that it is activating as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors (PMID: 35948633). In vivo mouse studies with Fgfr2ΔE18 variant driven tumor transplants demonstrated sensitivity when treated with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). Patient-derived xenografts with Fgfr2ΔE18 variants also demonstrated sensitivity when treated with debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 L776fs*6 mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice expressing the corresponding mouse isoform FGFR2 L681fs*6 demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and of patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 C287R mutation is located in the helical domain of the FGFR2 protein. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma, among others (PMID: 35948633). Expression of this fusion in mice demonstrated that it is activating as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies of mice with orthotopically transplanted tumors expressing this fusion demonstrated sensitivity to clinical FGFR2 inhibitor AZD4547 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 E565A mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in two patients with FGFR2-fusion positive cholangiocarcinoma following progression on the FGFR kinase inhibitor BGJ398 (PMID: 28034880). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, in silico structural modeling of this mutation suggests that it confers resistance to BGJ398 by destabilizing the inactive conformation of the kinase to which BGJ398 binds (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR2-G3BP2 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement fusing exons 1 through exon 16 of FGFR2 and the entirety of G3BP2, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). In vitro studies with PDC-DUC18828 cells expressing FGFR2-G3BP2 demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by constitutive kinase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 36274097). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies with patient-derived models of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma expressing FGFR2-G3BP2 have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with pemigatinib as measured by impaired cell viability following treatment (PMID: 36274097).

The FGFR2 K641R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein (PMID: 23527311). This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 28034880). Expression of this mutation in HEK293 cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 23527311). Crystal structure analysis of this mutation reveals that it disrupts kinase autoinhibition, enabling ligand-independent activity, and confers resistance to BGJ398 by destabilizing the inactive conformation of the kinase to which BGJ398 binds (PMID: 28034880, 17803937). This mutation was found in a patient with FGFR2-fusion positive cholangiocarcinoma following progression on the FGFR kinase inhibitor BGJ398 (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR2 T341P mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 9539778).

The FGFR2 H242Y mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type II of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 26343386). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 H242Y demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 W290R mutation occurs in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a mouse model demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased FGFR2 expression, signaling, and development of murine features typical of Crouzon syndrome (PMID: 20503384, 22872266).

The FGFR2 V392A mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 V392A demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2 L617V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a patient with FGFR2-fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma following progression on the FGFR kinase inhibitor BGJ398 (PMID: 28034880). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, in silico structural modeling of this mutation suggests that it confers resistance to BGJ398 by destabilizing the inactive conformation of the kinase to which BGJ398 binds (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR2 M640I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 M640I demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2-HOOK1 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal HOOK1, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a clinical study, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-HOOK1 was treated with an FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated an overall survival of 804 days (PMID: 33106918).

The FGFR2 V564I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells suggests that it is activating, as measured by increased FGFR2 phosphorylation and proliferation compared to wildtype FGFR2 (PMID: 23908597). FGFR2 V564I was identified as an acquired resistance mutation in patients with cholangiocarcinoma and gastric cancer following disease progression after treatment with pemigatnib (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419). In vitro experiments suggest that this variant is resistant to dovitinib and ponatinib, as measured by sustained cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23908597). This mutation was identified in a screen for BGJ398 resistant FGFR2 mutations in which TEL-FGFR2 expressing cells were exposed to lethal doses of BGJ398 and the resistant clones were analyzed for the presence of mutations (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR2 I288_E295delinsT mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 33926920). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, one patient with FGFR2 I288_E295delinsT mutant cholangiocarcinoma had a durable partial response to Debio1347 for 24+ months (PMID: 33926920).

The FGFR2 W290C mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 18552176). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 W290C demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity and proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467). In a Phase I trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2 W290C was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 12.7 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2-CCDC170 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal CCDC170, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). Therefore, while not characterized per se, as a fusion that results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2, this fusion is likely oncogenic (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a Phase II clinical trial, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma expressing FGFR2-CCDC170 was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 6.9 months (PMID: 33218975).

The FGFR2-KIAA1598 fusion (also known as FGFR2-SHTN1) results from an in-frame rearrangement fusing exon 8 through exon 18 of KIAA1598 to exon 1 through exon 17 of FGFR2, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This fusion has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma and non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 31911531, 30267839). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2-KIAA1598 demonstrated this fusion is likely activating as measured by increased transformation activity and proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a case report, a patient with cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-KIAA1598 was treated with infigratinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of eight months (PMID: 31911531).

The FGFR2 N549T mutation is located at the cleft between the two portions of the FGFR2 tyrosine kinase domain. In vitro kinase assays demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by increased auto- and effector-phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 17803937). Crystallization studies suggest that this mutation may lead to ligand-independent kinase activation by directly disengaging the molecular brake in the hinge region (PMID: 17803937).

The FGFR2 R330W mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 R330W demonstrate this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR2-POC1B fusion is a fusion of the N-terminus of FGFR2, including the kinase domain, with the C-terminus of POC1B. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, other FGFR2 fusions have been shown to be oncogenic and therefore this fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 26048680, 23558953). In a Phase I trial, a patient with extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-POC1B was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 4.8 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2 A371V mutation is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 A371V demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

This mutation has been identified in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633). In a clinical study, a patient with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring FGFR2-TRIM55 was treated with an FGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor and demonstrated an overall survival of 662 days (PMID: 33106918).

The FGFR2 S773* mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein and results in the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35948633). In vivo studies with mice expressing the corresponding mouse isoform FGFR2 T678* demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 35948633). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

The FGFR2 K659E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 17525745). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR2 K659E demonstrate this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity and proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

FGFR2 amplification is often associated with constitutive FGFR2 activation leading to increased tumor cell proliferation and survival. The oncogenic mechanism is likely increased downstream signaling through target pathways PI3K/AKT and MAPK/ERK, due to constitutive and ligand-independent receptor activation (PMID: 20094046). FGFR2-IIIb specific antibody, GP369 has been used to support the findings that dysregulated FGFR signaling is one of the critical pathways involved in tumor maintenance and initiation. Patients with amplification of FGFR2 signaling could benefit from therapeutic intervention with FGFR2 inhibitors (PMID 20709759). This is especially seen in breast and gastric cancers and it has provided the rationale for targeting this pathway in clinical trials (PMID: 20101236, PMID 20709759). Patients with advanced solid tumors (cholangiocarcinoma, gastric and breast cancers) harboring FGFR2 amplifications demonstrated objective responses to the highly selective, irreversible FGFR1–4 inhibitor futibatinib (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR2-KCTD1 fusion results from an in-frame rearrangement between N-terminal FGFR2 and C-terminal KCTD1, causing the truncation of exon 18 of FGFR2. This mutation has been identified in cholangiocarcinoma (PMID: 35100704). Numerous FGFR2 variants with truncation of exon 18 have been shown in vivo to be activating and oncogenic as measured by rapid induction of mammary tumors in mice (PMID: 35948633). In vitro studies with NIH3T3 cells expressing FGFR2-KCTD1 demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by ligand-independent autophosphorylation and activation of downstream MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 26258846). Preclinical studies of mice and patient-derived xenografts expressing truncated FGFR2 exon 18 variants have demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with clinical FGFR2 inhibitors AZD4547, pemigatinib, BGJ398 and debio-1347 as measured by suppressed tumor growth (PMID: 35948633).

There is conflicting functional information for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 26992226). However, expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein stability (PMID: 29478821)

Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 26992226).

The FGFR3 A391E mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in Crouzon syndrome and bladder cancer (PMID: 23437153 ). Expression of this variant in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased activation in the absence of ligand compared to wildtype (PMID: 23437153).

FGFR3 fusions typically involve the N-terminus of FGFR3 fused to the C-terminus of a fusion partner, although there are some instances in which the N-terminus of a fusion partner is fused to the C-terminus of FGFR3. Expression of these fusions in murine and rat cell lines demonstrated that they are activating as measured by increased cell proliferation (PMID: 23661334, 23558953, 22837387).

The FGFR3 D617G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in aerodigestive tract cancer. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 26992226).

The FGFR3 G380R mutation is located in the transmembrane domain of the protein and is a hotspot residue. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in dwarfism (PMID: 10611230). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in vitro, in embryonic kidney and rat mesenchymal stem cell lines and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity and protein accumulation in mouse growth plates compared to wildtype (PMID: 10611230, 21324899, 12461689). However, expression of this mutation in a chondrocyte cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and differentiation compared to wildtype (PMID: 10646125).

Expression of this mutation in murine fibroblast, multiple myeloma and epithelial cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 11429702, 19749790, 11429702). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the FGFR inhibitor BGH398 when present in a TEL-FGFR3 Fusion-expressing murine B-cell line as measured by the sustained cell proliferation following drug treatment (PMID: 28034880).

In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the FGFR inhibitor BGJ398 when expressed in TEL-FGFR3 fusion-positive murine fibroblasts as measured by sustained proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 28034880).

The FGFR3 P63S mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR3 P63S demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR3 R669Q mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro kinase activity assays with FGFR3 R669Q demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26992226).

In a Phase II trial, a patient with cancer of unknown primary harboring FGFR3-RGS12 was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR3-TACC3 fusion involves the N-terminus of FGFR3, including the FGFR3 extracellular and kinase domains, fused to the C-terminus of TACC3, including the TACC3 coiled-coil domain. Two patients with glioma harboring this mutation demonstrated clinical responses to erdafitinib (PMID: 25609060). A patient with gastric cancer harboring an FGFR3–TACC3 fusion had a confirmed response to the highly selective, irreversible FGFR1–4 inhibitor futibatinib (PMID 34551969).
