In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors quizartinib, sorafenib, ponatinib, and crenolanib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-expressing murine B-cells as measured by sustained cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 26108694).

The FLT3 F691L mutation is located in the hinge region of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 23392356, 23969938, 22504184). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor sorafenib but sensitive to ponatinib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-expressing murine B-cells as measured by cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 19318574, 23430109).

The FLT3 S451F mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 18068628, 22658276, 27276561). Expression of this variant in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by downstream pathway activation and factor-independent growth (PMID: 18068628).

The FLT3 T167A mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18068628).

The FLT3 L601_K602insNVDFREYEYDL mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 27288520). Although not functionally characterized per se, expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FLT3 D586_E596dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 27288520). Expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FLT3 Y572C mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18068628).

The ETV6-FLT3 fusion involves the N-terminus of ETV6 fused to the C-terminus of FLT3. This mutation has been found in myeloproliferative disorders. Expression of this fusion protein in hematopoietic cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and cytokine-independent growth compared to other non-oncogenic ETV6-FLT3 fusion variations (PMID: 16761019).

The FLT3 S584_F605dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FLT3 K868N mutation occurs in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastric adenocarcinoma. Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 27272783).

The FLT3 V579A mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 14984498). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, cell proliferation and decreased apoptosis compared to wildtype (PMID: 16410449).

The FLT3 D835G mutation is located in the activation loop in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 27288520). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells and blast samples expressing FLT3 D835G demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 28077790). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrate resistance to PLX3397, sunitinib, AG1295, AGS324 and sorafenib, as measured by sustained cellular proliferation, and sensitivity to crenolanib, ponatinib, midostaurin, lestaurtinib, linifanib, quizartinib, TTT-3002 and E6201, as measured by inhibition of cellular proliferation (PMID: 25847190, 28077790, 26822154).

The FLT3 S585_F594dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 22237025). Although not functionally characterized per se, expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FLT3 D835N mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid and lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in simian fibroblast, murine B-cell and murine bone marrow cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ligand-independent protein and pathway activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 11290608, 15256420). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors quizartinib, sorafenib, ponatinib, and crenolanib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-expressing murine B-cells as measured by sustained cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 26108694).

The FLT3 F590G mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 14984498). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, cell proliferation and decreased apoptosis compared to wildtype (PMID: 16410449).

The FLT3 N676D mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor quizartinib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-positive murine B-cell line as measured by sustained protein activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 22875611).

FLT3 internal tandem duplications (ITDs) are located in either the juxtamembrane domain and/or the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. These mutations have been found in acute myeloid leukemia (AML) (PMID: 23631653). Expression of these mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447). Analysis of patients with AML harboring these mutations demonstrated that expression of ITDs that were composed of sequence endogenous to the wildtype FLT3 sequence were more likely to respond favorably to treatment with either chemotherapy or FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors as compared to patients expressing FLT3 ITDs composed of exogenous sequence in between the duplication (PMID: 30181385).

The FLT3 A680V mutation is located in the N-terminal kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 27288520). In vitro kinase activity assays with FLT3 A680V demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased autophosphorylation compared to wildtype (Abstract: Tarlock et al. Abstract# 617, Blood 2015. https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0006497118470668). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FLT3 A680V also demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased IL-3 independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 33563661). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with gilteritinib as measured by decreased cell viability and FLT3 phosphorylation upon drug treatment (PMID: 33563661).

The FLT3 Y842C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 15345593, 27276561). Expression of this mutation in murine bone marrow cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 15345593).

The FLT3 G831E mutation is located in the catalytic tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 18068628). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein activity and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18068628). However, structural modeling of the G831 residue demonstrated that this mutation may be inactivating due to stabilization in a permanently autoinhibited conformation (PMID: 18068628).

The FLT3 V592G mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18068628).

The FLT3 Y597_E598insDEYFYVDFREY mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 22817890). Although not functionally characterized per se, expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FLT3 S451E mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18068628).

The FLT3 N841I mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 15178581). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and downstream pathway activation compared to vector control (PMID: 15178581).

The FLT3 A627T mutation is located in the ATP binding pocket of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 22675565, 23856246). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the FLT3 small molecule inhibitor midostaurin when expressed in a murine B-cell line as measured by sustained cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 15374944).

The FLT3 D835H mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hematologic malignancies (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in simian fibroblast, murine B-cell and murine bone marrow cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ligand-independent protein and pathway activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 11290608, 15256420). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the FLT3 tyrosine kinase inhibitors sorafenib and ponatinib but is sensitive to quizartinib and crenolanib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-expressing murine B-cells as measured by sustained cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 26108694).

The FLT3 N676S mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia. In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor pexidartinib when expressed in FLT3 internal tandem duplication-positive murine B-cell line as measured by sustained protein activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 25847190).

The FLT3 D593_F594insSPEDNEYFYVD mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Although not functionally characterized per se, expression of FLT3 juxtamembrane domain internal tandem duplication mutations in murine bone marrow, murine B-cell and simian fibroblast cells lines and in an in vivo bone marrow transplant model demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation and the induction of an in vivo myeloproliferative phenotype compared to wildtype (PMID: 11756186, 23631653, 9737679, 11090077, 12384447).

The FOXL2 C134W mutation has been found in granulosa cell tumors. Expression of this mutation in a granulosa cell tumor cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating, as shown by a failure to induce apoptosis compared to wildtype FOXL2 (PMID: 23372819).

FOXL2 truncation mutations occur throughout the entire gene and result in loss of protein function. Loss of FOXL2 has been identified in Blepharophimosis syndrome type I and premature ovarian failure (PMID: 28924383, 15056605). In vitro studies with 293T cells expressing various truncated FOXL2 transcripts demonstrate that FOXL2 truncation is inactivating as measured by increased nuclear aggregation and loss of StAR inhibition compared to wildtype FOXL2 (PMID: 33796131).

GATA3 truncating mutations in the range of amino acids 1 to 307 occur in the N-terminal region of GATA3 and result in the loss of the zinc finger 2 domain and the C-terminus. GATA3 truncating mutations in this range have been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 27251275). Truncated N-terminal transcripts of GATA3 have been identified as inactivating as measured by reduced transcriptional regulation of genes compared to wildtype and truncated C-terminal transcripts of GATA3 (PMID: 27588951). Truncated N-terminal transcripts of GATA3 are suggested to negatively impact the dimerization of the protein (PMID: 27588951, 31107186, 25410484).

GATA3 amplification has been identified in pancreatic cancer, neuroblastoma and T-cell malignancies (PMID: 16087702, 20154722, 11441075). There are conflicting results on the functional effect of GATA3 amplification. In vitro studies with colorectal cancer cell lines overexpressing GATA3 demonstrate that amplification of GATA3 is likely neutral as measured by comparable levels of cellular apoptosis and tumor growth to normal GATA3 expression (PMID: 32760217). In contrast, other in vitro studies with FaDu and A375 head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells overexpressing GATA3 demonstrate that amplification of GATA3 is activating as measured by significantly increased cellular migration and invasion compared to GATA3 knockdown and control vectors (PMID: 28263977).

The GNA11 Q209L mutation is located in the GTP-binding pocket of the RAS-like domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in cutaneous and uveal melanoma (PMID: 21083380, 26825879). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased induction of cutaneous and uveal melanomas compared to wildtype (PMID: 29490280).

The GNA11 E234K mutation is located in the G-alpha domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 27149842). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNA11 E234K demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

GATA3 truncating mutations in the range of amino acids 308 to 443 occur in the C-terminal region of GATA3 and typically result in stable and functional proteins. GATA3 truncating mutations in this range have been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 15361840, 24758297). Truncated C-terminal transcripts of GATA3 have been identified as activating as measured by increased tumor growth, upregulation of genes related to peptidyl-tyrosine modification and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and increased protein stability compared to wildtype and truncated N-terminal transcripts of GATA3 (PMID: 27588951, 29535312, 32232341, 35154280). Preclinical studies with MCF10A cells expressing truncated C-terminal transcripts of GATA3 demonstrate sensitivity to inhibitors of the histone methyltransferases G6A/GLP as measured by reduced cell viability (PMID: 27588951).

The GNA11 E191G mutation is located in the G-alpha domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 29209985). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNA11 E191G demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

The GNA11 R183C mutation is located in the switch region I of the protein. This mutation has been found in uveal melanomas. Expression of this mutation in a murine melanocyte cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased tumor formation in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 21083380).

The GNAQ F228L mutation is located in the G-alpha domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 29209985). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNAQ F228L demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

The GNAQ G48V mutation is located in the G-alpha protein subunit of the protein. This mutation has been identified in hemangioma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 31189994). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNAQ G48V demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

The GNAQ T96S mutation is located in the G-protein alpha subunit region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26416732). In vitro studies with SK-Hep-1 cells expressing GNAQ T96S demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, migration and MAPK pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 33807071).

The GNAQ R183Q mutation is located in switch region I of the protein. This mutation has been found in uveal melanoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). It is mutually exclusive with the BRAF mutations and GNAQ/GNA11 Q209 mutations (PMID: 22236444). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNAQ R183Q demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

The GNAQ Q209L mutation is located in the GTP-binding pocket of the RAS-like domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in choroidal hemangioma and uveal melanoma (PMID: 31336681, 19718445, 21083380). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes and murine fibroblasts demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased anchorage-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 1328859, 19078957).

The GNAQ G48L mutation is located in the G-alpha protein subunit of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 33126538). In silico analysis of GNAQ G48L suggests that the mutation is activating through stabilization of the protein and increased MEK pathway activation (PMID: 33126538). GNAQ G48L is suggested to be sensitive to MEK inhibitor trametinib as measured by a patient with uveal melanoma harboring GNAQ G48L and FGFR4 C172G demonstrating stable disease after two months of treatment (PMID: 33126538).

The GNAQ Q209P mutation is located in the G-alpha domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 19078957). In vitro studies with HEK293T cells expressing GNAQ G209P demonstrated that the mutation is activating as measured by constitutive activation of downstream signaling pathways compared to wildtype (PMID: 30352874).

The GNAQ T175R mutation is located in the G-alpha domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 21083380). In vitro studies with uveal melanoma cells expressing GNAQ T175R demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by downstream signaling comparable to wildtype (PMID: 33262460).

The GNAS Q227R mutation is located in the GTP conformational change domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in pituitary tumors. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 2549426).

The GNAS Q227L mutation is located in the GTP conformational change domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 15246564). Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 2549426).

GATA3 deletions have been detected in patients with breast cancer and commonly results in the production of truncated protein forms (PMID: 15361840). Experimental studies suggest that these mutations alter the cellular localization of the protein (PMID: 15361840), and affects DNA-binding and transactivation abilities (PMID: 7829479, 10935639, 24758297, 26637396) leading to increased cellular invasiveness.

The GNAS R160C mutation is located in the G-protein alpha subunit of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. Although not functionally characterized, preclinical studies suggest that GNAS R160C is resistant to treatment with tipifarnib as measured by lack of tumor growth reduction compared to wildtype (PMID: 29760048).

The GNAS R201H mutation is located in the switch I domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in appendiceal adenocarcinoma and intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (PMID: 26257060, 28868010). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a transgenic mouse model for pancreatic cancer demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity and tumorigenesis in cooperation with the KRAS G12D mutation compared to wildtype (PMID: 2549426, 26257060).

The HNF1A T196A mutation is located in the DNA binding domain. Experimental evaluation of this mutation in Cos7 cells showed that it exhibits normal DNA binding and transactivation capacities (PMID: 21170474).

The GNAS R201C mutation is located in the switch I domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastric adenocarcinoma (PMID: 25288233). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model for intestinal cancer demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased intestinal adenoma formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20531296).

Experimental studies of HeLa cells containing deleted forms of HNF1A demonstrate that these mutations lead to a loss-of-function effect with defective nuclear localization of HNF1A (PMID: 12574234). Additionally, given the role of HNF1A in transcriptional regulation, loss of HNF1A in pancreatic cells leads to activation of AKT and mTOR signaling resulting in promotion of cell growth and defective apoptosis (PMID: 25793983) and indicating an oncogenic role of HNF1A loss.

The HNF1A I27L mutation is located in the N-terminus of the protein. While this mutation is a statistically significant cancer hotspot, and may predispose to diabetes when found in the germline, it is present in a large percentage of the population (gnomad) and is likely benign (PMID: 29895593, 26619011). In vitro studies with HEK293 and HepG2 cells expressing HNF1A I27L demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of regulation leading to an increase in reporter gene activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 29066969).

The HNF1A P291Qfs*51 mutation is located in the beta isoform C domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in the germline of families with maturity-onset diabetes of the young (MODY) and as a somatic mutation in colorectal cancer (PMID: 9313763,16917892,12574234, 12730871, 27756406). Structural analysis of HNF1A P291Qfs*51 suggests that the mutation is likely inactivating as measured by the loss of the transactivation domain (Abstract: AlSaif et al. Abstract# 35, HPB 2019. https://www.hpbonline.org/article/S1365-182X%2819%2930227-8/fulltext).

HNF1A truncating mutations are frequent germline events in patients with maturity onset diabetes of the young (MODY), predominantly occurring in the transactivation domain (PMID: 18003757). Experimental studies of HeLa cells containing truncated forms of HNF1A demonstrate that these mutations lead to a loss-of-function effect with aberrant cytoplasmic localization (PMID: 12574234). Additionally, given the role of HNF1A in transcriptional regulation, loss of HNF1A in pancreatic cells leads to activation of AKT and mTOR signaling resulting in promotion of cell growth and defective apoptosis (PMID: 25793983) and indicating an oncogenic role of HNF1A loss.

The HRAS G12Y mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased focus formation and growth in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS A59T mutation is located in the switch II region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in intestinal and esophageal cancer (PMID: 28481359, 25839328). Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as shown by increased protein activation and increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 1730690, 3043178).

The HRAS G12Q mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased focus formation and growth in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS G12C mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer and melanoma (PMID: 18024870, 22499344, 22683711). Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased focus formation and soft agar growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS K117N mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and thyroid cancer (PMID: 28481359, 22865907, 23264394). While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, it is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011).

The HRAS G12A mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and thyroid cancer (PMID: 25679062, 1708628, 18381570). Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased focus formation and soft agar growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS K117R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation is found in patients with Costello's syndrome (PMID: 16443854, 17054105). Expression of this mutation in vitro, in human embryonic kidney cells and in murine hematopoietic cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, pathway activation, and cytokine-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24247240, 17979197).

The HRAS G12V mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in cervical cancer (PMID: 9208611). Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased focus formation and soft agar growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684). In vivo studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the farnesyltransferase inhibitor tipifarnib in a genetically engineered model of HRAS G12V-driven thyroid cancer as measured by decreased pathway activation and reduced tumor burden (PMID: 24123531).

The HRAS Q61H mutation is located in the switch II region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in skin and thyroid cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 8453633, 12947056, 7630645, 26619011). Structural analysis of the Q61 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at Q61 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS A11_G12insVN mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 3018526).

The HRAS P34R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline variant in cardio-facio-cutaneous syndrome (PMID: 17211612). Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and anchorage-independent growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 16474404, 8246952).

The HRAS Q61R mutation is located in the switch II region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in adrenal cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 8453633, 12947056, 7630645, 26619011). Structural analysis of the Q61 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at Q61 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

In vitro expression of this mutation demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24224811).

The HRAS G12I mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased focus formation and growth in soft agar compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684).

The HRAS Q22K mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline variant in Costello's syndrome and congenital myopathy with excess muscle spindles (PMID: 17412879). This mutation has not yet been functionally characterized.

The HRAS Q61L mutation is located in the switch II region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in vemurafenib-treated squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 22256804). Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation compared to wildtype. Structural analysis of the Q61 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at Q61 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib in a murine B cell line as measured by sustained proliferation in the presence of the drug (PMID: 22256804).

Structural analysis of the Q61 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at Q61 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID:9219684).

The HRAS A11_G12insPGSG mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased focus formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 3018526).

Expression of this mutation in rat fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased focus formation and soft agar growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 6092966). Structural analysis of the G12 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for HRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at G12 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 9219684). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to the EGFR inhibitor erlotinib in head and neck squamous cancer cells as measured by sustained pathway activation and cell viability in the presence of the drug (PMID: 24123531).
