The KIT T574insTQLPYD mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 15930355). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a clinical study of 31 GIST patients treated with imatinib, one individual had an initial response to imatinib before developing secondary resistance (PMID: 15930355).

The KIT exon 14 T670I mutation is located in the kinase domain of KIT. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16751810, 16954519, 17545544, 17699867, 23840364). Biological characterization of this mutation in a variety of cell lines, including Ba/F3 cells, demonstrated that this alteration is activating and promotes growth, as demonstrated by pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 16751810, 16954519, 17545544, 17699867, 23840364). The KIT T670I mutation is a gatekeeper mutation that has been associated with resistance to most KIT-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors in vitro and in the clinical setting (PMID: 16551858, 1675110, 16954519, 17545544, 17699867, 23840364, 31270078).

The KIT V560del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in thymic cancer (PMID: 15201427, 22357254, 19861435) and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 16551858, 25605837) samples. Biological characterization of the KIT V560del variant in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as evidenced by pathway activation and factor-independent growth (PMID: 19861435). Cells expressing KIT V560del are sensitive to imatinib and sunitinib in vitro, as measured by decreased cell growth and decreased effector activation (PMID: 19861435)

The KIT N564_Y578del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16952044). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with a GIST harboring the KIT N564_Y578del mutation had a clinical response to imatinib treatment (PMID: 16952044).

The KIT Y823D mutation is located in the activation loop in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 18980976), chronic eosinophilic leukemia (PMID: 22301675) and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 15930355, 16551858, 16954519) samples. Biological characterization of this variant in Ba/F3 cells demonstrates that it is activating and promotes growth, as determined by pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 22301675). KIT Y823D interferes with the binding of imatinib to KIT, causing primary or secondary resistance to imatinib in the clinic (PMID: 18623623, 18955458). Though the KIT Y823D mutation confers resistance to imatinib and sunitinib, in vitro data suggests it retains sensitivity to motesanib (PMID: 18623623, 18955458, 22089421, 22069175, 20633291).

The KIT E839K mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in hematopoietic malignancies (PMID: 15790786). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells did not lead to pathway activation or transformation and is known to inactivate the kinase domain of the protein, suggesting that this variant is not oncogenic (PMID: 15790786, 9990072).

The KIT D820A mutation is located in the activation loop in exon 17 of KIT. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) samples (PMID: 25239608, 16954519, 18955458, 16954519, 23840364). While this variant has not been functionally validated, biological characterization of this alteration in Ba/F3 and patient-derived GIST cell lines in combination with known activating variants have demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to imatinib and sunitinib but sensitive to sorafenib and nilotinib (PMID: 25239608, 23840364). This mutation has been seen as a secondary KIT mutation in patients with GIST who have acquired resistance to imatinib (PMID: 18955458, 16954519).

The exon 13 KIT K642E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), melanoma and thymic cancer samples (PMID: 25239608, 14645423, 25304235, 24855380). Biological characterization of this variant in CHO and GIST cell lines determined that KIT K642E is activating, as evidenced by downstream pathway activation (PMID: 25239608, 14645423, 11526490, 16954519). While laboratory experiments demonstrate that GIST cells expressing KIT K642E may be sensitive to imatinib as measured by reduced KIT pathway output and growth inhibition (PMID: 14645423, 11526490), the clinical data is not conclusive. Indeed, two patients with GIST harboring exon 13 KIT mutations had partial clinical responses to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 14645423), a single patient with thymic cancer harboring KIT K642E failed to respond to imatinib and instead responded to sorafenib (PMID: 24855380). Three patients with melanoma harboring the KIT K642E mutation had stable disease in response to nilotinib treatment (PMID: 23940219, 25695690).

The KIT D820V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized, a patient harboring a KIT D820V-mutant GIST demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with avapritinib as measured by tumor reduction (PMID: 29093181). KIT D820V was identified as a secondary mutation associated with imatinib resistance in a patient with a GIST (PMID: 18294292).

The KIT V560D mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 9438854, 16551858, 16954519, 18955458, 25605837, 16954519, 23840364, 25239608) and melanoma (PMID: 23775962). Biological characterization of the KIT V560D variant in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as evidenced by pathway activation and factor-independent growth (PMID: 25239608). Cells expressing KIT V560D are sensitive to FDA-approved multikinase inhibitors imatinib, sunitinib, regorafinib and ponatinib in vitro, as measured by decreased cell growth and decreased effector activation (PMID: 25239608). In a clinical study of patients with GIST treated with imatinib, two patients with GIST harboring KIT V560D had clinical benefit upon treatment with imatinib (one partial response and one response with secondary progression) (PMID: 16551858).

The KIT exon 11 P577_R588dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation is found recurrently in gastrointestinal stromal tumor patient samples and comprises a hotspot, suggesting it is likely oncogenic (PMID: 26619011).

The KIT A502_Y503dup alteration occurs in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation is found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and pediatric mastocytosis (PMID: 16954519, 17699867, 25239608, 16954519, 18955458, 21527588, 22350270, 19865100). Biological characterization of this variant in Ba/F3 and CHO cells demonstrated that this alteration is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 16954519, 17699867, 25239608, 18955458). In vitro studies of cells expressing A502_Y503dup suggest that this variant is sensitive to sunitinib but may be resistant to imatinib, as measured by protein activation and cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 25239608). In a Phase II clinical study in imatinib-resistant patients, 14 of 16 patients with this alteration achieved a clinical response to suntinib therapy (5 partial responses, 9 stable disease, 2 progressive disease) (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT P577_W582delinsPYD mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 23775962). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a phase II clinical study of metastatic melanoma patients treated with imatinib, one patient with this variant achieved a partial response after imatinib therapy (PMID: 23775962).

The KIT D820E alteration is located in the activation loop in exon 17 of KIT. This variant has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 15685537, 25886408) and thymic cancer (PMID: 19461405) samples. While this variant has not been functionally validated, this mutation has been seen as a secondary KIT mutation in patients with GIST who have acquired resistance to imatinib (PMID: 15685537) and as a primary mutation in a patient with thymic cancer who responded to sorafenib (PMID: 19461405).

The exon 15 KIT D737N mutation is located in the kinase domain. While this variant has not been functionally validated, structural and bioinformatics studies suggest that this variant may be activating and may be oncogenic (PMID: 26863566).

The KIT Y568_L576delinsVN mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II study in patients with imatinib-resistant GIST, one patient with KIT Y568_L576delinsVN in combination with a KIT V654A mutation was found to be sensitive to sunitinib treatment (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT T417_D419delinsI mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 8 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 15790786). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 hematopoietic cells determined that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation, transformation, and cell viability assays (PMID: 15790786). In vitro studies of cells expressing KIT T417_D419delinsI suggest that this mutation is sensitive to treatment with imatinib, as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 15790786).

The KIT K509I mutation occurs in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation is found in pediatric mastocytosis (PMID: 19865100). Expression of this variant in COS cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein phosphorylation compared to wildtype KIT (PMID: 19865100).

The KIT R634W alteration is located in the kinase domain in exon 13 of the protein. This mutation has been found in hemaopoietic malignancies (PMID: 15790786). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation and transformation assays (PMID: 15790786). In vitro studies suggest that this mutation is moderately sensitive to treatment with imatinib, as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 15790786).

The KIT R796G mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. Expression of this mutation in HEK293T cells demonstrated that it is an inactivating mutation, as measured by abolished KIT protein phosphorylation and abolished downstream signaling (PMID: 20824047).

The KIT M552_K558del alteration is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 25239608). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with GIST harboring KIT M552_K558del had a partial response to imatinib but later progressed and failed further treatment with imatinib, sunitinib, sorafenib, regorafenib, pazopanib and ponitinib (PMID: 25239608).

The KIT X550_splice alteration is located in the juxtamembrane cytoplasmic domain of the KIT protein encoded by exon 11. This alteration, similar to other alterations in KIT exon 11, has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) (PMID: 15507676, 15824741, 12181401, 15451219, 16098458, 18235121). In silico studies have demonstrated that this alteration is likely activating, as it affects two highly-conserved exonic splicing enhancers (ESEs) and is predicted to disrupt important autoinhibitory interactions, which can lead to oncogenesis through the constitutive activation of KIT (PMID: 15824741). Approximately 90% of patients with GISTs harboring KIT exon 11 alterations derive clinical benefit from treatment with imatinib (PMID: 12181401, 15451219, 16098458, 18235121).

The KIT D816G mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 25239608). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that KIT D816G is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 25239608). In vitro studies of cell lines expressing KIT D816F suggest that this mutation is resistant to treatment with imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib and ponatinib as evidenced by cell viability and pathway activation studies (PMID: 25239608).

The KIT D52N mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in myeloproliferative disorders (MPD) (PMID: 9168438). Peripheral blood and bone marrow of patients with KIT D52N mutant MPD had higher baseline proliferation in the absence of stimulation with stem cell factor (SCF) than blood and bone marrow from patients without KIT mutations, suggesting that this mutation may be activating (PMID: 9168438). However, the lack of data in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors suggests that the mutation's effect is inconclusive.

The KIT T847M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in T-cell lymphoma-leukemia and melanoma (PMID: 26437031, 23633454). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with primary penile melanoma harboring KIT T847M and KIT L576P was treated with imatinib and demonstrated complete remission with a progression-free survival of six months (PMID: 33283249).

The KIT V569_L576del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16551858). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in clinical studies of GIST, two patients with GIST harboring KIT V569_L576del responded to imatinib therapy (PMID: 16551858, 15930355).

The KIT P551_M552del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) samples (PMID: 18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a phase II clinical study of gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) patients who were resistant to imatinib, one patient with a KIT P551_M552del mutation achieved stable disease in response to sunitinib therapy (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT P551_V555del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutant has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 9438854). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells determined that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as determined by pathway activation, factor-independent proliferation, and tumor formation (PMID: 9438854).

The KIT E554_K558del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 15930355). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II study of imatinib in unresectable GIST, two patients whose tumors harbored the KIT E554_K558del mutation had partial response to treatment with imatinib before acquiring secondary resistance (PMID: 16954519). In a separate study, one patient with this mutation in combination with a V654A mutation had stable disease for more than six months upon treatment with sunitinib (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT W557_V560del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors and melanoma (PMID: 18955458, 23775962). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II trial in melanoma, a patient with KIT W557_V560del had stable disease in response to imatinib therapy (PMID: 23775962).

The KIT K550_V555delinsI mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 9438854). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells determined that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as determined by pathway activation, factor-independent proliferation, and tumor formation (PMID: 9438854).

The KIT S709F mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 14 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16551858). While this variant has not been functionally validated, KIT S709F was identified as a secondary KIT mutation in a patient with GIST who developed resistance to imatinib therapy (PMID: 16551858).

The KIT N463S mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 21642685). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II study of imatinib in advanced melanoma, one patient with this alteration had progressive disease on imatinib therapy (PMID: 21642685).

The KIT V559C mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 21642685, 25695690). While this variant has not been functionally validated, another amino acid substitution at this position (V559D) has been shown to be gain-of-function and oncogenic (PMID: 9438854), and in silico modeling predicts the V559C mutation to be gain-of-function (PMID: 15897563). Several patients with melanoma harboring the KIT V559C mutation responded to treatment with tyrosine kinase inhibitors targeting KIT, including imatinib and nilotinib (PMID: 21642685, 25695690).

The KIT K550_K558del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 9438854). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells determined that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as determined by pathway activation, factor-independent proliferation, and tumor formation (PMID: 9438854). In a Phase II study of imatinib in unresectable GIST, three patients whose tumors harbored the KIT K550_K558del mutation had partial response to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 16954519).

The KIT V560G mutation is found in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation is found in metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 14645423), hematopoietic malignancies (PMID: 15790786), and mast cell disorders (PMID: 16397263, 16434489). Biological characterization of this mutation in CHO, Ba/F3 hematopoietic, and mast cells have demonstrated that this mutation is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by enhanced pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 14645423, 15790786, 16397263, 16434489). Mast cells expressing this variant were found to be sensitive to imatinib and dasatinib treatment, as demonstrated by inhibition of pathway activation (PMID: 16397263, 16434489). In a Phase II study of imatinib in unresectable GIST, one patient whose tumor harbored the KIT V560G mutation had partial response to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 16954519).

The KIT D816I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 16956837). In vitro studies with COS, Ba/F3, TF1 and EML cells expressing KIT D816I demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased GSK3B phosphorylation, increased transformation of cells and activation of the STAT pathways compared to wildtype (PMID: 19865100, 20484085).

The KIT C443Y mutation occurs in the extracellular domain in exon 8 of the protein. This mutation is found in pediatric mastocytosis (PMID: 19865100). Expression of this variant in COS cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein phosphorylation compared to wildtype KIT (PMID: 19865100).

The KIT E490K mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation has been found in thymic carcinoma (PMID: 22357254). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with thymic carcinoma harboring the KIT E490K mutation was sensitive to imatinib treatment (PMID: 22357254).

The KIT K558_E562del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 25735500). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with a GIST harboring the KIT K558_E562del mutation had a partial response to imatinib treatment before developing a secondary KIT mutation and acquired resistance (PMID: 25735500).

The KIT D419del mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 8 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in mastocytosis and gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16143141, 23599150). Expression of KIT D419del in COS-7 cells resulted in increased KIT basal phosphorylation compared to wildtype cells (PMID: 16143141). Additionally, cells expressing this mutant exhibited sensitivity to imatinib in vitro as evidenced by decreased protein phosphorylation upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 16143141). A single patient with a GIST harboring KIT D419del had no evidence of disease after surgical resection of the tumor and 24 months of adjuvant imatinib treatment (PMID: 23599150).

The KIT V559A mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and melanoma (PMID: 16908931, 15897563, 19812602, 26424760). While this variant has not been functionally validated, another amino acid substitution at this position (V559D) has been shown to be gain-of-function and oncogenic (PMID: 9438854), and in silico modeling predicts the V559A mutation to be gain-of-function (PMID: 15897563). Patients with melanoma harboring the KIT V559A mutation have responded to treatment with imatinib or nilotinib (PMID: 19812602, 26424760).

The KIT M552_W557del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 16551858). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in clinical studies of GIST treated with imatinib, two patients with KIT M552_W557del had an initial response to imatinib before developing secondary progression (PMID: 16551858, 16954519).

The KIT D816H mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 25239608, 16954519, 18623623, 18955458), melanoma (PMID: 18980976, 25304235), leukemia (PMID: 16956837), and mast cell disorders (PMID: 16397263). Biological characterization of this mutation in various cell lines, including Ba/F3 cells, demonstrated that KIT D816H is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation, colony growth and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 25239608, 16397263, 25304235). In vitro studies of cell lines expressing KIT D816H suggest that this mutation is resistant to treatment with imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib and ponatinib as evidenced by cell viability and pathway activation studies (PMID: 25239608).

The KIT N822K mutation is located in the activation loop in exon 17 of KIT. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID:16954519, 22614970, 24490049, 26316776, 17699867, 23840364), melanoma (PMID: 21642685, 25695690) and leukemia (PMID: 21482694) samples. Biological characterization of hematopoietic, COS and GIST patient cells expressing the KIT N822K variant demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as evidenced by pathway activation (PMID: 21482694, 22614970, 17699867, 23840364), and expression of KIT N822K in Ba/F3 cells led to factor-independent growth (PMID: 17699867, 15790786). Laboratory experiments demonstrated that this mutation may be a putative acquired resistance mechanism to multikinase inhibitors imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib, but remains sensitizing to ponatinib (PMID: 25239608). Consistent with this data, KIT N822K is a common secondary KIT mutation associated with acquired resistance to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (PMID: 22614970). Patients with GIST harboring KIT N822K mutations progressed on imatinib and sunitinib, but derived clinical benefit from regorafenib (PMID: 22614970).

The KIT exon 11 Q575_P585dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation is found recurrently in gastrointestinal stromal tumor patient samples and comprises a hotspot, suggesting it is likely oncogenic (PMID: 26619011).

The KIT exon 17 D820Y hotspot mutation occurs in the KIT activation loop and has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), virtually always arising as a secondary resistance mechanism post-treatment with GIST first-line therapies imatinib or sunitinib (PMID: 14977822, 15930355, 16551858, 18623623, 18955458, 22614970, 17699867, 25239608). While cell line experiments with KIT D820Y expressed alone did not demonstrate that this mutation transformed cells (PMID: 17699867), D820Y confers resistance to imatinib/sunitinib when coincident with a primary, activating and imatinib/sunitinib-sensitizing KIT mutation (PMID: 23840364, 25239608). Additionally, cell line studies demonstrate that multi-tyrosine kinase inhibitors nilotinib, dasatinib and sorafenib have inhibition activity in cells co-expressing KIT D820Y with KIT V599D (PMID: 17699867). Patients with GIST harboring KIT D820Y mutations typically present after having progressed on imatinib or sunitinib, but have derived clinical benefit from GIST third-line regorafenib therapy (PMID: 22614970).

The KIT V559I mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in mastocytosis (PMID: 17259998). Expression of this variant in HEK293 cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased KIT phosphorylation compared to wildtype KIT (PMID: 17259998). In vitro studies of KIT V559I suggest that this variant is resistant to imatinib as measured by sustained protein phosphorylation upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 17259998).

The KIT K558N mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of KIT. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) and melanoma (PMID: 18980976). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with melanoma harboring KIT K558N responded to imatinib therapy, as evidenced by radiographic response (PMID: 18980976).

The KIT W557R mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the KIT protein (PMID: 14977822, 22357254). This mutation has been recurrently observed in GIST, melanoma and thymic cancers (PMID: 20859122, 20859122, 18980976, 21325067, 19018266, 21906875, 21953054). Mutations and deletions within the juxtamembrane region have been shown to disrupt its autoinhibitory, kinase domain-binding function, thereby allowing constitutive activation of KIT (PMID: 25079768, 10224103). Germline KIT W557R mutations predispose patients to gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 14977822). GISTs and thymic cancers harboring the W557R mutation are sensitive to imatinib treatment (PMID: 22357254, 12888812), however imatinib sensitivity may be tumor etiology specific as a melanoma patient with the W557R mutation did not respond to imatinib (PMID: 21642685).

The KIT exon 11 Y578_D579dup mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation is found recurrently in gastrointestinal stromal tumor patient samples and comprises a hotspot, suggesting it is likely oncogenic (PMID: 26619011).

The KIT W557G mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of KIT. This alteration has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 15342366). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating as measured by constitutive protein activation in cells expressing the mutation, and is sensitive to imatinib treatment (PMID: 23567324). A patient with a GIST harboring the KIT W557G mutation had stable disease in response to imatinib treatment (PMID: 15342366).

The KIT Y418_D419del mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 8 of the protein. This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 22825855, 19603346), familial gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and mastocytosis (PMID: 16143141). Cell line experiments indicate that this mutation is activating, as evidenced by ligand-independent constitutive protein activation (PMID: 16143141). In vitro experiments demonstrated that, similar to wildtype KIT, KIT Y418_D419del maintains a dose-dependent sensitivity to imatinib, but requires higher drug concentrations to achieve the same level of KIT inhibition (PMID: 16143141).

The KIT Y570H mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 21642685). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with melanoma harboring KIT Y570H had stable disease in response to imatinib therapy (PMID: 21642685).

The KIT V559D mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 17699867, 9438854, 15930355, 16954519, 18955458, 25605837), melanoma (PMID: 18980976, 17372901) and hematopoietic malignancy (PMID: 15790786) samples. Biological characterization of Ba/F3 and 293T cell lines expressing this variant demonstrated that this mutation is activating and promotes cell growth, as evidenced by pathway activation and tumor growth in vivo (PMID: 9438854, 15790786, 17699867). Cells transformed with KIT V559D alone or in combination with KIT D820Y are sensitive to imatinib, dasatinib, sorafenib and nilotinib in vitro as measured by cell growth and apoptosis (PMID: 17372901, 17699867).

The KIT P573_D579del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 9438854) and mast cell neoplasms (PMID: 12569358). Biological characterization of this variant in a mastocytoma cell line demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as determined by pathway activation (PMID: 9438854). In vitro studies of cells expressing this variant suggest that KIT P573_D579del is sensitive to imatinib treatment, as measured by inhibition of kinase activity (PMID: 12569358).

The KIT I563_L576del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 15930355). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a study of 31 GIST patients, one patient with a GIST harboring this alteration responded to imatinib therapy (PMID: 15930355).

The KIT exon 11 Y578_D579insEQQLPY mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation is found recurrently in gastrointestinal stromal tumor patient samples and comprises a hotspot, suggesting it is likely oncogenic (PMID: 26619011).

The KIT N822Y mutation is located in the kinase loop in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in familial gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 18724244). While this variant has not been functionally validated, another amino acid substitution at this position (N822I) has been shown to be gain-of-function and oncogenic (PMID: 21689725). Two patients with GIST harboring the KIT N822Y mutation had complete and partial response, respectively, to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 18724244).

The KIT V559G mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 23348204). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 hematopoietic cells demonstrated that this variant is activating, promotes factor-independent growth, and confers sensitivity to imatinib in vitro (PMID: 12569358). A patient with a GIST harboring the KIT V559G mutation responded to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 23348204).

The KIT T574_R588delinsL mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II study of imatinib-resistant GIST, one patient with KIT T574_R588delinsL in combination with a secondary KIT alteration had a clinical response to sunitinib therapy (PMID: 18955458).

This KIT deletion lies in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation is found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 15365079). Mutations and deletions within this exon result in gain of function and increased downstream signaling through disruption of the autoinhibitory, kinase domain-binding activity of the juxtamembrane domain (PMID: 17372901, 25079768). Approximately 90% of patients bearing gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) harboring KIT exon 11 alterations derive clinical benefit from treatment with imatinib (NCCN Guidelines Soft Tissue Sarcoma Version 2.2016, PMID: 12181401, 15451219, 16098458, 18235121). Patients with melanoma harboring exon 11 deletions have had clinical benefit with nilotinib treatment (PMID: 26424760).

The KIT L783V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 28481359). Although not functionally characterized per se, KIT L783V was identified as an acquired secondary mutation in a patient with duodenal gastrointestinal stromal tumors treated with imatinib (PMID: 36267752).

The KIT E554_V559del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 18980976). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a clinical study of melanoma patients treated with imatinib, one patient with this alteration had a clinical benefit from imatinib treatment (PMID: 18980976).

The KIT N655K mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 13 of KIT. This mutation is found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 17489795). Expression of this variant in 293T cells demonstrated that it is likely activating, as shown by protein activation and cellular proliferation (PMID: 17489795). In vitro studies of cells expressing KIT N655K suggest that this variant is sensitive to imatinib as measured by decreased protein activation and decreased cell growth upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 17489795). Co-expression of this mutation with the KIT D816V mutation in BaF3 cells demonstrated that it reduces sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor midostaurin but retains sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor avapritinib compared to expression of D816V alone (PMID: 31270078).

The KIT L576P mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 15930355, 16954519, 18955458, 25605837), melanoma (PMID: 18980976, 21642685, 23775962, 25695690, 26264378, 19671763, 26424760) and thymic cancer samples (PMID: 22357254). Biological characterization of Ba/F3 cells expressing KIT L576P demonstrated that this alteration is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation (PMID: 17372901, 19671763). Cells expressing KIT L576P have in vitro sensitivity to dasatinib, though in vitro sensitivity to imatinib varies by cell lineage (PMID: 17372901, 19671763). In multiple studies, patients with melanoma harboring KIT L576P derived clinical benefit from imatinib treatment or nilotinib treatment (PMID: 18980976, 25695690, 22068222, 26424760). Additionally, multiple patients with GIST harboring KIT L576P mutations had stable disease in response to sunitinib (PMID: 18955458)
The KIT G812V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is inactivating (PMID: 36166736).

The KIT N822I mutation is located in the activation loop in exon 17 of KIT. This mutation has been identified in familial mastocytosis (PMID: 21689725). Expression of this variant in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 21689725). In vitro studies of cells expressing KIT N822I suggest that it is sensitive to dasatinib but not imatinib treatment as evidenced by decreased protein activation and decreased cell proliferation upon treatment with dasatinib but not imatinib (PMID: 21689725).

The KIT D60N mutation occurs in the extracellular domain in exon 1 of the protein (PMID: 16226710). Mice engineered to harbor the gain-of-function KIT-D60N mutation exhibited myeloid defects associated with myeloproliferation (PMID: 24211109). Biological characterization of the D60N mutant KIT demonstrated that this mutant is incompletely N-glycosylated which prevents receptor dimerization and this is associated with decreased AKT and ERK signaling, but conversely upregulated JAK2 signaling (PMID: 24211109).

The KIT V559_V560del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16551858) and hematopoietic malignancies (PMID: 15790786). Biological characterization of Ba/F3 hematopoietic cells expressing this variant demonstrated that this mutation is activating and promotes growth, as determined by pathway activation and factor-independent growth (PMID: 15790786). In vitro studies have suggested that this mutation is sensitive to imatinib, as evidenced by pathway activation and cell viability (PMID: 15790786). In a phase II study of 147 patients with advanced, unresectable GIST treated with imatinib, one individual with KIT V559_V560del responded to imatinib before acquiring secondary resistance (PMID: 16954519).

The KIT A504_Y505ins mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16551858). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a clinical study of 32 GIST patients, six patients with KIT A504_Y505ins mutation had clinical benefit from treatment with imatinib, though five of the six patients developed secondary progression (PMID: 16551858). One patient with KIT A504_Y505ins mutation in the same study had progressive disease outright (PMID: 16551858).

The KIT V559del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and melanoma (PMID: 10485475, 23993026). Expression of this mutation in COS-1 fibroblast cells demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as determined by enhanced pathway activation (PMID: 15236194, 16751810). KIT V559del is sensitive to imatinib as shown by decreased activation of downstream effectors in vitro (PMID: 15236194, 16751810).

The KIT R804W mutation is located in the activation loop in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and colorectal cancer (PMID: 30205045, 31660073). Although not functionally characterized per se, in silico analysis suggests that the mutation has lower binding affinity to imatinib compared to wildtype (PMID: 20140688).

The KIT exon 13 V654 mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 23840364, 18623623, 16751810, 16954519) and melanoma (PMID: 21642685). Biological characterization of KIT V654A in COS-1 and CHO cells demonstrated that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation (PMID: 23840364, 16751810, 16954519). In preclinical studies, COS-1 cell lines expressing this variant were insensitive to imatinib but sensitive to sunitinib and nilotinib, as determined by inhibition of pathway activation (PMID: 23840364). Co-expression of this mutation with the KIT D816V mutation in BaF3 cells demonstrated reduced sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor midostaurin compared to expression of D816V alone, but retains sensitivity to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor avapritinib that is comparable to D816V alone (PMID: 31270078). In a Phase II clinical study of patients with metastatic, imatinib-resistant gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs), twelve patients with tumors harboring the KIT V654A mutation were sensitive to sunitinib therapy, including two with partial responses and ten with stable disease (PMID: 18955458), though all patients in this study had secondary KIT alterations and had previously exhausted imatinib therapy.

The KIT T417_D419delinsRG mutation is located in the extracellular domain in exon 8 of the protein. This variant has been identified in acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 15790786). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 hematopoietic cells determined that this variant is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation, transformation, and cell viability assays (PMID: 15790786). In vitro studies of cells expressing T417_D419delinsRG suggest that this mutation is sensitive to treatment with imatinib, as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 15790786).

The KIT H697Y mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 14 of KIT. This mutation has been found in thymic cancer (PMID: 19861435). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that this variant is activating, as measured by factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 19861435). In vitro studies suggest that KIT H697Y is more sensitive to sunitinib than imatinib, as measured by decreased cell proliferation (PMID: 19861435).

The KIT Y578C mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 23567324). Biological characterization of cancer cells engineered to express KIT Y578C demonstrated that it is activating as measured by constitutive protein activation, and is sensitive to imatinib in a dose-dependent manner (PMID: 23567324). In a clinical case report, one patient with GIST harboring dual W557G and Y578C mutations achieved a complete response following treatment with imatinib. Both mutants have been biologically characterized to be associated with sensitivity to imatinib, as evidenced by pathway inhibition upon drug treatment (PMID: 23567324)

The KIT D579del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of KIT. This mutation has been found in thymic cancer and gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 24419427,18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with poorly differentiated thymic cancer harboring KIT D579del achieved a durable response on imatinib therapy, while a patient with GIST harboring KIT D579del achieved stable disease on sunitinib therapy (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT D820G mutation occurs in the activation loop in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) patient samples (PMID: 23840364, 16551858, 16954519, 18623623, 18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, this mutation has been seen as a secondary KIT mutation in patients with GIST who have acquired resistance to imatinib (PMID: 18955458, 18623623, 16954519, 16551858). Expression of this mutation alone in COS-1 cells resulted in sensitivity to sunitinib, as evidenced by pathway activation studies (PMID: 23840364), while expression with other KIT activating mutations also resulted in sensitivity to sorafenib, regorafenib, dasatinib, nilotinib and ponatinib (PMID: 23840364, PMID: 25239608). In a Phase II clinical study in patients resistant to imatinib, one patient with this alteration (in combination with the 502_503AYins mutation) achieved a clinical response to sunitinib (PMID: 18955458), while in another study, a patient with this mutation in combination with an exon 11 insertion mutation achieved a clinical response to nilotinib (PMID: 21456006)

The KIT C809G mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16954519, 18955458, 17139461). While this variant has not been functionally validated, KIT C809G was identified as a secondary KIT mutation in patients with GIST who developed resistance to imatinib therapy (PMID: 16954519, 18955458, 17139461). Cell lines expressing this mutation are resistant to imatinib, as measured by persistent protein activation in the presence of imatinib treatment (PMID: 16954519).

The KIT D572A mutation occurs in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation is found in pediatric mastocytosis (PMID: 19865100). Expression of this variant in COS cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein phosphorylation compared to wildtype KIT (PMID: 19865100).

The KIT A829P mutation is located in the activation loop in exon 18 of KIT. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) and melanoma (PMID: 25239608, 18955458, 18623623, 18980976, 21642685) samples. While this variant has not been functionally validated, the KIT A829P alteration confers resistance to imatinib in vitro when expressed with a primary, activating KIT mutation (PMID: 18955458, 25239608). Several patients with GISTs harboring KIT A829P mutations progressed upon treatment with imatinib (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT R634Q mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 13 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and colorectal cancer (PMID:  30205045, 26517354). Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with metastatic melanoma harboring KIT R634Q was treated with ripretinib and demonstrated progressive disease (PMID: 35753087).

The KIT V555_L576del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 23840364). Biological characterization of this variant in COS-1 cells demonstrated that the mutation is activating, as evidenced by pathway activation (PMID: 23840364). In vitro studies of cell lines expressing KIT V555_L576del suggest that this mutation is sensitive to imatinib, sunitinib and nilotinib as measured by kinase inhibition (PMID: 23840364).

The KIT P838L mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 21642685). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a phase II clinical study, one patient with a melanoma harboring the KIT P838L mutation achieved stable disease in response to imatinib therapy (PMID: 21642685).

The KIT K558_V559del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16954519, 18955458). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a clinical study of 147 GIST patients with advanced disease treated with imatinib, two patients with this alteration had partial responses to imatinib before aquiring secondary resistance (PMID: 16954519, 18955458).

The KIT G961S mutation is located in the C-terminal region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in ovarian cancer (PMID: 21720365). Although not functionally characterized per se, KIT G961S was identified as an acquired secondary mutation in a patient with rectal cancer treated with regorafenib (PMID: 28915719).

The KIT D816V mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) (PMID: 17545544, 14645423), mastocytosis (PMID: 7479840, 15790786, 26002753, 23659595, 19193436, 16779792, 15972446, 16397263, 16434489, 23416972, 12569358), and leukemia (PMID: 22301675, 15725473, 16254134) samples. Biological characterization of this variant in Ba/F3, 293T, CHO, and mastocytoma cells demonstrated that this alteration is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation, colony formation, and xenograft assays (PMID: 15790786, 16397263, 16434489, 23416972, 12569358). In vitro studies of cell lines expressing KIT D816V suggest that this mutation is resistant to treatment with imatinib as evidenced by cell viability and pathway activation studies (PMID: 15790786, 12569358). In several studies, patients with KIT D816V mutations progressed on imatinib treatment, while some patients experienced clinical benefit from nilotinib treatment (PMID: 15725473, 26002753). The KIT D816V mutation in combination with serum b2-microglobulin levels and pathogenic variants in ASXL1, RUNX1, and/or DNMT3A predicts progression free survival among patients with indolent systemic mastocytosis (PMID: 31151985).

The KIT exon 11 P573Q mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally characterized, this mutation is found recurrently in gastrointestinal stromal tumor patient samples and comprises a hotspot, suggesting it is likely oncogenic (PMID: 26619011).

The KIT S501_A502dup alteration occurs in the extracellular domain in exon 9 of the protein. This mutation is found in mast cell leukemia (PMID: 22324351). Expression of this variant in COS cells demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein phosphorylation in the absence of ligand (PMID: 22324351). A patient whose mast cell leukemia harbored a KIT S501_A502dup alteration derived clinical benefit from treatment with the KIT tyrosine kinase inhibitor masitinib (PMID: 22324351)

The KIT K558delinsNP mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of KIT. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) samples (PMID: 16954519, 11526490, 25239608). Biological characterization of Ba/F3 cell lines expressing KIT K558delinsNP demonstrated that this mutation is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 25239608). In vitro studies of cells expressing KIT K558delinsNP suggest that this variant is sensitive to imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib and ponatinib, as evidenced by decreased protein activation and decreased cell proliferation (PMID: 11526490, 25239608). A patient with GIST harboring the KIT K558delinsNP mutation had stable disease persistent for greater than six months upon treatment with sunitinib (PMID: 18955458).

The KIT I653T mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 13 of KIT. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 21642685). While this variant has not been functionally validated, a patient with melanoma harboring KIT I653T had stable disease in response to imatinib therapy (PMID: 21642685).

The KIT N822H mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 14645423, 16954519, 18955458). Biological characterization of this variant in CHO cells demonstrated that the mutation is activating, as evidenced by pathway activation (PMID: 14645423). In vitro studies have suggested that this mutation is sensitive to treatment with imatinib as measured by decreased kinase activity upon imatinib treatment (PMID: 14645423).

The KIT D816F mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 17 of the protein. This mutation has been found in hematological malignancies (PMID: 16397263). Biological characterization of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that KIT D816F is activating and promotes growth, as evidenced by pathway activation and factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 16397263). In vitro studies of cell lines expressing KIT D816F suggest that this mutation is resistant to imatinib but sensitive to dasatinib treatment as evidenced by cell viability and pathway activation studies (PMID: 16397263).

The KIT Y553_K558del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 16954519). While this variant has not been functionally validated, in a Phase II study of 147 GIST patients treated with imatinib, one patient with KIT Y553_K558del had an initial response to imatinib before acquiring a secondary KIT mutation and developing secondary progression (PMID: 16954519).

The KIT Q556_K558del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 19369884). While this variant has not been functionally validated, most exon 11 deletions have been shown to be gain-of-function and oncogenic (PMID: 17372901, 25079768). A patient with GIST harboring a KIT Q556_K558del mutation had a partial response to imatinib before later developing resistance (PMID: 19369884).

The KIT L576del mutation is located in the juxtamembrane domain in exon 11 of the protein. This mutation has been found in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) (PMID: 12717247) and melanoma (PMID: 19802003). Expression of this mutant in melan-A cells demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as shown by increased protein activation and downstream pathway activation (PMID: 19802003). In vitro studies have suggested that KIT L576del is likely oncogenic, as it is able to induce colony formation of melan-A cells in the presence of HIF-1alpha (PMID: 19802003).

The KMT2D C1430R mutation lies in the PHD5 domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation as recombinant protein demonstrated it is inactivating, as measured by decreased binding ability of the PHD domain and decreased nucleosomal methylation activity compared to wildtype KMT2D (PMID: 23249737).

The KMT2D C1471Y mutation lies in the PHD5 domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation as recombinant protein demonstrated it is inactivating, as measured by decreased binding ability of the PHD domain and decreased nucleosomal methylation activity compared to wildtype KMT2D (PMID: 23249737).

Truncating mutations are the most common cancer-associated mutations of KMT2D and lead to several forms of C-terminally truncated proteins causing mRNA degradation and nonsense-mediated decay (PMID: 24633898). These alterations ablate the SET domain of KMT2D leading to global loss of methyltransferase activity and dysregulation of gene expression (PMID: 24240169). Conditional deletion of KMT2D in mice result in enhanced B cell proliferation and increases tumor development in a BCL2 overexpression model (PMID: 26366712).

KMT2D deletions result in mRNA degradation and nonsense-mediated decay of KMT2D (PMID: 24633898). These alterations commonly disrupt the SET domain of KMT2D leading to global loss of methyltransferase activity and dysregulation of gene expression (PMID: 24240169). Conditional deletion of KMT2D in mice result in enhanced B-cell proliferation and increases tumor development in a BCL2 overexpression model (PMID: 26366712).

The KMT2D R5432W mutation is located in the SET domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 32187361). In silico analysis of KMT2D R5432W suggests that the mutation is inactivating and deleterious (PMID: 31727177).

The KMT2D Y5426A mutation lies in the SET domain of the protein. While this mutation alone has not been characterized, expression of Y5426A in combination with the KMT2D Y5512A mutation in a human fibroblast cell line demonstrated these mutations are inactivating, as measured by a reduced ability to catalyze mono-, di- and trimethylated H3K4 compared to wildtype KMT2D (PMID: 28013028).

The KRAS E63K mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in leukemia and intestinal cancer (PMID: 25425670, 25207766, 18022911, 22773565). Expression of this mutation in a fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation and migration and xenograft tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 1554412, 31289513).

The KMT2D Y5512A mutation lies in the SET domain of the protein. While this mutation alone has not been characterized, expression of Y5512A in combination with the KMT2D Y5426A mutation in a human fibroblast cell line demonstrated these mutations are inactivating, as measured by a reduced ability to catalyze mono-, di- and trimethylated H3K4 compared to wildtype KMT2D (PMID: 28013028).

The KRAS G12C mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and colorectal cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in lung and breast cancer cell lines and mouse models demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation, cell proliferation, colony formation and in vivo tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25705018, 26841430, 16051643, 32792368). In vitro studies of cells expressing the KRAS G12C mutation demonstrate that it is sensitive to several targeted therapies designed specifically for this allele, including ARS853 (PMID: 26841430, 24256730). In a phase I clinical trial of the KRAS G12C inhibitor AMG510 in which thirteen patients with non-small cell lung cancer harboring this mutation were given the target drug dose, 100% of patients responded, with seven patients having partial response and six patients having stable disease (Abstract: Fakih et al. Abstract# 3003, ASCO 2019. https://meetinglibrary.asco.org/record/172411/abstract). KRAS G12C has been identified as an acquired resistance mutation in two patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer following a durable response to osimertinib (PMID: 38096473).

The KRAS R164Q mutation is located in the Switch III region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal and endometrial cancer (PMID: 20147967). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in a fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in pathway activation or colony formation compared to wildtype. However, gene expression profiling of the cells did demonstrate a distinct gene expression signature compared to wildtype and expression of this mutation in fibroblast cell lines along with the KRAS G12V mutation demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein clustering and increased cell proliferation and colony formation compared to KRAS G12V alone (PMID: 20147967, 26274561). Additionally, in vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS R164Q demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS S65N mutation is located in the Switch II region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in thyroid cancer (PMID: 24798740). Expression of this mutation in human embryonic kidney and thyroid cancer cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 8626650, 24798740).

The KRAS Q61E mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been identified in glioma and colorectal cancer (PMID: 9107428, 21122130). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS Q61E demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS A146T mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in leukemia and in colorectal and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in various cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein stability, increased protein activation and increased pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19075190, 20147967, 20570890, 2403644, 34117033). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to BRAF inhibition in lymphoid cells as measured by decreased pathway activation in the presence of the drug, but is sensitive to the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib (PMID: 30341394). A patient with hairy cell leukemia acquired a KRAS G12D mutation following relapse on the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib but was successfully treated with the cobimetinib for at least 12 months (PMID: 30341394).

The KRAS K117R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and acute lymphoblastic B-cell leukemia (PMID: 28120820, 27655895). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS K117R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS N116S mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS N116S demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS V14I mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation was found as a germline mutation in Noonan syndrome (PMID: 16474405). Expression of this mutation in a simian cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation compared to wildtype, while expression of this mutation in mouse models results in the development of a disorder comparable to Noonan Syndrome (PMID: 16474405, 20949621, 34117033).

The KRAS Q131H mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS Q131H demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by MAPK signaling activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G60R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in leukemia (PMID: 24030381). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a murine cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by decreased binding to negative regulatory proteins and increased pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621).

The KRAS A146P mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS A146P demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G13A mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and endometrioid carcinoma (PMID: 17663506, 16256179). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS G13A demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS Q22R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation was found as a germline mutation in Noonan syndrome (PMID: 21263000). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a simian cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621).

The KRAS I21L mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS I21L demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS F28L mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation was found as a germline mutation in Noonan or cardio-facio-cutaneous syndromes (PMID: 16474405). Expression of this mutation in mouse embryonic fibroblasts demonstrated that it is activating specifically in the context of NF1 loss as measured by increased in downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype, while expression of the KRAS F28L mutation alone, however, only modestly activated the protein and did not lead to downstream pathway activation (PMID: 25600866, 20949621).

The KRAS G13R mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS G13R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS K176del mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS K176del demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G13C mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung and colorectal cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein activation, modestly increased downstream signaling, increased colony formation, and resistance to apoptosis compared to wildtype (PMID: 21079152, 25705018).

The KRAS D119G mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in fibrolamellar carcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is activating (PMID: 35058622).

The KRAS T144I mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS T144I demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS A59E mutation is located in the GTP binding site of the protein. This mutation has been identified in plasma cell myeloma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 25302557). In vivo studies with KRAS+/LSL-A59E mice demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by autophosphorylation of the protein compared to wildtype (Abstract: Johnson et al. Abstract# 84, AACR 2021. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/81/13_Supplement/84/669649/Abstract-84-Characterization-of-oncogenic-KRAS-A59). Autophosphorylation of KRAS is suggested to promote colorectal cancer tumorigenesis through a MAPK-independent signaling pathway, which is consistent with in vivo studies of KRAS A59E demonstrating inhibition of KRAS-effector interactions with the MAPK, AKT and Hippo signaling pathway (Abstract: Johnson et al. Abstract# 84, AACR 2021. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/81/13_Supplement/84/669649/Abstract-84-Characterization-of-oncogenic-KRAS-A59).

The KRAS A18D mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in leukemia (PMID: 26648538, 23319568, 25207766). Expression of this mutation in a fibroblast cell line and in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased IL3-independent proliferation and colony-formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19490892).

The KRAS G60D mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS G60D demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033). One patient with colorectal cancer harboring this mutation demonstrated a partial response to the EGFR inhibitor cetuximab (PMID: 21632860).

The KRAS K117N mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma, colorectal and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in human embryonic kidney and fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20147967, 20570890).

The KRAS G60V mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia and acute myeloid leukemia (PMID: 24446311, 27288520). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS G60V demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

KRAS amplification results in overexpression of the protein. This mutation has been found in germ cell tumors and esophagogastric and ovarian cancer (cBioPortal, Zehir, A et al. Nature Medicine, 2017). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor crizotinib, EGFR inhibitors cetuximab or panitumumab, MET inhibitors PHA-665752 or JNJ38877605 and MEK inhibitors AZD6244 or GSK1120212 in patient-derived lung cancer cell line and xenograft models, colorectal cancer cell line models, MET-amplified cell line models and gastric cancer cell line models (PMID: 29808010, 30072474, 23404247, 20841479). Analyses of 475 patients with endometrial cancer demonstrated that KRAS amplification is associated with metastasis (PMID: 23099803).

The KRAS A11_G12insGA mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer. Expression of this mutation in a fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, increased colony formation and increased tumor growth in vivo compared to wildtype (PMID: 24642870).

The KRAS Y40A mutation is located in the Switch I region of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and decreased binding to negative regulatory proteins compared to wildtype (PMID: 26841430, 11333268).

The KRAS Q22E mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in Noonan syndrome (PMID: 17324647, 21263000). Expression of this mutation in a simian cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621).

The KRAS Q61K mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 26619011). This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and plasma cell myeloma (PMID: 19884549, 28234344). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS Q61K demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G12D mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung, colorectal, pancreatic and ovarian cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in cell lines and mouse models demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased downstream pathway activation, colony formation and in vivo tumor development across multiple lineages compared to wildtype (PMID: 20570890, 20147967, 11751631, 15093544,19296721,17349581, 32792368). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to BRAF inhibition in lymphoid cells as measured by decreased pathway activation in the presence of the drug, but is sensitive to the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib (PMID: 30341394). A patient with hairy cell leukemia acquired a KRAS G12D mutation following relapse on the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib but was successfully treated with the cobimetinib for at least twelve months (PMID: 30341394). Preclinical studies with xenograft mouse models expressing KRAS G12D demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with ASP3082 as measured by reduced tumor volume following treatment (Abstract: Nagashima et al. Abstract# 5735, AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/7_Supplement/5735/722276).

The KRAS P34R mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation was found as a germline mutation in Noonan syndrome (PMID: 16474405). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a simian cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by decreased binding to regulatory proteins and increased pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621). In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS P34R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G10dup is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation was found in a patient with childhood myeloid leukemia. Expression of this mutation in human and simian cells demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased colony formation and downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype and biochemical characterization showed that it was constitutively active (PMID: 8955068).

The KRAS E31K mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal cancer (PMID: 31681616). There is conflicting functional data on this mutation. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein GTPase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 20570890). However, structural analysis of this mutation demonstrated that it may be activating as measured by reduced binding to regulatory proteins (PMID: 16483931).

The KRAS Y64D mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrates that it is activating as measured by decreased binding to Ras-GAPs compared to wildtype (PMID: 30644389).

The KRAS R149G mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. While this mutation has not been functionally validated, molecular modeling predicts that this mutation is likely activating because it alters the KRAS structure (PMID: 25412182). A patient with histiocytic neoplasm harboring this mutation demonstrated a partial response (>50% regression) to the MEK1/2 inhibitor cobimetinib (PMID: 30867592).

The KRAS G13D mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in colorectal cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as shown by increased protein activation, downstream pathway activation, colony formation and in vivo tumor formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22722830, 26037647, 20147967, 32792368).

The KRAS G12V mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal, lung and pancreatic cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in cell lines and mouse models demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased pathway activation, colony formation and in vivo tumor formation across various lineages compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621, 20570890, 20147967, 20516123, 25359494, 12957286). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to BRAF inhibition in lymphoid cells as measured by decreased pathway activation in the presence of the drug, but is sensitive to the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib (PMID: 30341394). A patient with hairy cell leukemia acquired a KRAS G12D mutation following relapse on the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib but was successfully treated with the cobimetinib for at least twelve months (PMID: 30341394).

The KRAS Y64A mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrates that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and decreased binding to negative regulators compared to wildtype (PMID: 26841430, 12628188).

The KRAS T58I mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in leukemia and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 20949621). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to the BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors, imatinib and dasatinib, in BCR-ABL-expressing murine leukemia cells as measured by sustained proliferation in the presence of the drug. In a case study, one patient with chronic myeloid leukemia that acquired this mutation developed resistance to imatinib despite initially responding to the drug (PMID: 18509354).

The KRAS R68S mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS R68S demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G12T mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. In vitro studies using a Novellus FACT assay with Ba/F3 cells expressing KRAS G12T demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased MAPK signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 34117033).

The KRAS G12R mutation is located in the P-loop of the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung, colorectal, pancreatic and ovarian cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in colorectal cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased RAS-GTP levels, downstream pathway activation, and in vivo tumor growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 32792368). In vitro studies of cells expressing KRAS G12R suggest that this mutation is resistant to cetuximab (PMID: 22722830). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to BRAF inhibition in lymphoid cells as measured by decreased pathway activation in the presence of the drug, but is sensitive to the MEK inhibitor cobimetinib (PMID: 30341394). A patient with hairy cell leukemia acquired a KRAS G12D mutation following relapse on the BRAF inhibitor vemurafenib but was successfully treated with the cobimetinib for at least twelve months (PMID: 30341394).

The KRAS E62K mutation is located in the catalytic G-domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 25691825). Expression of this variant in human embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation compared to wildtype, as well as tumor formation in four of six implanted mice (PMID: 27147599).
