The NRAS Q61K mutation is located in the switch II region of the catalytic domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma and lung cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23515407, 19492075, 26619011). Expression of this mutation in primary murine melanocytes demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased downstream pathway activation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID:22718121), while knockdown of the endogenously expressed mutation in lung cancer cell lines resulted in decreased cell proliferation, decreased tumor volume in xenograft models and decreased pathway activation (PMID: 23515407). Structural analysis of the Q61 residue demonstrates that it is crucial for NRAS GTP hydrolyzing activity suggesting that any mutation at Q61 would render the protein constitutively active (PMID: 10574788, 20194776, 9219684). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation confers resistance to crizotinib and erlotinib in EGFR-mutant models, but is sensitive to the MEK1/2 inhibitors trametinib and selumetinib as measured by decreased cell viability and pathway activation in the presence of the drug (PMID: 23515407). A patient with BRAF V600E-mutant lung adenocarcinoma who acquired an NRAS Q61K mutation demonstrated resistance to treatment with the BRAF inhibitor dabrafenib and the MEK1/2 inhibitor trametinib (PMID:29631033). In a basket trial of refractory solid tumors treated with a single-agent MEK inhibitor, binimetinib, eight patients with codon 61 NRAS-mutated colorectal cancer (n = 5 patients with Q61K) had a significantly longer OS and PFS compared to sixteen patients with colorectal cancer harboring a mutation in codon 12/13 (PMID: 33637626).

This mutation has been identified in acute lymphoblastic B-cell leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 17344859). In vitro studies with PAX5-/- bone marrow cells expressing PAX5 V26G demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by partial rescue of protein function with minimally reduced BP-1 expression compared to wildtype (Abstract: Nakitandwe et al. Abstract# 10, Blood 2010. https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/116/21/10/64473/Acute-Lymphoblastic-Leukemia-Associated-PAX5).

Truncating mutations in PAX5 occur throughout the gene and lead to loss of PAX5 function. These mutations have been identified in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 21549623, 17344859). In vivo studies with PAX5-haploinsufficient mice demonstrate loss of PAX5 is inactivating as measured by increased penetrance and reduced latency of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 25855603).

PAX5 amplification typically results in the overexpression of the protein. Amplification of PAX5 has been identified in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) and is associated with poor prognosis (PMID: 29296789). PAX5 overexpression in S-type neuroblastoma cells demonstrated PAX5 amplification is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation, anchorage-independent growth and tumor formation in vivo (PMID: 15155532). Intragenic amplification of PAX5 was identified as a recurrent alteration in patients with B-ALL, resulting in multiple additional copies of numerous exons in the 5' end of PAX5 (PMID: 23538749, 30643249, 35245931).

PAX5 deletion mutations result in the loss of the protein. These mutations have been identified in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 21549623, 17344859). In vivo studies with PAX5-haploinsufficient mice demonstrate loss of PAX5 is inactivating as measured by increased penetrance and reduced latency of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 25855603).

PBRM1 deletion is associated with reduced protein expression and function and typically co-occurs with loss of the VHL protein, another important gene in renal cell carcinoma pathogenesis (PMID: 23867514). These alterations have been shown to disrupt the activity of the switching defective/sucrose non-fermenting (SWI/SNF) histone remodeling complex (PMID: 21248752). In addition, PBRM1 truncating mutations can no longer bind and remodel the p21 locus leading to cell cycle defects and aberrant cell proliferation (PMID: 18339845). Loss of PBRM1 correlates with advanced tumor progression, low differentiation grade and poor prognosis (PMID: 22949125). Deletion of PBRM1 and VHL in the kidney synergize to form clear cell tumors (PMID: 28329682).

PAX5-ELN rearrangements result from the chromosomal translocation t(7;9)(q11;p13). This fusion protein has been identified in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) (PMID: 30257940). In vivo studies with mouse models expressing PAX5-ELN demonstrate that the fusion is inactivating as measured by dysregulated transcriptional regulation leading to pro B-cell expansion and the development of B-ALL compared to wildtype (PMID: 30257940).

The PAX5 P80R mutation is located in the DNA binding domain of the protein. In vivo studies with PAX5-deficient transgenic mice expressing PAX5 P80R demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by aberrant differentiation of B-cells and development of B-lineage leukemia compared to wildtype (PMID: 30643249).

Abstract# 10, ASH 2010. https://ashpublications.org/blood/article/116/21/10/64473/Acute-Lymphoblastic-Leukemia-Associated-PAX5).

The PBRM1 D1308Gfs* mutation (also cited as D1333Gfs*) is located in the high mobility group domain of the protein. This mutation was identified in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (PMID: 25911086). Somatic studies of this mutation demonstrated PBRM1 D1308Gfs* is inactivating as measured by loss of PBRM1 expression (PMID: 25911086).

The PDGFRA W559_R560del mutation occurs in the protein's juxtamembrane domain. This mutation has been identified in a gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) patient sample (PMID: 26396737). While this mutation has not yet been functionally validated, a patient with the W559_R560del mutation achieved clinical responses to imatinib and sunitinib therapy (PMID: 26396737).

Truncating mutations in PBRM1 causes reduced protein function, leading to the disruption of several important signaling programs. These alterations have been shown to disrupt the activity of the switching defective/sucrose non-fermenting (SWI/SNF) histone remodeling complex (PMID:21248752). Consequently, the ability of the SWI/SNF complex to be effectively recruited to target loci to alter chromatin is impaired (PMID: 21654818). In addition, PBRM1 truncating mutations can no longer bind and remodel the p21 locus leading to cell cycle defects and aberrant cell proliferation (PMID: 18339845, 22949125). Loss of PBRM1 activity is also associated with chromosomal instability due to its inability to promote cohesion (PMID: 24613357) and significantly correlates with response to immunotherapy in patients with clear cell renal cell carcinoma (PMID: 31486842).

The PDGFRA N659K mutation occurs in the ATP binding domain of the protein rendering PDGFRA constitutively activated. PDGFRA N659K was identified as an acquired resistance mutation in a patient with a PDGFRA-driven gastrointestinal stromal tumor after treatment with avapritinib (PMID: 32972961). Expression of the PDGFRA N659K mutation in epithelial cells results in enhanced activation of PDGFRA signaling (PMID: 15928335).

The PDGFRA Y375_K455del mutation occurs in the protein's Ig-like extracellular domain and renders PDGFRA constitutively active. Expression of this mutant in fibroblasts results in increased downstream signaling, including activation of the PI3-kinase/AKT pathway (PMID:12569364, 20889717). Activation of downstream signaling pathways leads to enhanced cellular growth, as evidenced by proliferation and colony assays. Implantation of PDGFRA Y375_K455del altered cells into mice results in the generation of tumors, indicating that this alteration is oncogenic (PMID:12569364, 20889717).

The PDGFRA D842_H845del mutation has been found in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST) and is located in the protein's tyrosine kinase domain. Its expression is associated with constitutive activation of PDGFRA. Expression of PDGFRA D842_H845del in cell lines resulted in hyperactivation of PDGFRA signaling. Additionally, this mutant demonstrated sensitivity to imatinib (PMID: 22745105).

The PDGFRA S584L mutation occurs in the protein's juxtamembrane domain and results in increased activity of PDGFRA. Expression of this mutation in hematopoietic cells resulted in a modest increase in PDGFRA signaling (PMID: 24132921). Further functional assays are required to determine if this mutation is oncogenic.

The PDGFRA S478P mutation which occurs in the extracellular domain of PDGFRA. Expression of this mutation in 293T cells does not lead to increased PDGFRA activity; it has been suggested that the mutation is a polymorphism (SNP rs 35597638) (PMID:12949711, 19366796, 22733151). Therefore, this alteration is not likely oncogenic.

Focal amplification of PDGFRA is found in glioblastoma (PMID: 18772890), diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma (PMID: 21931021), intimal sarcoma (PMID: 20685895) and in malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (PMID: 16357008). Cell lines with amplification of PDGFRA have increased PDGFRA activation (PMID: 22745105, 20685895).

The PDGFRA E996K mutation occurs in the protein's second tyrosine kinase domain and does not affect the activation status of PDGFRA. Expression of this mutation in hematopoietic cells did not result in increased signaling, as evidenced by pathway activation assays (PMID: 23752188).

The FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion protein juxtaposes the N-terminal portion of FIP1L1 with the kinase domain of PDGFRA, disrupting the PDGFRA auto-inhibitory domain and resulting in constitutive PDGFRA kinase activity (PMID: 16690743). The FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion has been found in patients with hypereosinophilic syndrome or chronic eosinophilic leukemia (PMID: 12660384, 19187542, 24057647, 16608506). Expression of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion protein in hematopoietic stem cells and in mouse models demonstrated that it is activating and oncogenic as shown by enhanced pathway activation, proliferation, colony formation, and the development of a leukemia-like disease (PMID: 12660384, 21224473, 16030188, 16645167, 24407160, 19212337, 16754777, 27021554, 12781364, 21224473). Patients with the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion are sensitive to treatment with imatinib (PMID: 18950453).

The ETV6-PDGFRA fusion protein is expected to constitutively activate PDGFRA, although this has not been experimentally verified. In vitro experiments involving cell lines and mouse models expressing this mutation show that it is not sensitive to the kinase inhibitor, imatinib, as evidenced by sustained signaling and proliferation in the presence of the drug (PMID: 24132921, 16030188, 22665524, 15928335, 23970477, 18794084, 22745105, 15685537, 18955458, 23752188, 12522257, 17087936, 19217431, 12949711).

A case study demonstrated that a patient with hypereosinophilic syndrome harboring the KIF5B-PDGFRA achieved a complete response to imatinib after six months of therapy (PMID: 16498388).

Fusions of PDGFRA arise from chromosomal translocations that generally fuse the N-terminal portion of a partner protein with the C-terminal kinase-domain-containing portion of PDGFRA and disrupts the PDGFRA auto-inhibitory domain, resulting in constitutive PDGFRA kinase activity. In vitro biological characterization of PDGFRA fusion proteins demonstrate that they are activating and oncogenic as shown by increased pathway activation and the ability to induce anchorage-independent colony formation as well as tumor formation in vivo (PMID: 12781364, 21224473, 16690743) and are sensitive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors including imatinib and PTK787 (PMID: 20889717).

Therefore, the PDGFRA T674I mutation is likely an imatinib-resistant mutation.

The PDGFRA R748G mutation renders cell lines and mouse models sensitive to imatinib treatment as evidenced by proliferation, signaling and mouse xenograft assays (PMID: 21224473).

Mutations that occur in exon 14 of PDGFRA have been implicated in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 12522257).

Expression of this mutant in hematopoietic cells resulted in increased downstream signaling in the absence of growth factor stimulation, as evidenced by phosphorylation of STAT5. The PDGFRA Y849S-mutant cells also exhibited enhanced proliferation as evidenced in growth and colony assays (PMID: 21224473).

The PIK3CA E726K mutation is located between the accessory and the kinase domains of the protein. There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 but not MCF10A cell lines led to proliferation in the absence of growth factors (PMID: 29533785).

var_description: The PIK3CA E600K mutation is located in the accessory domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer, breast cancer and endometrial cancer (PMID: 27478040, 22722193, 22653804, 28481359). Expression of this mutation in PC9 cells suggested that it is likely activating as measured by increased cell proliferation in the context of erlotinib treatment compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 27478040).

The PIK3CA E545A mutation is located in the helical domain in exon 10 of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 31996845). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts, Ba/F3 cells or MCF10A breast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased downstream pathway activation, cytokine- and factor-independent proliferation and anchorage-independent growth compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 17376864, 26627007). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845). Mutations at this position are predicted to abrogate p85-mediated inhibition of catalytic activity, thus likely resulting in constitutive activation of PIK3CA enzymatic activity (PMID: 20593314).

However, in vivo studies also demonstrated that this mutation may be resistant to the SRC inhibitor saracatinib in a colorectal cancer patient-derived xenograft model as measured by sustained tumor burden in the presence of the drug (PMID: 22553375).

The PIK3CA E110K mutation is located in the adaptor binding domain in exon 2 of the protein. Expression of this mutation (called G106_R108delGNR) in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased proliferation in the absence of growth factors compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 29533785).

Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845). This mutation is predicted to constitutively activate the catalytic subunit of PI3K (p110α) by exposing the catalytic loop towards the plasma membrane where its substrate, PIP2, is found (PMID: 17376864, 20593314).

The PIK3CA C420R mutation is located in the linker region between the C2 domain and the helical domain in exon 8 of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial carcinoma and glioblastoma (PMID: 21266528, 31996845). Expression of this mutation in MCF10A breast cells and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity, proliferation, invasion, colony formation, and in vivo glioblastoma tumor burden compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 18074223, 22949682, 31996845).

The PIK3CA H1047R mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 21 of the protein (PMID: 16341083,17376864, 22120714). This mutation has been found in various cancers, including breast, head and neck, lung, colorectal and endometrial cancers (PMID: 27126994, 25631445, 23787421, 25079552, 22960745, 22941189, 17376864, 23636398). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts, Ba/F3 cells and MCF10A breast cells and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity, downstream pathway activation, cytokine- and factor-independent proliferation, colony growth in soft agar, invasion and in vivo glioblastoma tumor burden compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 17376864, 26627007, 16432179, 16322248, 31996845). Genetically engineered mouse models have shown that the PIK3CA H1047R mutation promotes tumor formation in breast, colon, ovarian and lung cancer and malignant mesothelioma (PMID: 22370636, 23940356, 22214849, 21822287, 21324922, 19029981, 31911549). Mutations at this position are predicted to constitutively activate the catalytic subunit of PI3K (p110α) by exposing the catalytic loop towards the plasma membrane where its substrate, PIP2, is found (PMID: 17376864, 20593314). Patients with breast cancer harboring this mutation achieved partial response (n=2) or stable disease (n=1) following treatment with the PI3Kα inhibitor, alpelisib (PMID: 27126994). In a phase III trial of palbociclib/fulvestrant for ER+, HER2− advanced breast cancer that had previously progressed on endocrine therapy, patients with PIK3CA alterations, including the H1047R mutation, were found at a significantly higher percentage in end-of-treatment samples as compared to pre-treatment samples, suggesting that this mutation may play a role in resistance to fulvestrant (PMID: 30206110). Preclinical studies with mice expressing PIK3CA H1047R demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with RLY-2608 as measured by reduced tumor volume following treatment (Abstract: Varkaris et al. Abstract# CT017, AACR 2023. https://www.abstractsonline.com/pp8/#!/10828/presentation/10256).

The PIK3CA E542K mutation is located in the helical domain in exon 10 of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and colon cancer and glioblastoma (PMID: 17376864, 31996845). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts (CEFs), Ba/F3 cells and MCF10A breast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity, downstream pathway activation, cytokine- and factor-independent proliferation, anchorage-independent growth and tumor growth in xenograft models compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 17376864, 26627007, 16432179). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845). Mutations at this position are predicted to abrogate p85-mediated inhibition of catalytic activity, thus likely resulting in constitutive activation of PIK3CA enzymatic activity (PMID: 20593314). In a phase III trial for ER+, HER2− advanced breast cancer that had previously progressed on endocrine therapy, patients were given either palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor) plus fulvestrant (ESR1 antagonist) or placebo plus fulvestrant. PIK3CA alterations, including the E542K mutation, were found at a significantly higher percentage in end-of-treatment samples as compared to pre-treatment samples in patients from both treatment arms, suggesting that PIK3CA alterations may play a role in resistance to fulvestrant. E542K was found more frequently than any other PIK3CA alteration in this study (PMID: 30206110). Expression of this mutation in a patient-derived xenograft model of lung squamous cell carcinoma demonstrated that it was sensitive to the pan-PIK3CA inhibitor BKM120 and the PIK3CAalpha-specific inhibitor BYL719 compared to PDX models expressing wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 30093452).

PIK3CA amplification is an infrequent event across cancers (PMID: 28481359), although several individual studies have reported them in lung squamous cell carcinoma, ovarian, esophagus, cervical, and head and neck tumors (PMID: 22960745, 21720365, 25631445, 23636398). PIK3CA gene amplification has been correlated with PIK3CA protein overexpression (PMID: 17992665,19697359). PIK3CA overexpression enhances growth and migration (PMID: 17803655, 26876212). PIK3CA amplifications associate with poor prognosis in several cancers (PMID: 22994622, 22292935, 27095573). Some studies have found a correlation between PIK3CA copy number amplification and sensitivity to PI3K inhibitors (PMID: 24608574, 23136191). Amplification of PIK3CA known pathogenic mutant alleles have also been reported (PMID: 19706770). Expression of this mutation in a patient-derived xenograft model of lung squamous cell carcinoma demonstrated that it was not sensitive to the pan-PIK3CA inhibitor BKM120 similar to PDX models expressing wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 30093452).

The PIK3CA C378Y mutation is located in the PI3K-C2 domain of the protein. There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 but not MCF10A cell lines led to proliferation in the absence of growth factors (PMID: 29533785).

The PIK3CA C24Y mutation is located N-terminally of the p85 binding domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by failure to proliferate in the absence of growth factors (PMID: 29533785).

var_description: The PIK3CA N345I mutation is located in the C2 domain in exon 5 of the protein. Expression of this mutation in MCF10A and Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased cytokine- and factor-independent growth compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 26627007, 29533785). This mutation is predicted to disrupt the interaction with the iSH2 domain of the regulatory subunit p85 (PIK3R1), leading to protein activation (PMID: 20593314).

The PIK3CA Y1021C mutation is located in the C-terminus of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 31996845). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased growth factor-independent proliferation (PMID: 29533785). However, expression of this mutation in MCF10A cells and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by failure to induce growth factor-independent proliferation or in vivo glioblastoma formation (PMID: 29533785, 31996845).

var_description: The PIK3CA Q75E mutation is located in the PI3K-ABD domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in glioma (PMID: 30333046). In vitro studies with PCI-52-SD1 cells expressing PIK3CA Q75E demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by cellular transformation and increased cellular proliferation, migration and AKT phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 34779417). In a clinical case study, a patient with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma harboring PIK3CA Q75E was treated with alpelisib and demonstrated partial response with 73% tumor shrinkage (PMID: 34779417). Preclinical studies with cells expressing PIK3CA Q75E demonstrate sensitivity to alpelisib as measured by decreased cellular proliferation and increased apoptosis following treatment (PMID: 34779417).

The PIK3CA E545K mutation is located in the helical domain in exon 10 of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and colon cancer and glioblastoma (PMID: 17376864, 31996845). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts, Ba/F3 cells, MCF10A breast cells and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity, downstream pathway activation, factor-independent proliferation, anchorage-independent colony formation, in vivo tumor growth in xenograft models, and in vivo glioblastoma formation compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 17376864, 26627007, 16432179, 16322248, 31996845). Mutations at this position are predicted to abrogate p85-mediated inhibition of catalytic activity, thus likely resulting in constitutive activation of PIK3CA enzymatic activity (PMID: 20593314). In a phase III trial for ER+, HER2− advanced breast cancer that had previously progressed on endocrine therapy, patients were given either palbociclib (CDK4/6 inhibitor) plus fulvestrant (ESR1 antagonist) or placebo plus fulvestrant. PIK3CA alterations, including the E545K mutation, were found at a significantly higher percentage in end-of-treatment samples as compared to pre-treatment samples in patients from both treatment arms, suggesting that PIK3CA alterations may play a role in resistance to fulvestrant (PMID: 30206110). Expression of this mutation in a patient-derived xenograft model of lung squamous cell carcinoma demonstrated that it was sensitive to the pan-PIK3CA inhibitor BKM120 and the PIK3CAalpha-specific inhibitor BYL719 compared to PDX models expressing wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 30093452). Preclinical studies with mice expressing PIK3CA E545K demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with RLY-2608 as measured by reduced tumor volume following treatment (Abstract: Varkaris et al. Abstract# CT017, AACR 2023. https://www.abstractsonline.com/pp8/#!/10828/presentation/10256).

The PIK3CA A1020V mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 21 of the protein. Expression of this mutation in MCF10A breast cells or Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by cytokine- and factor-independent growth comparable to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 26627007, 28528867).

var_description: The PIK3CA R115P mutation is located in the adaptor binding domain in exon 2 of the protein. This mutation has been found in a patient with lipofibromatous hamartoma of nerve and a patient with megalencephaly-capillary malformation syndrome, both conditions associated with somatic PI3K/AKT activating mutations (PMID: 23100325). In vitro studies with MCF-7 cells expressing PIK3CA R115P demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased cell growth and migration compared to wildtype (PMID: 31632573). Preclinical studies of PIK3CA R115P suggest the mutation is resistant to treatment with fulvestrant as measured through persistent cell growth following treatment in MCF-7 cells compared to wildtype (PMID: 31632573).

The PIK3CA H1047L mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 21 of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer, colon cancer and glioblastoma (PMID: 17376864, 31996845). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts (CEFs), Ba/F3 and MCF10A breast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activity, downstream pathway activation, factor-independent growth, focus formation in soft agar and invasion compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 22120714, 17376864, 26627007, 29533785). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845). This mutation is predicted to constitutively activate the catalytic subunit of PI3K (p110α) by exposing the catalytic loop towards the plasma membrane where its substrate, PIP2, is found (PMID: 17376864, 20593314). In a phase III trial of palbociclib/fulvestrant for ER+, HER2− advanced breast cancer that had previously progressed on endocrine therapy, patients with PIK3CA alterations, including the H1074L mutation, were found at a significantly higher percentage in end-of-treatment samples as compared to pre-treatment samples, suggesting that this mutation may play a role in resistance to fulvestrant (PMID: 30206110).

var_description: The PIK3CA E110del mutation is located in the N-terminus of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation and proliferation in the absence of growth factors compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785, 30205045). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845).

The PIK3CA E81K mutation is located in the adaptor binding domain in exon 2 of the protein. This mutation has been found in megalencephaly-capillary malformation (MCAP) syndrome, endometrial carcinoma and glioblastoma (PMID: 25915946, 21266528, 31996845). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Fibroblasts isolated from patients with MCAP syndrome harboring germline PIK3CA E81K mutation showed increased levels of phospho-AKT (Threonine-308 and Serine-473) and phospho-p70S6K compared to control fibroblasts as well as factor-independent proliferation that could be inhibited with inhibitors of PI3K (PMID: 25915946). However, expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines and in a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by failure to proliferate in the absence of growth factors and failure to promote in vivo glioblastoma formation (PMID: 29533785, 31996845).

The PIK3CA E545Q mutation is located in the helical domain in exon 10 of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells or MCF10A breast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cytokine- and factor-independent growth compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 26627007, 29533785). Mutations at this position are predicted to abrogate p85-mediated inhibition of catalytic activity, thus likely resulting in constitutive activation of PIK3CA enzymatic activity (PMID: 20593314).

The PIK3CA M1043V mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 21 of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 17376864). Expression of this mutation in chicken embryonic fibroblasts and Ba/F3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased downstream pathway activation, focus formation in soft agar and proliferation in the absence of IL-3 compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 17376864, 29533785).

The PIK3CA P366R mutation is located in the C2 domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 29533785). This mutation was identified in a patient within a cohort of metastatic and treatment-resistant ER+ breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in MCF10A cells resulted in increased PIK3CA downstream pathway activity compared to WT MCF10A cells as measured by western blot (PMID: 30205045).

var_description: The PIK3CA P449_L455delPHGLEDL mutation is located in the PI3K-C2 domain of the protein. The PIK3CA G118D mutation is located in the linker region between the adaptor binding domain and the Ras binding domain in exon 3 of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial carcinoma and glioblastoma (PMID: 22949682, 31996845). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and proliferation in the absence of growth factors compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 29533785, 22949682). Expression of this mutation in a transgenic mouse model was not sufficient to drive glioblastoma formation (PMID: 31996845).

The PIK3CA N1068fs*4 mutation is located in the kinase domain in exon 21 of the protein. Expression of this mutation in mouse hepatocytes led to increased downstream pathway activation compared to PIK3CA wildtype hepatocytes and led to tumor formation in a transgenic mouse model (PMID: 21703185). However, expression of PIK3CA N1068fs*4 in vitro in cell lines did not lead to activation of AKT or transformation (PMID: 21703185).

var_description: The PIK3CA A1066V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in urothelial carcinoma (PMID: 22430209). Expression of this mutation in fibroblasts and urothelial cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, cell proliferation and colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 22430209). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the PIK3CA inhibitor GDC-0941 in a bladder cancer cell line that also harbored two TSC1 mutations as measured by decreased pathway activation and cell proliferation in the presence of the drug (PMID: 27465249).

The PIK3CA R38S mutation is located in the p85 binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colorectal and endometrial cancer (PMID: 22653804, 27149842). While this variant has not been functionally characterized, in silico crystal structure models predict that this mutation is activating (PMIDs: 19962665, 18079394).

The PIK3CA E103_G106delinsD mutation is located in the p85 binding domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased proliferation in the absence of growth factors compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 29533785).

The PIK3CA L766F mutation is located between the accessory domain and the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by failure to proliferate in the absence of growth factors (PMID: 29533785).

var_description: The PIK3CA R93Q mutation is located in the adaptor binding domain in exon 2 of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial carcinoma in conjunction with other PIK3CA mutations (PMID: 21266528). Expression of this mutation in U2OS osteosarcoma cells suggests that this mutation is likely activating, as measured by mildly increased downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 21266528).

The PIK3R1 K379E mutation occurs in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the inhibitory interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110 domain, but can still bind p110α in biochemical assays. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, enhanced colony formation, and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3CA D549N mutation is located in the helical domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and MCF10A cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by increased factor-independent proliferation compared to wildtype PIK3CA (PMID: 29533785).

The PIK3R1 I559_D560insDKRMNS mutation is located in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1 (p85α subunit), the domain that regulates p110α binding. This frameshift mutation likely disrupts the binding interaction between PIK3R1 and the catalytic p110 domain (PMID: 20713702). Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by increased proliferation, colony formation and downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 W333R mutation is located in the SH2 domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 22810696). In vitro studies with EFE-184 and KLE cells expressing PIK3R1 W333R demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by increased cell viability, clonogenic growth capacity, invasion and migration compared to wildtype (PMID: 34507989).

The PIK3R1 N564K mutation occurs in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the inhibitory interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110α domain, but it can still stabilize p110α binding. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, modest colony formation, and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 Y452H mutation is located in the phosphatase binding domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing PIK3R1 Y452H demonstrate this mutation is inactivating as measured by increased transformation ability compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The PIK3R1 K288Q mutation is found in the RHO-GAP domain of PIK3R1. This mutation was identified in urothelial cancer samples (PMID: 24367658). Biological characterization of this variant in MEF cells did not affect p110α binding; however, this variant caused a modest increase in colony formation (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 X475_splice mutation results in the deletion of exon 11, which encodes for a portion of the iSH2 domain. This mutation leads to decreased binding of PIK3R1 to the catalytic PI3K subunit (P110δ), thereby causing aberrant activation of the PI3K pathway (PMID: 25488983, 25133428). Expression of this mutation in primary T cells resulted in increased downstream AKT/mTOR signaling as evidenced by an increase in phospho-AKT (PMID: 25488983, 25133428).

The PIK3R1 L372_R373del mutation is located in the SH2 domain of the protein. In vitro studies with EFE-184 and KLE cells expressing PIK3R1 L372_R373del demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by increased cell viability, clonogenic growth capacity, invasion and migration compared to wildtype (PMID: 34507989).

The PIK3R1 D560Y mutation occurs in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the inhibitory interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110α domain, but it can still stabilize p110α binding. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, modest colony formation, and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 N564D mutation is found in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1, a domain important for stabilization of p110α. This variant has been shown to preserve the stabilizing interaction but disrupt inhibitory interactions between p85α and p110α. Biological characterization of MEF cells expressing this mutation demonstrated that this variant is inactivating and promotes growth, as demonstrated by enhanced PI3K/AKT signaling and increased colony formation (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 E218* mutation is found in the RHO-GAP domain of PIK3R1. This mutation was identified in urothelial cancer samples (PMID: 24367658). Biological characterization of this variant in mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) demonstrated that it eliminates binding of PIK3R1 to p110α, but does not alter downstream PI3K/AKT signaling. However, expression of this variant was associated with a modest increase in colony formation (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 R503W mutation lies in the iSH2 domain in exon 11 of the protein (PMID: 21984976). This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer and colorectal cancer (PMID: 21984976, 25957691). Expression of PIK3R1 R503W in Ba/F3 cells led to pathway activation and factor-independent growth, suggesting that this mutation is inactivating and oncogenic (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R1 W624R mutation is located in the cSH2 domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in high grade serous ovarian carcinoma (PMID: 32075097). Structural prediction models and patient-derived xenograft models demonstrate that this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by increased sensitivity to PI3K inhibitors compared to control cell lines (PMID: 32075097).

The PIK3R1 K567E mutation is located in the iSH2 domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in glioma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29263181). Immunohistochemistry analysis of patient-derived breast cancer samples expressing PIK3R1 K567E demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by abrogated inhibitory activity of PI3KCA and usual ductal hyperplasia expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 26718977).

The exon 4 PIK3R1 R162* mutation occurs in the RHO-GAP domain and has been found in in urothelial cancer (PMID: 24367658). Cell line experiments demonstrate that this mutation is likely inactivating and likely transforming as measured by colony formation (PMID: 24367658). This mutation eliminates binding of PIK3R1 to p110α (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 W237_Y242del mutation is found in the RHO-GAP domain of PIK3R1. This mutation was identified in urothelial cancer samples (PMID: 24367658). In vitro studies with MEF cells expressing this mutation demonstrated PIK3R1 W237_Y242del is inactivating as measured by increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658). This mutation did not demonstrate any effect on PI3K catalytic subunit p110α binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 K459_S460delinsN mutation occurs in the nSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the inhibitory interaction between PIK3R1 and the catalytic p110 domain, but can still bind p110α in biochemical assays (PMID: 20713702). Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by increased proliferation, enhanced colony formation and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 E137K mutation is found in the RHO-GAP domain of PIK3R1. This mutation was identified in urothelial cancer samples (PMID: 24367658). In vitro studies with MEF cells expressing this mutation demonstrate PIK3R1 E137K is inactivating as measured by increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658). This mutation did not demonstrate any effect on PI3K catalytic subunit p110α binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658).

The PIK3R1 G376R mutation occurs in the nSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the binding interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110 domain. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, modest colony formation, and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 Q579_L581del mutation occurs within the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1. In vitro studies with MEF cells and BaF3 cells overexpressing this mutation demonstrated PIK3R1 Q579_L581del is inactivating as measured by increased cellular proliferation and anchorage-independent growth (PMID: 19962665). This mutation did not demonstrate any effect on PI3K catalytic subunit p110α binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 19962665).

Deletions of PIK3R1 resulting in loss of the regulatory subunit of PI(3)-kinase have been identified in patients with breast cancer (PMID: 24229379). Studies in primary human immunodeficiency with lymphoproliferation demonstrate that PIK3R1 truncating mutations likely lead to loss of PIK3R1 function, as measured by increased pathway activation, proliferation and survival compared to wildtype (PMID: 25133428, 25488983). These mutations are predicted to disrupt the ability of p85α to inhibit the PI3K catalytic subunit, p110α, thus resulting in aberrant activation of AKT-mTOR signaling

The PIK3R1 R262T mutation is found in the RHO-GAP domain of PIK3R1. This mutation was identified in urothelial cancer samples (PMID: 24367658). In vitro studies with MEF cells expressing this mutation demonstrated PIK3R1 R262T is inactivating as measured by increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658). This mutation did not demonstrate any effect on PI3K catalytic subunit p110α binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 24367658).

The exon 9 PIK3R1 truncating L370fs mutation is located in the SH2 domain of the protein and likely results in an inactive truncated PIK3R1 protein. Experiments in cancer cell lines demonstrate that this mutation is associated with aberrant PI3K catalytic activity and downstream activation of MEK (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase), and JNK (Jun N-terminal kinase signaling pathways (PMID: 25284480). Expression of this mutation leads to increased proliferation and cellular transformation (PMID: 25284480).

Truncating mutations of PIK3R1, including nonsense and frameshift mutations, likely lead to loss of PIK3R1 function and thus PI3K pathway activation. Studies in Ba/F3 cells have shown that expression of PIK3R1 truncating mutations lead to cytokine-independent cell growth in an otherwise cytokine-dependent cell line, suggesting they are transforming (PMID: 25284480). Additionally, a cohort of patients with PASLI disease (p110δ-activating mutations causing senescent T cells, lymphadenopathy, and immunodeficiency disease) and patients with hypogammaglobulinemia were found to harbor PIK3R1 frameshift mutations, which were demonstrated to lead to activation of PI3K signaling and result in a disease-related phenotype (PMID: 25488983, 25133428).

The PIK3R1 E160* mutation disrupts the binding between PIK3R1 and the catalytic subunit (p110α), thus leading to aberrant PI3K catalytic activity and downstream activation of AKT/mTOR signaling pathways (PMID: 21984976, 25284480). This mutant protein can no longer bind and stabilize the tumor suppressor PTEN (Phosphatase and Tensin) leading to its degradation (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutant in cell lines leads to increased proliferation, cellular transformation, colony formation, and tumor xenograft formation (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R1 R348* mutation occurs within the nSH2 domain of PIK3R1 and disrupts the binding between PIK3R1 and the catalytic subunit (p110α), thus leading to aberrant PI3K (phosphoinositide 3-kiase) catalytic activity and downstream activation of MEK (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase) and JNK (Jun N-terminal kinase) signaling pathways (PMID: 21984976, 25284480, 21478295). This mutation can still bind and stabilize the tumor suppressor PTEN (Phosphatase and Tensin) (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutation in cell lines results in increased proliferation, cellular transformation, colony formation and growth in tumor xenograft models (PMID: 21984976). Cell lines and tumor xenograft models engineered to express this mutation were sensitive to treatment with various MEK (mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase) and JNK (Jun N-terminal kinase) inhibitors (PMID: 21984976, 25284480), but insensitive to mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin), p110 and p38-MAPK (p38-mitogen activated protein kinase) inhibition as evidenced by resistance to rapamycin, GDC0941, and SB203580 (PMID: 25284480).

The PIK3R1 E439del mutation is located in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1. This mutation likely disrupts the binding interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110 domain. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, modest colony formation and increased downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 R574fs mutation occurs in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1 (p85α subunit), the domain that regulates p110α binding. This gain-of-function frameshift mutation likely disrupts the binding interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110 domain. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, colony formation, and downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 T576del mutation occurs in the iSH2 domain of PIK3R1 (p85α subunit), the domain that regulates p110α binding. This gain-of-function frameshift mutation likely disrupts the binding interaction between PI3KR1 and the catalytic p110 domain. Biological characterization of this variant in chicken embryonic fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation leads to increased proliferation, colony formation, and downstream PI3K/AKT signaling (PMID: 20713702).

The PIK3R1 X434_splice mutation results in the deletion of exon 11, which encodes for a portion of the iSH2 domain. This mutation leads to decreased binding of PIK3R1 to the catalytic PI3K subunit (P110δ), thereby causing aberrant activation of PI3K pathway (PMID: 25488983, 25133428). Expression of this mutation in primary T cells resulted in increased downstream AKT/mTOR signaling as evidenced by an increase in phospho-AKT (PMID: 25488983, 25133428).

The exon 13 PIK3R1 X582_splice mutation is located towards the C-terminus of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. This mutation has not been functionally tested. While some PIK3R1 splice and truncating mutations have been shown to be inactivating and associated with hematologic and immune diseases, others have been shown to be neutral (PMID: 25488983, 25133428, 25284480).

The PIK3R1 K448_Y452del mutation is located in the iSH2 domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrioid carcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies in breast epithelial cells have demonstrated that this mutation is oncogenic as demonstrated by suppression of anchorage-independent cell adhesion/survival, loss of lipid and protein phosphatase activities and reduced protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 32366478). This mutation also leads to loss of PTEN function by yeast gene interaction assay, by altered developmental rate in Drosophila, by changes in rat neural development and by becoming a dominant negative regulator of the PI3-AKT signaling pathway (PMID: 32350270).

The PTEN C71Y mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in brain cancer (PMID: 28481359, 11051241). Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it was inactivating as measured by decreased protein phosphatase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 10866302, 11051241).

The PTEN G165E mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in pancreatic cancer and glioblastoma (PMID: 21828076). The PTEN K128Q mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 22653804). Expression of this mutation in prostate cancer cells demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by increased downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 25447541).

Expression of this mutation in yeast cells demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 21828076).

The PTEN L320S mutation is located between the C2 and phosphatase domains of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma and leiomyosarcoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 27433843, 28481359, 26619011). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein phosphatase activity compared to wildtype. However, expression of this mutation in isolated glioma cells demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by protein mislocalization and increased downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 28263967).

The PTEN H93Y mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial cancer (PMID: 21828076). This mutation also leads to loss of PTEN function by yeast gene interaction assay, by altered developmental rate in Drosophila, by changes in rat neural development and by becoming a dominant negative regulator of the PI3-AKT signaling pathway (PMID: 32350270).

The PTEN L42R mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioma (PMID: 11678426, 10560660, 9090379). There is conflicting functional data on this mutation. Expression of this mutation in vitro and endogenous expression of this mutation in a glioblastoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in phosphatase activity or pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 28464039, 10866302). However, expression of this mutation in a glioblastoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 25527629).

The PTEN F21A mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. The PTEN C124G mutation is located in the phosphatase tensin-type domain of the protein and is a statistically significant hotspot. In vitro studies with U87MG cells expressing PTEN C124G demonstrate that this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by loss of phosphatase activity and inability to suppress cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 9823298).

The PTEN S362L mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in lung cancer cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19329485).

The PTEN L112R mutation occurs in the phosphatase domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in vitro demonstrated that it was inactivating as measured by decreased protein phosphatase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 10866302).

The PTEN R173H mutation is located in the phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in brain cancer (PMID: 17098662, 28270234, 15679305). The PTEN Y177D mutation is located in the phosphatase tensin-type domain of the protein. The PTEN D301N mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in lung cancer cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19329485).

The PTPN11 F71I mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with F71I mutant alleles show an increased protein phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).
The PTPN11 G503V mutation is located in its protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain. Cells transfected with G503V mutant alleles show a modest increase in phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).

The PTPN11 E69K mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain of PTPN11 and has been found to occur in patients with juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (PMID: 12717436). Biological characterization of the PTPN11 E69K mutant demonstrates that this mutation is associated with an approximately 15 increase in protein phosphatase activity (PMID:15604238).
The PTPN11 Y63C mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with Y63C mutant alleles show a modest increase in phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).

The PTPN11 E76Q mutation is located in the SH2 domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 16518851). In vitro studies with MCF10A cells expressing PTPN11 E76Q demonstrate the mutation is likely neutral as measured by cell viability and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 29533785).

The PTPN11 R498W mutation is located in the tyrosine phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been reported in the germline of Noonan syndrome (NS) individuals, as well as somatically in leukemia patients (PMID: 17053061, 24891296). A case report of an NS patient carrying both PTPN11 P491S and R498W mutations suggested that the latter mutation was inactivating as measured by counteracting the P491S-mediated increase in PTPN11 phosphatase activity (PMID: 17053061, 24891296).

The Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase (PTP) domain of the PTPN11 protein is a catalytic region, which, when activated, dephosphorylates its targets leading to increased activity of the RAS/ERK pathway (PMID: 18286234). Mutations in the PTP domain have been described in juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, the Noonan and LEOPARD syndromes (PMID 18286234), and in acute myeloid leukemia and neuroblastoma (PMID: 15604238). Mutations in this domain that have been described in cancer and include T507K, which occurs at the interface between SH2 and PTP (PMID: 15604238). In its resting state, there is tonic inhibition of SH2 of the PTP, which is relieved when SH2 interacts with a phosphorylated receptor tyrosine kinase. Mutations in this domain result in increased activity of PTPN11 (PMID: 15604238).

The PTPN11 R498L mutation has been identified in LEOPARD syndrome (LS) patients. Cells transfected with PTPN11 R498L show a moderate increase in SHP2 association with Gab1 upon EGF or HGF stimulation, although an increase in downstream ERK phosphorylation was not clear (PMID: 24935154).

The PTPN11 A461T mutation occurs within the protein-tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain of the protein, specifically in a motif conserved in this domain family. In an in vitro assay, this mutation was shown to abolish the enzymatic function of PTPN11. In a cell line assay of ERK phosphorylation, the mutation also suppressed normal PTPN11 function in a dominant-negative manner, despite the addition of growth factor (PMID: 16377799). The mutation is hypothesized to disrupt the catalytic cleft in the PTP domain.

The causative role of PTPN11 deficiency remains to be determined, but is likely due to a loss-of-function mutation (PMID: 22869052). In a mouse model, selective deletion of PTPN11 in hepatocytes led to impaired regenerative capacity of the liver following hepatectomy. Though the association of PTPN11-activating mutations with oncogenes would lead to the anticipation that inactivating mutations of PTPN11 would be protective against malignancy development this was not the case. Indeed, at 12-months, PTPN11 deficient mice developed macroscopic adenomas suggesting a duality to PTPN11, and its potential role as a tumor suppressor.

The PTPN11 E76K mutation is located in the protein's N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with E76K mutant alleles show MAPK signaling activation and increased proliferation rates (PMID: 12717436, 15834506).

PTPN11 T468M is a germline mutation is located in the protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain and frequently occurs in LEOPARD syndrome patients. Unlike other PTPN11 missense mutations, T468M has an inactivating effect, as demonstrated by the in vitro loss of PTPN11 catalytic activity in cells transfected with this mutation (PMID: 16358218). This loss of PTP activity leads to an impaired ability to activate the RAS-ERK pathway, an effect mediated by parafibromin, a Wnt-pathway regulator (PMID: 26742426). Another study explored the metabolic consequences of PTPN11 T468M knock-in mice and showed reduced adiposity and protection against diet-induced obesity (PMID: 25288766).

PTPN11 D106A is a germline mutation that has been reported in Noonan syndrome (PMID: 18286234). This mutations occurs in the inter-SH2 domain linker, and likely creates a "kink" in the protein conformation of the phosphatase structure, thereby activating the catalytic activity of Protein Tyrosine Phosphatase (PTP) (PMID: 18286234).
The PTPN11 Q79R mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with Q79R mutant alleles show a modest increase in phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).
The PTPN11 E76A mutation is located in the protein's N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with E76A mutant alleles showed an increased phosphatase activity (PMID: 12717436, 15834506).

The PTPN11 A72V mutation is located in the N-SH2 domain of the protein. Cells transfected with A72V mutant alleles show a sharp increase in phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506). Molecular dynamics studies predict that this mutation is activating (PMID: 16358218) and a patient with BRAF V600E-mutant gliofibroma developed a PTPN11 A72V mutation upon tumor progression (PMID: 31179415).

The PTPN11 F285S mutation is located in the tyrosine phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in myeloid neoplasms and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 31366621). In silico analysis of PTPN11 F285S suggests that the mutation is activating (PMID: 35440950).
The PTPN11 S502T mutation is located in its protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain. Cells transfected with S502T mutant alleles show increased phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).
The PTPN11 M504V mutation is located in its protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain. Cells transfected with M504V mutant alleles show increased phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).

The PTPN11 E139D mutation has been found in the germline of Noonan syndrome (NS) patients and somatically in leukemia patients. Enzymatic studies comparing phosphatase activity of PTPN11 E139D mutant vs. wildtype did not show differences in basal conditions, but a consistent four-fold increase for the mutant upon stimulation with a PTPN11 substrate (PMID: 16358218).
The PTPN11 Y62C mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with Y62C mutant alleles show a modest increase in phosphatase activity (PMID: 15604238).

The PTPN11 K590R mutation affects a key residue for protein SUMOylation. PTPN11 (SHP2) SUMOylation at lysine 590 enhances ERK signaling, anchorage independent cell growth and tumor growth in a hepatocellular carcinoma cell model. The SUMOylation-defective PTPN11 K590R mutation impairs these oncogenic effects (PMID: 25823821).
The PTPN11 V45L mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Lung adenocarcinoma V45L-mutant cells showed a modest increase in protein phosphatase activity (PMID: 15604238).

The PTPN11 Q510E loss-of-function mutation has been indentified in LEOPARD syndrome patients, which frequently show hipertrophic myocardiopathies. Studies in mouse cardiomyocites expressing PTPN11 Q510E mutation showed a decrease in cell differentiation, an increase in cell migration and phosphorylation of Akt and Gsk3-β and the activation of mTOR signaling pathway (PMID: 22058153, 25359717, 21803945).

The PTPN11 G464A mutation has been identified in LEOPARD syndrome (LS) patients. Cells transfected with PTPN11 G464A show a moderate increase in SHP2 association with Gab1 upon EGF or HGF stimulation, although an increase in downstream ERK phosphorylation was not clear (PMID: 24935154).

The PTPN11 I282V mutation is located in its protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain. Cells transfected with I282V mutant alleles show increased phosphatase activity, prolonged ERK2 activation in response to EGF and higher proliferation rates (PMID: 14974085, 15834506).

The PTPN11 A72S mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with A72S mutant alleles show increased phosphatase activity, prolonged ERK2 activation in response to EGF and higher proliferation rates (PMID: 14974085).

The PTPN11 P491S mutation has been reported in the germline of Noonan syndrome (NS) patients. A case report of a NS patient carrying both PTPN11 P491S and R498W mutations suggested that PTPN11 P491S mutation confers increased PTPN11 phosphatase activity, but this is dampened by the opposite action of R498W, suggesting that additional genetic alterations might be responsible for this patient's phenotype (PMID: 24891296).
The PTPN11 D61N mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with D61N mutant alleles show augmented phosphatase activity but are not able to enhance ERK signaling (PMID: 15834506).
The PTPN11 T73I mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with T73I mutant alleles show an increased phosphatase activity (PMID: 15834506).

The PTPN11 D61Y mutation is located in its N-SH2 domain. Cells transfected with D61Y mutant alleles show augmented phosphatase activity, enhanced MAPK signaling and increased proliferation rates (PMID: 12717436, 15834506).

The PTPN11 N308D mutation is located in its protein tyrosine phosphatase (PTP) domain. Cells transfected with N308D mutant alleles show increased phosphatase activity, prolonged ERK2 activation in response to EGF and higher proliferation rates (PMID: 14974085, 15834506, 12717436).

The RB1 R621C mutation is located in the linker domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in intestinal cancer (PMID: 29360550, 24755471). Expression of this mutation in cervical cancer and sarcoma cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased cell apoptosis compared to wildtype (PMID: 20594292).

The RB1 N480del mutation is located in the N terminus of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation with low penetrance in retinoblastoma. Expression of this mutation in a lung cancer cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein phosphorylation and no change in the transcriptional activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 18677112).

The RB1 R661W mutation is located in pocket domain B of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation with low penetrance in retinoblastoma (PMID: 1352883, 16269091, 17096365, 26925970). There is conflicting functional data for this mutation. Expression of this mutation in lung cancer and osteosarcoma cell lines demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein phosphorylation and no change in the ability to induce cell differentiation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18677112). However, endogenous expression of this mutation in gastrointestinal cancer or in a knock-in mouse model, as well as expression of this mutation in osteosarcoma cell lines, demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by decreased protein stability, inability to bind E2F and increased retinal defects compared to wildtype (PMID: 18677112, 9420334, 16449662).

The RB1 C706F mutation is located in the pocket domain B of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 2288878, 20016488, 2168563). Expression of this mutation in a lymphoblastoid cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activity, transcriptional activity and effect on differentiation compared to wildtype (PMID: 18677112).

The RB1 L607I mutation is located in the linker domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23474753). Expression of this mutation in cervical cancer and sarcoma cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein stability and decreased cell apoptosis compared to wildtype (PMID: 20594292). One patient with breast cancer harboring this mutation did not respond to neoadjuvant anthracycline or mitomycin (PMID: 23474753).

The RB1 R698W mutation is located in the pocket domain B of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 20594292, 27135926). Expression of this mutation in cervical cancer and sarcoma cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased cell apoptosis and decreased protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 20594292).

The RB1 S567L mutation is located in the linker domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in familial retinoblastoma (PMID: 10671068). Expression of this mutation in a sarcoma cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased binding to E2F, failure to induce G1 arrest and failure to promote differentiation compared to wildtype (PMID: 9420334).

RB1 truncating mutations produce several forms of C-terminally truncated RB1 proteins. These mutations have been found as germline mutations in familial retinoblastoma (PMID: 14769601). Loss of RB1 in an osteosarcoma cell line resulted in increased genome instability, DNA damage and tumor growth in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 31138663). Loss of RB1 in germinal center B-cells of an in-vivo mouse model induced hyperproliferation of splenic B cells that eventually resulted in increased cell death compared to wildtype (PMID: 26607597). Six patients with ER+HER2- advanced breast cancer harboring RB1 mutation, out of a study of 127 patients, demonstrated resistance to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib in combination with the ESR1 inhibitor fulvestrant (PMID: 30206110). Truncating mutations of RB1 often predispose patients who have been successfully treated for hereditary retinoblastoma to secondary malignancies (PMID: 22205104).

Deletion of RB1 results in the loss of the RB1 protein. This mutation has been found in almost half of all cases of familial retinoblastoma (PMID: 16127685). Deletion of RB1 in an osteosarcoma cell line resulted in increased genome instability, DNA damage and tumor growth in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 31138663). Deletion of RB1 in germinal center B-cells of an in-vivo mouse model induced hyperproliferation of splenic B cells that eventually resulted in increased cell death compared to wildtype (PMID: 26607597). Six patients with ER+ /HER2- advanced breast cancer harboring RB1 mutation demonstrated resistance to the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib in combination with the ESR1 inhibitor fulvestrant in a study of 127 patients (PMID: 30206110).

The RB1 C712R mutation is located in pocket domain B of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation with low penetrance in retinoblastoma. Expression of this mutation in a lymphoblastoid cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein phosphorylation and no change in transcriptional activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 18677112).

The RET D631N mutation is located adjacent to the cysteine-rich domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as measured by no increased foci formation or phosphorylation compared to wildtype RET (PMID: 10049754).

The RET D898_E901del mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in medullary thyroid cancers (PMID: 29515777, 31605946). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 and NIH3T3 cells demonstrated it is activating as measured by cell growth in the absence of IL-3 and increased downstream ERK activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 32284345). In vitro experiments demonstrated that this mutation is sensitive to the RET tyrosine kinase inhibitors selpercatinib and pralsetinib, and to a lesser extent crizotinib, as measured by decreased cell growth and decreased downstream pathway activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 32284345).

The RET C611Y mutation is located in the cysteine-rich domain of RET. Expression of this mutation into NIH3T3 cells induces transformation and activation of RET as demonstrated by higher levels of phospho-tyrosine. This mutation is thought to disrupt the transport of RET to the plasma membrane or its maturation (PMID: 9230192).

The RET C634W mutation is located in the cysteine-rich domain of the protein. In vitro studies with COS7 cells expressing RET C634W demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased colony formation and migration and increased phosphorylation of RET, AKT and PI3K compared to wildtype (PMID: 34905813). In vitro experiments demonstrated that this variant is sensitive to sorafenib, as measured by decreased pathway activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 17664273).

The RET D631_L633delinsE is located in exon 11 of the RET protein. This mutation has been found in a patient with medullary thyroid cancer (PMID: 27082517). While the RET D631_L633delinsE mutation has not been functionally characterized, other indel variants in exon 11, such as E632_L633del and R635-T636insELCR, have been found to be associated with germline predisposition to medullary thyroid cancer (PMID: 15858153, 9191060). In vitro studies of RET exon 11 indel variants have demonstrated that they are activating, as measured by increased foci formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 9191060).

The RET A883T mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in medullary thyroid cancer (PMID: 21810974, 15531548). Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells suggested that this variant is activating, as measured by modestly increased proliferation and foci formation compared to wildtype RET (PMID: 21810974).

The RET M848T mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 resulted in high transforming activity in colony formation assays compared to wildtype cells. However, NIH3T3 cells expressing the RET M848T mutation did not show increased proliferation rates compared to control cells (PMID: 21810974).
The RET A919P mutation is predicted in silico to be activating (PMID: 16928683).

The RET M918T mutation is located in the substrate binding pocket of the RET kinase domain. This mutation increases the affinity of RET for ATP and thus stabilizes the active form of the protein (PMID: 22584710, 24561444). The M918T mutation activates transforming properties of MET, and leads to constitutive activation of the RET kinase independently of dimer formation (PMID: 9681850, 8755580, 7824936). Autosomal dominant germline M918T mutations are associated with the MEN2B syndrome, characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC), pheochromocytoma, multiple mucosal neuromas, intestinal ganglioneuromas and marfanoid habitus (PMID: 22584710, 24561444).

The RET L633_C634dup mutation is located in the cysteine-rich portion of the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (PMID: 10918602). Expression of this mutation in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased downstream pathway activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 10918602).

The RET C630R mutation is located in the cysteine-rich domain of RET. Expression of this mutation into NIH3T3 cells induces transformation and activation of RET as demonstrated by higher levels of phospho-tyrosine. This mutation is thought to disrupt the transport of RET to the plasma membrane or its maturation (PMID: 9230192). The activity of this mutant is 3-5 fold lower than that of RET with a codon 634 mutation.

The RET E768D mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating, as measured by colony formation, though likely less activating than the RET C634R mutation (PMID: 10445857).

The RET V804G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating, as expression of this variant with the RET C634R mutation decreased its kinase activity and its transforming ability (PMID: 15184865).

The RET S765P mutation is located in the protein's kinase domain. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is inactivating, as measured by abolished kinase activity in vitro (PMID: 11438491).

The RET K603Q mutation is located in the cystein-rich extracellular domain of the RET protein. This mutation has been found in familial medullary and papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) (PMID: 15277225, 11746981). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is activating, as measured by increased kinase activity and cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 15277225).

The RET E511K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been detected in the germline of individuals with inherited medullary thyroid cancer (PMID: 20103606, 21551259). In vitro studies in fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation is activating as evidenced by elevated receptor phosphorylation levels and its effect on downstream ERK signaling and its transforming ability (PMID: 20103606, 21551259). In reporter assays, cells were sensitive to sorafenib (PMID: 21551259).

The NCOA4-RET fusion protein combines the N-terminus of NCOA4 with the C-terminus of RET, preserving the kinase domain of RET. This fusion protein has been found in patients with papillary thyroid cancer (PMID: 34237031), sporadic microsatellite instability-high colorectal cancers (PMID: 30279230), lung cancer (PMID: 23150706), pediatric lipofibromatosis-like neural tumors (LPF-NT) (PMID: 31219820) and breast cancer (PMID: 30446652). Expression of this fusion protein in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it was activating as shown by increased colony formation and pathway activation compared to expression of RET alone (PMID: 30279230). Expression of this mutation in drosophila demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased EMT and cell migration compared to wildtype RET (PMID: 27626672). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that the NCOA4-RET fusion is constitutively activated and induces transformation of non-tumorigenic cells as measured by cell viability assay and xenograft tumor formation, which can be inhibited with the RET inhibitor cabozantinib (PMID: 30446652). A patient with metastatic breast carcinoma and a patient with lipofibromatosis, both harboring the NCOA4-RET fusion, responded to the RET inhibitors cabozantinib and selpercatinib, respectively (PMID: 30446652, 32923911).

The RET L790F mutation is found at the tyrosine kinase domain and it affects the ATP binding by the RET intercellular domain and may enhance transition to the active conformation (PMID: 15753368, 20444924). Germline mutations at this residue are associated with familial medullary thyroid carcinoma (FMTC) and multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2A (MEN2A) which are usually led by heritable activating mutation of RET (PMID: 15753368). This mutation needs to be further characterized in vitro and in vivo.

The RET R886W mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified as a germline variant in patients with sporadic medullary thyroid carcinoma (PMID: 21551259). In vitro studies in fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that this mutation is activating as evidenced by elevated receptor phosphorylation levels and its effect on downstream ERK signaling and its transforming ability (PMID: 21551259). In a reporter assay, cells expressing the R886W mutation were sensitive to sorafenib (PMID: 21551259).

The RET R833C mutation lies in the kinase domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrated that it is likely activating, as measured by tumor formation in mice (PMID: 21810974). However, this mutation did not confer invasion potential, and only weakly activated the kinase activity of the protein (PMID: 21810974).

The RET D631Y mutation is located adjacent to the cysteine-rich domain of the protein. Expression of this variant in NIH3T3 cells demonstrate that it is activating, as measured by increased foci formation compared to wildtype RET (PMID: 10049754). In vitro studies with COS7 cells expressing RET D631Y demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased colony formation and migration and increased phosphorylation of RET, AKT and PI3K compared to wildtype (PMID: 34905813).

The RET G810C mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, this mutation was identified as a secondary resistance mutation in a patient with lung adenocarcinoma harboring the KIF5B-RET fusion after treatment with selpercatinib (PMID: 35304457). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation results in steric hindrance to RET inhibitors due to the bulky residue substitution (PMID: 29650534).

The EML4-RET fusion results from the fusion of the N-terminal domain of EML4 with the C-terminal domain of RET. While this fusion has not been functionally characterized, other RET fusions have been shown to be activating and suggest that the EML4-RET fusion is also likely activating (PMID: 22327623, 25064355). A patient with EML4-RET fusion-positive lung cancer with brain and leptomeningeal metastases who progressed on the RET inhibitor RXDX-105 had a clincal response to LOXO-292 followed by a confirmed radiologic response and a confirmed partial response in the brain (Abstract: Guo et al. JCO PO, 2019. https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.19.00021).

The RET C634R mutation is located in the cysteine-rich domain of RET. Expression of this mutation into NIH3T3 cells induces transformation and activation of RET as demonstrated by higher levels of phospho-tyrosine. Expression of the C634R mutant induced the highest transforming activity in comparison with other cysteine mutations at codons 609, 611, 618, 620 and 630. This mutation is being thought to disrupt the transport of RET to the plasma membrane or is maturation (PMID: 9230192). RET C634 mutations are correlated with the development of MEN2A, as they are the most frequent mutations in MEN2A (about 80%).
