The ERBB3 T355I mutation is located in the receptor L domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in biliary tract cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29712892). In vitro studies with MCF-7 cells expressing ERBB3 T355I demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation and downstream signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 29963236).

The ERBB3 D297H mutation is located in the Furin-like region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in bladder cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29180607). Although not functionally characterized, in vitro studies with FaDu cells expressing ERBB3 D297H demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with kinase inhibitor neratinib as measured by decreased cell viability (PMID: 33473169).

The ERBB3 K329T mutation is located in the Furin-like region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with MCF-7 and T47D cells expressing ERBB3 K329T demonstrate that the mutation is likely neutral as measured by proliferation and activation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 29963236).

The ERBB3 A1131T mutation is located in the enzymatically inactive kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has not been functionally characterized; however, computational modeling of this mutation demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by disruption of protein stability (PMID: 23741632).

The ERBB3 N126K mutation is located in the receptor L domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 24755471). In vitro studies with HCT-15 cells expressing ERBB3 N126K demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation and ERK1/2 phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29963236).

The ERBB3 E928G mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in colonic epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation and colony formation when coexpressed with ERBB2 compared to wildtype (PMID: 23680147)(Abstract: Cabel et al. JCO PO, 2018, https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.17.00243).

The ERBB3 D297Y mutation is located in the Furin-like region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in biliary tract cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29420467). In vitro studies with MCF-7 and T47D cells expressing ERBB3 D297Y demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29963236).

The ERBB3 S846I mutation is located in the tyrosine kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and colon cancer (PMID: 29413684, 28481359, 16998794, 25344691, 27149842). Expression of this mutation in colonic epithelial and murine B-cell cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation and colony formation, especially when coexpressed with ERBB2, compared to wildtype (PMID: 23680147).

The ERBB4 D931Y mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer. Expression of this mutation in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618).

The ERBB4 R393W mutation is located in the receptor L domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 25957691). In vitro studies with gastric cancer cell lines expressing ERBB4 R393W demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation and metastasis compared to wildtype (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1). Preclinical studies suggest ERBB4 R393W is sensitive to treatment with ERBB2-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitors and pan-ERBB inhibitors (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1)

The ERBB4 R106H mutation is located in the receptor L domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 33262464). In vitro studies with gastric cancer cell lines expressing ERBB4 R106H demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation and metastasis compared to wildtype (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1). Preclinical studies suggest ERBB4 R106H is sensitive to treatment with ERBB2-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitors and pan-ERBB inhibitors (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1)

The ERBB4 T244R mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618)

The EZR-ERBB4 fusion involves the N-terminus of EZR, containing the EZR coiled-coil dimerization domain, fused to the C-terminus of ERBB4, containing the ERBB4 kinase and C-terminal domains. This mutation has been found in lung cancer. Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation, colony formation and tumor growth in xenograft models compared to empty vector. In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ERBB kinase inhibitors, lapatinib and afatinib when expressed in a murine fibroblast cell line as measured by decreased cell viability and tumor growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 24727320).

The ERBB4 S774G mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in esophageal adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23525077). In vitro studies with gastric cancer cell lines expressing ERBB4 S774G demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation and metastasis compared to wildtype (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1). Preclinical studies suggest ERBB4 S774G is sensitive to treatment with ERBB2-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitors and pan-ERBB inhibitors (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1)

The ERBB4 E542K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of ERBB4. This mutation has been found in melanoma, lung cancer and soft tissue sarcoma (PMID: 29681454, 19718025, 28481359). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, melanoma and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, anchorage-independent proliferation and dependence on ERBB4 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 E563K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 19718025). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and anchorage-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 K935I mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in simian and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, and increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618).

The ERBB4 L798R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in esophageal adenocarcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 23525077). In vitro studies with gastric cancer cell lines expressing ERBB4 L798R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased proliferation and metastasis compared to wildtype (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1). Preclinical studies suggest ERBB4 L798R is sensitive to treatment with ERBB2-specific tyrosine kinase inhibitors and pan-ERBB inhibitors (Abstract: Zeng et al. Abstract #0177, IDDF 2020. https://gut.bmj.com/content/69/Suppl_2/A22.1)

ERBB4 fusions typically involve the N-terminus of another protein fused to the C-terminus of ERBB4, containing the ERBB4 kinase domain. These fusions have been found in lung cancer. Expression of a fusion protein in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased pathway activation, colony formation and tumor growth in a xenograft model (PMID: 24727320).

The ERBB4 R1275W mutation is located in the intracellular C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in bladder cancer (PMID: 28481359). Expression of this mutation a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 24119685).

The ERBB4 T926M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colon cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in a breast cancer cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19098003).

The ERBB4 S303Y mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in colon, lung and penile cancer and is analogous to the ERBB2 S310 residue (PMID: 26517354, 28481359, 27135912). This mutation has not yet been functionally characterized but is predicted to be oncogenic based on structural analogy to ERBB2.

The ERBB4 D843N mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26343386, 28481359, 26214590). Expression of this mutation demonstrates that it is inactivating as measured by loss of protein activity compared to wildtype; however, it is still able to activate other members of the ERBB family upon dimerization (PMID: 20022944).

The ERBB4 E452K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, melanoma and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, anchorage-independent proliferation and dependence on ERBB4 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 Y285C mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947, 27923066). Expression of this mutation in simian and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, and increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618).

The ERBB4 H618P mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618)

The ERBB4 V348L mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and lung cancer (PMID: 27034166, 18948947). Expression of this mutation in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618)

The ERBB4 N181S mutation is located with the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618)

The ERBB4 R544W mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and anchorage-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 E836K mutation is located the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 19718025). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation and anchorage-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 D595V mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in simian and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, and increased cell proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 26050618).

The ERBB4 S303F mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in cell proliferation or colony formation compared to wildtype. In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ERBB2 inhibitor lapatinib but sensitive to copanlisib, afatinib and trastuzumab when expressed in breast cancer cell lines as measured by cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 30023006).

The ERBB4 E872K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer and melanoma (PMID: 19718025, 16187281). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, melanoma and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, anchorage-independent proliferation and dependence on ERBB4 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025).

The ERBB4 R306S mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in lung cancer (PMID: 18948947). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ligand-independent protein activation compared to wildtype but did not have any effect on ligand-dependent activation (PMID: 26050618)

The ERBB4 E317K mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioblastoma (PMID: 30044378). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney, glioblastoma, melanoma and murine fibroblast cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation, anchorage-independent proliferation and dependence on ERBB4 expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 19718025, 30044378).

The FUS-ERG fusion joins the N-terminal RNA-binding domain of FUS with the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of ERG. In vitro studies with human hematopoietic cells expressing this fusion protein demonstrate that FUS-ERG is activating as measured by an increase in cell proliferation, altered myeloid differentiation and self-renewal capacity compared to hematopoietic cells not expressing the fusion (PMID: 9653171, 8187069, 7970732).

The ERBB4 G936R mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 21499247, 19718025). This mutation has not been functionally characterized; however, computational modeling of this mutation demonstrated that it is likely activating (PMID: 21701703).

ERG fusions generally arise from translocations that fuse the 5' portion of a protein to exon 4 of ERG and result in ERG overexpression (PMID: 23625457, 19649210). These fusions have been reported in patients with prostate cancer in which the N-terminal gene fusion typically involves genes that are regulated by androgen and estrogen receptors (PMID: 20585344). In vitro studies with prostate cancer cells overexpressing ERG demonstrate that ERG fusions are likely activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to normal ERG expression levels (PMID: 18245377).

The EWSR1-ERG fusion encodes a chimeric protein with the N-terminal RNA-binding domain of EWSR1 and the C-terminal DNA-binding domain of ERG (PMID: 8162068). The EWSR1 (Ewing sarcoma breakpoint region 1) gene encodes the EWS protein. EWSR1-ERG has been poorly studied as compared to the more prevalent and highly homologous EWSR1-FLI1 fusion. Preclinical experiments have demonstrated that EWSR1-FLI1 is associated with malignant transformation of mesenchymal stem cells (PMID: 16357154). EWSR1-FLI1 causes transcriptional dysregulation by binding to and opening GGAA repetitive elements in the chromatin to activate transcription and conversely, binding to canonical ETS binding GGAA sites and suppressing transcription at these sites (PMID: 25453903). The EWSR1-ERG fusion, t(21;22)(q22;q12), is the second most common fusion product in the Ewing Sarcoma family of tumors (PMID: 8162068). ERG encodes a nuclear protein involved in platelet adhesion, hematopoeisis and megakaryocyte differentiation and maturation (PMID: 10749119, 18500345 ).

The TMPRSS2-ERG fusion is a result of a chromosomal translocation between the 5' region of TMPRSS2 fusing to exon 4 of ERG, resulting in overexpression of ERG (PMID: 17043636). This fusion protein has been identified in prostate cancer (PMID: 28849022). In vitro studies with prostate cancer cells overexpressing ERG demonstrate that the TMPRSS2-ERG fusion protein is likely activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to normal ERG expression levels (PMID: 18245377). Preclinical studies with VCaP xenograft mouse models expressing TMPRSS2-ERG demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with RGD-peptide-coated liposomal siRNA nanovectors as measured by suppressed tumor growth and enhanced efficacy of docetaxel chemotherapy (PMID: 31614005).

ESR1 fusions typically involve the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of another protein. These mutations have been found in breast cancer. Expression of these fusions in embryonic kidney or breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that they are activating as measured by increased ESR1 protein activity, anchorage-independent colony formation and tumor growth in xenograft models (PMID: 25099679, 24055055, 29360925).

The ESR1 L536Q mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24185510).

The ESR1-DAB2 fusion involves the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of DAB2. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 29360925). Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ESR1 protein activity compared to truncated ESR1 alone (PMID: 29360925).

The ESR1 Y537C mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 24398047). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 9500442, 24398047, 24185510). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to ESR1 inhibitors tamoxifen and fulvestrant when expressed in an embryonic kidney cell line as measured by sustained protein activity upon drug treatment (PMID: 24185510).

The ESR1 S432L mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707).

The ESR1 T585M mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in colorectal cancer (PMID: 29316426). In silico analysis suggests that the mutation is likely damaging (PMID: 27994185).

The ESR1 G442R mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrioid carcinoma (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with MCF7 cells expressing ESR1 G442R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased dimer formation and hormone-independent transcriptional activity and cellular growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 37883178). Preclinical studies of this mutation demonstrate wildtype-comparable sensitivity to fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, tamoxifen and raloxifene (PMID: 37883178).

ESR1 amplification results in overexpression of the protein. This alteration has been found in breast and ovarian cancer (PMID: 22020208, 18690166). Two separate analyses of 175 and 132 patients with breast cancer, respectively, demonstrated that ESR1 amplification is associated with clinical responses to the ESR1 antagonist, tamoxifen (PMID: 23099803, 19320640). However, another analysis of 120 patients with breast cancer demonstrated that ESR1 amplification is associated with resistance to tamoxifen (PMID: 20556506).

The ESR1-SOX9 fusion involves the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of SOX9. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 29360925). Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ESR1 protein activity compared to truncated ESR1 alone (PMID: 29360925).

The ESR1 L536P mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 27986707). Expression of this mutation in a breast cancer cell line demonstrated that it is activating, as measured by increased ligand-independent transcriptional activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707, 15282324, 1630819).

The ESR1 Y537S mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 24185512). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, cell proliferation and tumor growth in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 8923465, 9398213, 11914066, 26836308, 24185512, 30733228). In vitro and in vivo studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ESR1 inhibitors tamoxifen and fulvestrant, but is sensitive to AZD9496 when expressed in embryonic kidney and breast cancer cell lines as measured by protein activity, cell proliferation, and tumor growth upon drug treatment (PMID: 24185512, 24185510, 27986707). Among 195 patients with estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer who were treated with the CDK4/6 inhibitor palbociclib plus fulvestrant, the ESR1 Y537S mutation was found at a significantly higher percentage in post-treatment samples compared to pre-treatment samples (PMID: 30206110).

This ESR1-CCDC170 fusion involves the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of CCDC170. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 25099679). Expression of this fusion in breast epithelial and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation, cell motility, anchorage-independent growth and tumor growth in xenograft models compared to empty vector (PMID: 25099679).

The ESR1 Y537D mutation is located in the ligand binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with ER+ MCF7 cells expressing ESR1 Y537D demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by transient transcription activity in the absence of estradiol compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707).

The ESR1 F461V mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 30537512, 30205045). In vitro studies with MCF7 cells expressing ESR1 F461V demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased dimer formation and hormone-independent transcriptional activity and cellular growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 37883178). Preclinical studies of this mutation demonstrate wildtype-comparable sensitivity to fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, tamoxifen and raloxifene (PMID: 37883178).

The ESR1-YAP1 fusion involves the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of YAP1, lacking YAP1 functional domains and the ESR1 ligand-binding domain but retaining the ESR1 DNA binding domain. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this fusion in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased cell proliferation compared to vector control. In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation may be resistant to fulvestrant when expressed in breast cancer cells as measured by sustained cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 24055055).

The ESR1 L469V mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707).

The ESR1 L536R mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 24185512). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 24185512).

The ESR1-AKAP12 fusion protein results from a fusion between the 5' end of ESR1 and the 3' end of AKAP12. Although not functionally characterized per se, the ESR1-AKAP12 fusion was identified in samples from patients with breast cancer that were resistant to letrozole aromatase inhibitor treatment (PMID: 31106278).

The ESR1 L536H is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in an endometrial cancer cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 15159406).

The ESR1 K303R mutation is located in the ER hinge domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 23236557). In vitro studies with ESR1-negative MDA-MB-453 cells expressing ESR1 K303R demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by induced chromatin opening at the FOXA1 binding region and disruption of target gene regulation compared to wildtype (PMID: 36436079).

The ESR1 E380Q mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in a hamster ovary cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 8114756, 9259327). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ESR1 inhibitor tamoxifen when expressed in hamster ovary cells as measured by increased protein activity upon drug treatment compared to wildtype (PMID: 8114756).

The ESR1 D538G mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 24185512). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, cell proliferation and tumor growth in xenograft models (PMID: 24398047, 24185512, 24185510, 24217577, 26836308, 30733228). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is resistant to the ESR1 inhibitors tamoxifen and fulvestrant when expressed in embryonic kidney and breast cancer cell lines as measured by sustained protein activity upon drug treatment (PMID: 24398047, 24185512, 24185510, 24217577).

The ESR1 V534E mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is neutral as measured by no change in protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707).

The ESR1 Y537N mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 24185512). Expression of this mutation in embryonic kidney and breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 9500442, 11322512, 24398047, 24185510, 9102207). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is resistant to the ESR1 inhibitors tamoxifen and fulvestrant when expressed in an embryonic kidney cell line as measured by sustained protein activity and proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 24185510, 24398047).

The ESR1 V422del mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 30820448). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, dimer formation and cellular proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 27986707, 37883178). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the ESR1 inhibitor fulvestrant when expressed in a breast cancer cell line as measured by decreased protein activity and cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 27986707). Preclinical studies of this mutation demonstrate wildtype-comparable sensitivity to fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, tamoxifen and raloxifene (PMID: 37883178).

The ESR1-MTHFD1L fusion protein results from an inframe fusion between exon 3 of ESR1 and exon 21 of MTHFD1L. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with metastatic breast cancer harboring the ESR1-MTHFD1L fusion was treated with fulvestrant plus palbociclib and achieved complete remission (PMID: 36493359).

The ESR1 L540Q mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer (PMID: 28481359). There is conflicting evidence on the oncogenic and biological effect of the mutation. In vitro studies with T47D and MCF-7 breast cancer cells and in vivo studies with nude mice expressing ESR1 L540Q demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by dominant negative inhibition of wildtype ESR1, inhibition of cell growth, induced apoptosis and induced tumor regression compared to wildtype (PMID: 11788792, 7628351). In contrast, other in vitro studies with 3T3 mouse fibroblast cells and ER-negative T47D:C4:2 cells expressing ESR1 L540Q demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased ligand-specific transcriptional activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 7531820, 12496244).

The ESR1-GYG1 fusion involves the N-terminus of ESR1 fused to the C-terminus of GYG1. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 29360925). Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ESR1 protein activity compared to truncated ESR1 alone (PMID: 29360925).

The ETV6 S22N mutation is located in the N-terminal pointed (PNT) domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely neutral as measured by similar repression of gene expression and similar nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is benign (PMID: 35586967).

The ESR1 S463P mutation is located in the ligand-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer. Expression of this mutation in breast cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, dimer formation and cellular growth compared to wildtype (PMID: 24185512, 37883178). Preclinical studies of this mutation demonstrate wildtype-comparable sensitivity to fulvestrant, elacestrant, camizestrant, tamoxifen and raloxifene (PMID: 37883178).

The ESR1-PLEKHG1 fusion protein results from a fusion between exon 6 of ESR1 and exon 14 of PLEKHG1. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with metastatic breast cancer harboring the ESR1-PLEKHG1 and ESR1-CCDC170 fusions was treated with fulvestrant plus abemaciclib and demonstrated stable disease for 4 months (PMID: 36493359).

The ETV6 R369W mutation is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) DNA binding domain of the ETV6 protein. This mutation has been found in families with inherited thrombocytopenia and pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 27365488, 26522332, 25581430). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of repression of gene expression and loss of nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). It is suggested that this mutation dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 retaining it in the cytoplasm and affecting its function through a dominant negative effect (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is inactivating based on its location in the protein (PMID: 27365488, 35586967).

The ETV6 R396G mutation is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) DNA binding domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of repression of gene expression and loss of nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). It is suggested that this mutation dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 retaining it in the cytoplasm and affecting its function through a dominant negative effect (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is damaging (PMID: 35586967).

The ETV6 Q347P mutation is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) DNA binding domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of repression of gene expression and loss of nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). It is suggested that this mutation dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 retaining it in the cytoplasm and affecting its function through a dominant negative effect (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is damaging (PMID: 35586967).

The ETV6 R369Q mutation has been observed in affected members of families with inherited thrombocytopenia and pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (PMID: 26522332, 25581430). This residue is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) domain of the protein, a conserved domain that binds DNA. R369 is predicted to be involved in both inter- and intramolecular interactions which would be perturbed by a bulky substitution (PMID: 27365488). This mutation reduces the protein's DNA-binding ability in an in vitro assay and when expressed in human cervical cancer cells alters intracellular localization and has a dominant negative effect in an assay of trans-repression (PMID: 25581430, 26102509). Additionally, the mutation reduces the proliferation of isolated human hematopoietic progenitor cells and confers a transcriptional profile distinct from the wildtype protein when expressed in a myeloid cell line (PMID: 25581430).

The ETV6 N385_R418del mutation is located in the ETS domain of the protein. This alteration has been identified as a germline mutation present in families with familial platelet disorders with predisposition to leukemia (PMID: 25807284). ETV6 reporter assays demonstrated that this alteration led to decreased repression of gene expression (PMID: 25807284). ETV6 N385_R418del dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 suggesting that this mutation functions as a dominant negative (PMID: 25807284).

The ETV6 H224Q mutation is located in the central regulatory domain (CRD) domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely neutral as measured by similar repression of gene expression and similar nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is benign (PMID: 35586967).

The ETV6 R399H mutation is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) DNA binding domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of repression of gene expression and loss of nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). It is suggested that this mutation dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 retaining it in the cytoplasm and affecting its function through a dominant negative effect (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is damaging (PMID: 35586967).

The ETV6 P214L mutation occurs in the central domain of ETV6. This alteration has been identified as a germline mutation present in families with familial platelet disorders with predisposition to leukemia. Expression of the ETV6 P216L mutation in cultured megakaryocytes resulted in an expansion of immature platelet cells and loss of nuclear localization. ETV6 reporter assays demonstrated that this alteration led to decreased repression of gene expression. ETV6 P214L dimerizes with wild-type ETV6 suggesting that this mutation functions as a dominant negative (PMID: 25807284).

The ETV6 W380R mutation is located in the E26 transformation-specific (ETS) DNA binding domain of the ETV6 protein. In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by loss of repression of gene expression and loss of nuclear expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 35586967). It is suggested that this mutation dimerizes with wildtype ETV6 retaining it in the cytoplasm and affecting its function through a dominant negative effect (PMID: 35586967). In silico analysis predicts that this mutation is damaging (PMID: 35586967).

ETV6 deletion mutations typically result in the loss of protein expression. In vivo studies with ETV6-knockdown mice demonstrate that loss of ETV6 is inactivating as measured by increased metastasis and tumor progression compared to vector control (PMID: 29455655).

The FANCA R435C mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 9371798, 10090479, 15523645, 28102861, 29098742, 24037726). Expression of this mutation in a Fanconi anemia fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it was inactivating, as measured by decreased protein expression and activity and the failure to rescue cells from treatment with a chemotherapeutic agent compared to wildtype (PMID: 11739169, 12444097).

ETV6 truncating mutations typically result in the loss of protein function. In vivo studies with ETV6-knockdown mice demonstrate that loss of ETV6 is inactivating as measured by increased metastasis and tumor progression compared to vector control (PMID: 29455655).

The ETV6 R418G mutation occurs in the ETS domain of ETV6. This alteration has been identified as a germline mutation present in families with familial platelet disorders with predisposition to leukemia. Expression of the ETV6 R418G mutation in cultured megakaryocytes resulted in an expansion of immature platelet cells and loss of nuclear localization. ETV6 reporter assays demonstrated that this alteration led to decreased repression of gene expression. ETV6 R418G dimerizes with wild-type ETV6 suggesting that this mutation functions as a dominant negative (PMID: 25807284).

The FANCA R1117G mutation is located in the FAAP20 binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 9371798, 22778927, 29098742). Expression of this mutation in a Fanconi anemia fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating, as measured by decreased protein expression, decreased activity and mislocalization of the protein compared to wildtype (PMID: 10373536, 11739169).

FANCA truncating mutations can produce several forms of C-terminally truncated proteins and have been shown to result in the complete loss of FANCA protein expression (PMID: 21273304). These mutations have been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 12827451). In vitro studies demonstrated that loss of FANCA results in sensitization of Fanconi anemia fibroblast cells to DNA cross-linking agents such as mitomycin C when as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 11739169, 12637330).

The FANCA Y510C mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 16720839). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer and lymphoblast cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased interaction with binding partners and aberrant cellular localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 16720839).

The FANCA R1055L mutation is located in the C-terminus of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 16720839). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer and lymphoblast cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased interaction with binding partners and aberrant cellular localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 16720839).

The FANCA H492R mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 12444097). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer and lymphoblast cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased interaction with binding partners and aberrant cellular localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 16720839). In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation is hypersensitive to the chemotherapeutic agent mitomycin C when expressed in fibroblasts as measured by cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 12444097).

This FANCA W183A mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a Fanconi anemia cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by the failure to rescue cells from treatment with a chemotherapeutic agent compared to wildtype; although expression in Fanconi anemia and embryonic kidney cell lines also demonstrated no change in protein stability or localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 11161829).

The FANCA L274P mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 16720839). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer and lymphoblast cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased interaction with binding partners and aberrant cellular localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 16720839).

The FANCA S1088F mutation is located in the partial leucine zipper region of the protein. This mutation has been found in prostate cancer. Expression of this mutation in a Fanconi anemia fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it was inactivating, as measured by decreased DNA repair foci in response to crosslinking agents compared to wildtype. In vitro studies demonstrated that this mutation confers increased sensitivity to the DNA damaging agents cisplatin and mitomycin C and to the PARP inhibitor olaparib when expressed in a Fanconi anemia fibroblast cell line as measured by cell viability upon drug treatment. One patient with metastatic prostate cancer harboring this mutation along with loss of heterozygosity of FANCA responded to cisplatin (PMID: 28864460).

The FANCA L210R mutation is located in the BRCA binding region of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 16720839). Expression of this mutation in breast cancer and lymphoblast cell lines demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased interaction with binding partners and aberrant cellular localization compared to wildtype (PMID: 16720839).

The FANCA S858R mutation is located at a phosphoserine site of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia and has been identified in a large percentage of the population. Endogenous expression of this mutation in Fanconi anemia samples demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by reduced protein expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 12955722).

Truncation mutations in FANCC produce C-terminally deleted FANCC proteins and their consequent inactivation. FANCC inactivation is know to be associated with Fanconi Anemia (PMID: 11520787). FANCC inactivation in a hepatocellular carcinoma cell line was found to confer sensitivity to DNA-interstrand crosslinking agents (PMID: 20509860). One study suggests that the FANCC protein may cooperate with BRCA2/Rad51 in homologous repair (PMID:16687415) and its loss is oncogenic. While Rad51 and FancD2 form colocalizing subnuclear foci independently of each other, it is clear that FANCC proteins are involved in homologous repair, likely in parallel with the Rad51-pathway.

The FGFR1 D128V mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 D128V demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

FANCA deletion results in loss of the FANCA protein. These mutations are found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 12827451). FANCA deletions in acute myeloid leukemia samples resulted in reduced protein expression compared to control samples (PMID: 14749703). In vitro studies demonstrated that loss of FANCA results in sensitization of Fanconi anemia fibroblast cells to DNA cross-linking agents such as mitomycin C when as measured by decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 11739169, 12637330).

The FGFR1 P514L mutation (also called P483L) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 P514L demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 P184S mutation (also called P150S) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 P184S demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 S269N mutation (also called S238N) is located in the Ig-like C2-type II domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR S269N demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1-PDE4DIP fusion is a fusion of the C-terminal end of the FGFR1 gene with the N-terminal end of the PDE4DIP gene. Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-PDE4DIP fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a Phase II trial, a patient with pancreatic cancer harboring FGFR1-PDE4DIP was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated stable disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1 G734S mutation (also called G703S) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 G734S demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 A635T mutation (also called A604T) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 A635T demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 E498K mutation (also called E467K) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 E498K demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 A154D mutation (also called A121D) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 A154D demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 S467F mutation (also called S436F) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR S467F demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 K687E mutation (also called K656E) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 K687E demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467). Expression of this mutation in a murine fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased colony formation compared to wildtype (PMID: 15509736). Preclinical studies with Ba/F3 cells and NIH3T3 cells expressing FGFR1 K687E demonstrated sensitivity to treatment with HQP1351 and futibatinib, as measured by inhibition of cell growth, and resistance to treatment with TKI258, as measured by sustained cell growth (PMID: 34114373, 34272467). In a Phase II trial, two patients with recurrent glioma harboring FGFR1 K687E were treated with infigratinib and demonstrated partial response and stable response with a progression-free survival of 21.9 months and 13.2 months, respectively (PMID: 35344029). In the Phase II FIGHT-207 trial examining pemigatinib treatment with patients harboring FGFR1 K687E, two patients with central nervous system tumors demonstrated progressive disease and partial response with a progression-free survival of 5 months and 10 months, respectively (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1 T59I mutation (also called T26I) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 T59I demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 V695L mutation (also called V664L) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 V695L demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR N224fs*8 mutation (also called N193fs*8) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR N224fs*8 demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1-MITF fusion is a fusion of the C-terminal end of the FGFR1 gene with the N-terminal end of the MITF gene. Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-MITF fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a Phase II trial, a patient with a central nervous system tumor harboring FGFR1-MITF was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1-WHSC1L1 fusion is a fusion of the C-terminal end of the FGFR1 gene with the N-terminal end of the WHSC1L1 gene. Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-WHSC1L1 fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a Phase II trial, a patient with cancer of unknown primary harboring FGFR1-WHSC1L1 was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1 N546K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in papillary glioneuronal tumor (PMID: 24777483). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 N546K demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation compared to wildtype (PMID: 29533785). In vitro studies with Rat-1 cells expressing FGFR1 N546K also demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased kinase activity and transforming potential due to auto-phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 19224897). Preclinical studies with NIH3T3 cells expressing FGFR1 N546K demonstrated resistance to treatment with erdafitinib, AZD4547, infigratinib, futibatinib, pemigatinib and TKI258 as measured by sustained tumor growth and cellular proliferation following treatment (PMID: 34272467). In a Phase I trial, a patient with pilocytic astrocytoma harboring FGFR1 N546K was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated partial response (PMID: 35176457). In a Phase II trial, three patients with breast cancer harboring FGFR1 N546K were treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1-ACVR1 fusion is a fusion of the C-terminal end of the FGFR1 gene with the N-terminal end of the ACVR1 gene. Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-ACVR1 fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a Phase II trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring FGFR1-ACVR1 was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The FGFR1 R840Q mutation (also called R809Q) is located in the C-terminus of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R840Q demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 T371M mutation (also called T340M) is located in the N-terminus of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 T371M demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 S619T mutation (also called S588T) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 S619T demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The CUX1-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of CUX1 fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1. This mutation has been found in stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 21330321). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased FGFR1 activation, downstream pathway activation and growth factor-independent proliferation compared to vector control cells (PMID: 21330321).

The FGFR1 V782A mutation (also called V751A) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 V782A demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1OP-FGFR1 fusion (sometimes called FOP-FGFR1) involves the N-terminus of FGFR1OP fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1. This mutation has been found in stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 21330321). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation and growth factor-independent cell proliferation compared to vector control (PMID: 11689702). In vitro studies demonstrate that this fusion is modestly sensitive to the FGFR inhibitor ponatinib when endogenously expressed in a myeloid leukemia cell line as measured by moderately decreased cell proliferation upon drug treatment (PMID: 29720732).

The FGFR1 E623G mutation (also called E592G) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 E623G demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 K687M mutation (also called K656M) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 K687M demonstrated this mutation is activating as measured by increased transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 R677W mutation (also called R646W) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R677W demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 V592M mutation (sometimes called V561M) is located in the ATP-binding pocket of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in vitro and in a simian fibroblast cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 15157880, 25686244).

The ZNF198-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of ZNF198 fused to the C-terminal of FGFR1. This mutation has been found in stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 20226962). Expression of this fusion in a murine B-cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased kinase activation, oligomerization and growth factor-independent proliferation compared to vector control (PMID: 10935490, 10887137).

The FGFR1 D166N mutation (also called D133N) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 D166N demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1-TACC1 fusion results from the fusion between the C-terminal end of FGFR1, retaining the intact kinase domain, with the N-terminal end of TACC1. This fusion has been identified in extraventricular neurocytoma and glioma (PMID: 29978331, 34734147). Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-TACC1 fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a Phase I trial, a patient with glioblastoma harboring FGFR1-TACC1 was treated with futibatinib and demonstrated partial response with a progression-free survival of 7.0 months (PMID: 34551969).

The FGFR1-EBF2 fusion protein results from fusion between intron 7 of EBF2 and exon 18 of FGFR1, retaining the kinase domain of FGFR1.  Fusions of FGFR1 retaining the kinase domain have been shown to be oncogenic, and therefore the FGFR1-EBF2 fusion is considered likely oncogenic (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702). In a case report, a pediatric patient with spindle cell sarcoma harboring the FGFR1-EBF2 fusion was treated with erdafitinib and demonstrated tumor regression (PMID: 36446043).

The FGFR1 R476W mutation (also called R445W) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R476W demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FN1-FGFR1 fusion results from an in-frame fusion of the 3′ end of exon 28 of FN1 and the 5′ end of exon 5 of FGFR1. This fusion has been identified in phosphaturic mesenchymal tumors (PMID: 25319834). Immunohistochemical analysis of patient samples harboring FN1-FGFR1 demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by increased expression of FGFR1 compared to non-phosphaturic mesenchymal tumor samples (PMID: 27443518). The FN1-FGFR1 fusion is predicted to serve as a ligand that is secreted, binds and subsequently activates FGFR1 to create an autocrine loop (PMID: 27443518).

The FGFR1 R220C mutation (also called R189C) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R220C demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The ZMYM2-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of ZMYM2 fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1, containing the FGFR1 kinase domain. This mutation has been found in myeloproliferative neoplasms (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in human CD34+ progenitor cells demonstrated that it was activating as measured by the development of acute myeloid leukemia upon engraftment of cells into mice (PMID: 29720732). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is moderately sensitive to the FGFR inhibitor BGJ398 when endogenously expressed in a murine stem cell leukemia/lymphoma cell line as measured by a moderate decrease in cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 29720732).

The FGFR1 M487I mutation (also known as M456I) is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. Although not functionally characterized per se, a patient with a cancer of unknown primary harboring FGFR1 M487I was treated with pemigatinib and demonstrated stable disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The CEP110-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of CEP110 to the C-terminus of FGFR1. This mutation has been found in stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 20226962). Expression of this mutation in murine and simian fibroblast cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by oligomerization, FGFR1 activation and ligand-independent kinase activation compared to vector control (PMID: 10688839).

The FGFR1 E701K mutation (also called E670K) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. Structural modeling of this mutation and expression of this mutation in zebrafish embryos demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by disrupted protein conformation and the inability to rescue an FGFR1 deficiency compared to wildtype (PMID: 19733072).

The CNTRL-FGFR1 fusion is a fusion between the CNTRL gene and a portion of the FGFR1 gene containing the kinase domain. Expression of the CNTRL-FGFR1 fusion protein in human CD34+ progenitor cells grafted in immunocompromised mice demonstrated that it is activating as the mice developed acute myeloid leukemia with high MYC expression. The mouse-derived stem cell leukemia/lymphoma cell lines, CEP2A and CEP5A, which endogenously express the CNTRL-FGFR1 fusion protein, had upregulated levels of MYC similar to other models expressing chimeric FGFR1 fusion proteins. Treatment of the CEP2A cell line with the FGFR1 inhibitor, BGJ398, resulted in the downregulation of MYC and a moderate decrease in proliferation (PMID: 29720732).

The FGFR1 S158L mutation (also called S125L) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 S158L demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 R281W mutation (also called R250W) is located in the Ig-like C2-type II domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R281W demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 A294V mutation (sometimes called A263V) is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 26826182). Expression of this variant in embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely neutral, as it exhibited no change in kinase activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 26826182).

The BAG4-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of BAG4 fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1. This fusion has been identified in non-small cell lung cancer (PMID: 24850843). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing BAG4-FGFR1 demonstrate this fusion is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467). In a Phase II trial, a patient with non-small cell lung cancer harboring BAG4-FGFR1 was treated with pemigatnib and demonstrated progressive disease (Abstract: Rodon et al. Abstract# CT016. AACR 2023. https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/83/8_Supplement/CT016/725419).

The BCR-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of BCR, containing the BCR oligomerization domain, fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1, containing the FGFR1 kinase domain. This mutation has been found in stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 20226962). Expression of this mutation in a murine B-cell line and in human CD34+ progenitor cells demonstrated that it is activating as measured by growth factor-independent cell proliferation compared to vector control and the development of acute myeloid leukemia upon transplantation of cells into mice (PMID: 11739186, 29720732). In vitro studies demonstrate that this fusion is sensitive to the FGFR inhibitors BGJ398 and ponatinib when expressed in hematopoietic cell lines as measured by reduced cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 29720732).

The FGFR1 D128N mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 D128N demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 T174R mutation (also called T141R) is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 T174R demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The ERLIN2-FGFR1 fusion involves the N-terminus of ERLIN2 fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 23558953). Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased ligand-independent protein activation compared to vector control (PMID: 23558953).

The FGFR1 T350A mutation (also called T319A) is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR T350A demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 K687* mutation (also called K656*) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 K687* demonstrated this mutation is inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 N577K mutation (also called N546K) is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse leptomeningeal tumors (PMID: 27061725). Expression of this mutation in vitro with rat and murine fibroblast cell lines and in vivo with a transgenic mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activity, proliferation, colony formation and transformed morphology compared to wildtype (PMID: 19224897, 23817572, 14602678).

The FGFR1 R506Q mutation (also called R475Q) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 R506Q demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

FGFR1 kinase domain duplication is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in glioma (PMID: 23583981). Endogenous expression of this mutation in glioma samples demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased pathway activation compared to normal brain (PMID: 23583981). In vitro studies demonstrate that this mutation is sensitive to the FGFR inhibitors BGJ398, AZD4547, ponatinib and axitinib when expressed in murine glioma cells as measured by decreased pathway activation upon drug treatment (PMID: 23583981) (Abstract: Vakil et al. Abstract# LG-64, SNO 2016. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4903541/).

The FGFR1 M487V mutation (also called M456V) is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 M487V demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

FGFR1 fusions typically involve the N-terminus of a fusion partner fused to the C-terminus of FGFR1 including the FGFR1 kinase domain, although there are some instances where the N-terminus of FGFR1 is fused to the C-terminus of a fusion partner. These mutations have been found in glioblastoma multiforme and stem cell leukemia/lymphoma (PMID: 21330321, 22837387). Expression of these fusions in various human, rat and murine cell lines demonstrated that they are activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation and increased cell proliferation compared to vector control (PMID: 22837387, 23558953, 10935490, 10887137, 10688839, 11739186, 29720732, 21330321, 11689702).

The FGFR1 A54T mutation (also called is located A21T) in the N-terminus of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 A54T demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 A299S mutation (also called A268S) is located in the Ig-like C2-type II domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 A299S demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by proliferation and transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR1 D351N mutation (also called D320N) is located in the Ig-like C2-type II domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR1 D351N demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

FGFR1 amplification results in overexpression of the protein. This mutation has been found in squamous cell lung, bladder and breast cancer (PMID: 22960745, 26451490, 24476821). In vitro studies demonstrate that FGFR1 overexpression in breast cancer cell lines promotes resistance to the ESR1 inhibitor fulvestrant as measured by sustained cell viability upon drug treatment (PMID: 31371343). A patient with FGFR1-amplified small cell lung cancer had a partial response to the FGFR-inhibitor pazopanib (Abstract: Russo et al. JCO PO, 2019. https://ascopubs.org/doi/full/10.1200/PO.19.00243).

FGFR4 amplification results in overexpression of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and lung cancer (PMID: 28572459). Overexpression of FGFR4 in multiple human cancer cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, pathway activation and cell proliferation (PMID: 25053532, 15863030, 20094046, 23344261).

The FGFR4 R707W mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 26343386). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R707W demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 C271* mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 C271* demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 D127H mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in cell lines demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased levels of downstream ERK phosphorylation compared to wildtype (PMID: 23836671).

The FGFR4 V548M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 21796119). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 V548M demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 S342F mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 28467829). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 S342F demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 G687fs*35 mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 G687fs*35 demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 G176C mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type II domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 G176C demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R80W mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in prostate cancer (PMID: 22610119). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R80W demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 N535K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in rhabdomyosarcoma (PMID: 28572459). Expression of this mutation in a murine rhabdomyosarcoma cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activation and increased tumor growth in a xenograft model (PMID: 19809159).

The FGFR4 A484V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 25839328). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 A484V demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R464W mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 26873401). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R464W demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R434Q mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in adenocarcinoma (PMID: 27149842). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R434Q demonstrated this mutation is likely neutral as measured by transformation activity and proliferation comparable to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 A749V mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 26343386). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 A749V demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 V550M mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in rhabdomyosarcoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 21412928). In vitro and in vivo studies with Ba/F3 cells and fisogatinib-resistant mice expressing FGFR4 V550M have demonstrated that the mutation is activating as measured by constitutive activation compared to wildtype (PMID: 31575540). Preclinical studies of FGFR4 V550M suggest the mutation is sensitive to pan-FGFR inhibitor LY2874455 as measured by delayed tumor growth in a xenograft model (PMID: 31575540). FGFR4 V550M has demonstrated resistance to FGFR4-specific inhibitor fisogatinib as measured by continued constitutive signaling following treatment in preclinical studies compared to wildtype (PMID: 31575540).

The FGFR4 R321W mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type III domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 24265153). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R321W demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 V550E mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in rhabdomyosarcoma (PMID: 24124571). Expression of this mutation in a murine rhabdomyosarcoma cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein activation, pathway activation and increased tumor growth in a xenograft model (PMID: 19809159).

The FGFR4 R134G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R134G demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R411fs*81 mutation is located in the cytoplasmic domain of the protein. In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R411fs*81 demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 C172G mutation is located in the extracellular domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 33126538). In silico analysis of FGFR4 C172G suggests that the mutation is activating through constitutive activation of the FGFR1 dimer state (PMID: 33126538). FGFR4 C172G is suggested to be sensitive to MEK inhibitor trametinib as measured by a patient with uveal melanoma harboring GNAQ G48L and FGFR4 C172G demonstrating stable disease after two months of treatment (PMID: 33126538).

The FGFR4 E681K mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in malignant melanoma (PMID: 28481359). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 E681K demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R59W mutation is located in the Ig-like C2-type I domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in transitional cell carcinoma (PMID: 24121792). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R59W demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).

The FGFR4 R635S mutation is located in the kinase domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in transitional cell carcinoma (PMID: 24121792). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing FGFR4 R635S demonstrated this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased proliferation and transformation activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 34272467).
