This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma and follicular lymphoma (PMID: 30802265, 33423045). In vitro studies with HeLa cells and SU-DHL4-shGNA13 UTR cells expressing GNA13 C18S demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by reduced protein stability, loss of palmitoylation, reduced pro-apoptotic function and increased cellular proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 33423045).

The GNA13 Q27H mutation is located in the N-terminal region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 23699601). In silico analysis suggests that this mutation is likely damaging (PMID: 23699601).

The GNA13 N370Y mutation is located in the C-terminal region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 23699601). In silico analysis suggests that this mutation is likely damaging (PMID: 23699601).

The GNA13 G224D mutation is located in the helical domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 23699601). In silico analysis suggests that this mutation is likely damaging (PMID: 23699601).

The GNA13 I158K mutation is located in the helical domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (PMID: 21796119). Expression of this mutation in an embryonic kidney cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein and pathway activation (PMID: 26616858).

The HDAC1 H141A mutation occurs in the histone deacetylase domain of the protein. In biochemical assays, the HDAC H141A mutation resulted in loss of deacetylase activity and reduced ability to activate HDAC2 (PMID: 19822520).

The gene S102F mutation occurs within the highly conserved gene globular domain. Expression of S102F mutant gene in mouse embryonic stem cells resulted in dramatically impaired association with chromatin relative to wildtype, suggesting that the mutation likely reduces the binding affinity and residence time of these H1 subtypes in chromatin. This in turn may compromise chromatin compaction and specific gene regulation (PMID: 24362818).

The IKZF3 Q147H mutation resides in the second zinc finger domain of the protein. Expression of this mutation in a human cell line demonstrated increased IKZF3 expression and decreased IKZF3 ubiquitination in the presence of lenalidomide therapy compared to wildtype IKZF3 (PMID: 24292625). In vitro studies in lymphoblast cell lines also demonstrated that the Q147H mutation is more resistant to lenalidomide therapy compared to wildtype IKZF3 (PMID: 24292625).

The HDAC1 K432R mutation occurs in the C-terminal of the protein. In biochemical assays, the HDAC K432R mutation resulted in reduced acetylation by p300, leading to lower activity of HDAC1 (PMID: 19822520).

Truncating mutations of HLA-A result in reduced HLA-A protein expression. Loss of HLA-A has been reported as a common characteristic of malignant cells and has been proposed to enable tumor cells to escape from cytotoxic T-lymphocyte surveillance (PMID: 15546342); however, this has yet to be functionally validated.

The HLA-A 596_619 splice mutation results in a novel transcript with a 24 base-pair deletion within exon 3 of the protein. Expression of HLA-A protein was not detected in patients harboring this mutation. While this mutation has not yet been functionally characterized, reduced levels of HLA-A is an established mechanism for tumors to evade the immune system (PMID: 16216676).

LATS1 deletion results in loss of the tumor suppressor LATS1 expression. Deletion of LATS1 in mice led to hyperplastic changes in the pituitary and the development of ovarian tumors (PMID: 9988269) which was associated with down-regulation of members of the Hippo-signaling pathway including WWTR1, STK4, STK3, LATS2 and YAP1 (PMID: 26040669, 23573293).

LATS2 truncation mutations occur throughout the gene and typically result in the loss of the protein. These mutations have been identified in multiple myeloma (PMID: 21245096). In vitro studies with LATS2-deficient multiple myeloma cells demonstrate that loss of LATS2 is inactivating as measured by dysregulation of the Hippo pathway and increased cell growth (PMID: 21245096).

Truncating mutations of LATS1 lead to several forms of C-terminally truncated proteins causing loss of tumor suppression function. Mouse models of N- terminally truncated LATS1 revealed associated mitotic defects, anchorage-independent cell growth and tumor formation in the immunocompromised animals (PMID: 23230145). Moreover, a C- terminally truncated LAT1 mouse model was shown to develop soft-tissue sarcomas and ovarian tumors (PMID: 9988269). In addition, experimental studies in Hela cells expressing these alterations suggest that LATS1 truncating mutations functions in a dominant negative manner over wild type LATS1 protein (PMID: 11850843).

Translocations involving IGH and MAF are found in patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and IGH rearrangements are predicted to be the primary initiating event in this disease (PMID: 28726797, 12576322). IGH-MAF rearrangements (t(14;16)) typically partner 3' IGH enhancer regions upstream of the MAF gene, resulting in upregulation of MAF expression (PMID: 24638926, 28726797). IGH fusion proteins are the product of altered class switch recombination during plasma cell differentiation or abnormal VDJ rearrangement (PMID: 26282654). In murine models, overexpression of MAF leads to transformation and the development of T-cell leukemias (PMID: 16424013). Additional functional experiments are required to determine the role of IGH-MAF fusions. Expression of MAF fusion proteins delineates a subgroup of MM patients that have a poor prognosis (PMID: 11877296, 28584253, 12576322).

LATS2 deletion has been found in malignant mesothelioma (PMID: 21245096). In cell lines, LATS2 homozygous deletion corresponds to loss of LATS2 protein expression, and rescue with wildtype LATS2 protein in these cells results in decreased proliferation and anchorage-independent growth compared to rescue with truncated LATS2 protein (PMID: 21245096). LATS2 loss was shown to propagate RAS-mediated transformation in cancer cells (PMID: 19855428).

Incativating mutations and deletions of MAX have been described in the germline of patients with pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas, have been described as somatic mutations in small cell lung cancer and are associated with loss of heterozygosity. Loss of MAX function is thought to enhance the oncogenic functions of MYC, a known MAX-interacting protein and cancer oncogene (PMID: 24362264). In vitro experiments demonstrated that rescue of MAX protein expression in MAX-null cells resulted in decreased cell proliferation (PMID: 24362264). MAX inactivation may synergize with loss of BRG1 to promote cell growth (PMID: 24362264).

The MAX R36W mutation is located in the helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in plasma cell myeloma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29563506). In vitro fluorescence polarization assays with MAX R36W demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by abolished DNA binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 27903915).

The MAX R60Q mutation is located in the basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLHZ) domain of MAX (PMID: 26070438, 27799065, 27903915).  This mutation has been found in acute myeloid leukemia, multiple myelomas, gliomas, pheochromocytomas, endometrial cancers, colorectal and stomach cancers, and poorly differentiated carcinomas (PMID: 26070438, 27799065, 27903915, 29596783). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as shown by reduced MAX binding to its consensus DNA sequence, and expression of this mutation in a pheochromocytoma cell line (PC12) led to reduced activity in comparison to wildtype (PMID: 27799065, 27903915).

The MAX H28R mutation is located in the helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrioid carcinoma and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 29155953). In vitro studies with endometrioid carcinoma cell lines expressing MAX H28R demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by increased affinity for canonical E-box sequences altering transcriptional profile and increased VEGFA expression compared to wildtype (PMID: 29155953).

MAX truncating mutations have been described in the germline of patients with pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas, have been described as somatic mutations in small cell lung cancer and are associated with loss of heterozygosity. MAX inactivating mutations are thought to enhance the oncogenic functions of MYC, a known MAX-interacting protein and cancer oncogene (PMID: 24362264).

The MAX R35H mutation is located in the helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in plasma cell myeloma (PMID: 22573403). In vitro fluorescence polarization assays with MAX R35H demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by abolished DNA binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 27903915).

The MAX R60W mutation is located in the basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLHZ) domain of the protein (PMID: 26070438, 27799065, 27903915).  This mutation has been found in multiple myelomas and pheochromocytomas (PMID: 26070438,  27903915). A study carried out in the PC12 pheochromocytoma cell line demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating as measured by the reduced ability of MAX to inhibit the expression of a reporter gene in comparison to wild-type (PMID: 26070438).

Amplification of MYB typically results in the overexpression of the protein. MYB amplification has been identified in non-Hodgkin lymphoma, colorectal cancer and breast cancer (PMID: 2204478, 3652034, 27197202). In vitro studies with SACC-83 cells overexpressing MYB demonstrate that amplification is activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation, migration and invasion compared to vector control (PMID: 30896785).

The MYB-NFIB rearrangement results from the MYB N-terminus fusing with the NFIB C-terminus, resulting in the loss of the MYB negative regulatory domain. This fusion has been identified in breast cancer, head and neck cancer and adenoid cystic carcinoma (PMID: 19841262, 21164292). In vitro studies with MCF10A cells expressing MYB-NFIB demonstrate that the mutation is activating as measured by increased cellular proliferation and survival compared to vector control (PMID: 32001675, 25587024).

The MYB-QKI rearrangement results from the MYB N-terminus fusing with the QKI C-terminus, resulting in the loss of the MYB negative regulatory domain. This fusion has been identified in angiocentric glioma (PMID: 26829751). In vivo studies with mice expressing MYB-QKI demonstrate that the fusion is activating as measured by increased tumor formation compared to vector control (PMID: 26829751).

The MAX R35L mutation is located in the helix-loop-helix DNA-binding domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in gastrointestinal stromal tumors (PMID: 28481359). In vitro fluorescence polarization assays with MAX R35L demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by abolished DNA binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 27903915).

MYOD1 truncating mutations typically result in the loss of protein function. In vitro studies with MYOD1-knockout myoblast cells demonstrate that loss of MYOD1 is inactivating as measured by resistance to apoptosis and increased cellular proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 17940048).

MYOD1 deletion mutations typically result in the loss of protein expression. In vitro studies with MYOD1-knockout myoblast cells demonstrate that loss of MYOD1 is inactivating as measured by resistance to apoptosis and increased cellular proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 17940048).

The NOTCH3 1_1972trunc mutations occur in the N-terminal and typically results in N-terminal fragments of NOTCH3. Truncating mutations in this range have been identified in patients with leukoencephalopathy (PMID: 25870235). Truncated N-terminal transcripts of NOTCH3 have been identified as inactivating as measured by impaired NOTCH3 signaling and abolished NOTCH3 expression (PMID: 25870235, 19825845).

The MYOD1 L122R mutation is located within the DNA binding domain of MYOD1. This mutation has been found in spindle cell rhabdomyosarcoma (PMID: 24272621). While this mutant is able to bind consensus MYOD1 binding sites, it does not lead to transcription of target genes, thereby competing with wildtype MYOD1 and in effect functioning as a dominant-negative (PMID: 24793135, 1329087). MYOD1 L122R binds to MYC binding sites, promotes cell cycle progression and transforms the basic domain of MYOD1 to the analogous MYC basic domain (PMID: 1329087). MYOD1 L122R has been implicated as a potential prognostic marker for rhabdomyosarcoma as the mutation has been identified in patients with aggressive rhabdomyosarcoma demonstrating poor outcome and limited response to therapy (PMID: 30181563).

The NOTCH3 1972_2321trunc mutations occur in the C-terminus and result in the loss of the negative regulatory PEST domain. Truncating mutations in this range have been identified in patients with lateral meningocele syndrome (PMID: 25394726). The C-terminal PEST domain functions in the negative regulation of protein stability by promoting degradation (PMID: 27157619). Loss of the NOTCH3 PEST domain through truncation mutations is suggested to be activating through increasing the NOTCH intracellular domain half-life and stability, leading to increased signaling activity (PMID: 25394726, 27157619).

The NUP93 Y629C mutation is located in the C-terminal coiled domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Expression of this mutation in podocyte and embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by reduced binding to coactivators, reduced downstream signaling and SMAD-dependent transcription dysregulation (PMID: 26878725).

The NUP93 G591V mutation is located in the C-terminal coiled domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (PMID: 31517150). Expression of this mutation in podocyte and embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by reduced binding to coactivators, reduced downstream signaling and SMAD-dependent transcription dysregulation (PMID: 26878725).

The NUP93 E14K mutation is located in the N-terminal region of the protein. This mutation has been identified in breast cancer and is a statistically significant hotspot (PMID: 22722193). In vitro studies with MCF10A cells and in vivo studies with mice expressing NUP93 E14K demonstrate that the mutation is inactivating as measured by increased colony formation, migration, invasion and metastasis compared to wildtype (PMID: 35196484).

The NUP93 K442Nfs* mutation is located in the C-terminal coiled domain of the protein. This mutation has been found as a germline mutation in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Expression of this mutation in podocyte and embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by reduced binding to coactivators, reduced downstream signaling and SMAD-dependent transcription dysregulation (PMID: 26878725).

Deletion of NUP93 exon 13 has been found as a germline mutation in steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome. Expression of this deletion in podocyte and embryonic kidney cells demonstrated that it is likely inactivating as measured by reduced binding to coactivators, reduced downstream signaling and SMAD-dependent transcription dysregulation (PMID: 26878725).

PARP1 truncating mutations occur throughout the gene and typically result in loss of the protein. In vitro studies with PARP1-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts demonstrated loss of PARP1 is inactivating as measured by reduced p53 induction and expression (PMID: 9285557).

Truncating mutations in PHOX2B occur across the gene and can lead to a variety of cellular effects (PMID: 23873030, 27129232). PHOX2B is a transcription factor of the paired family of homeobox proteins that is involved in neurologic development. Loss of certain key residues by truncation induces abnormal cellular localization of a calcium sensor involved in neuronal differentiation and tumorigenesis (PMID: 23873030). Germline mutations in PHOX2B are associated with Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome (PMID: 15888479, 18079495) and Neuroblastoma 2, a cancer syndrome (PMID: 15338462).

PARP1 deletion results in the loss of the protein. In vivo studies with PARP1-null mice demonstrate that loss of PARP1 is inactivating as measured by decreased TP53 induction and expression compared to wildtype expression (PMID: 9285557).

The PIK3R2 K376N mutation is located in the SH2 1 domain of the protein. This mutation has been observed in endometrial carcinomas (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated PIK3R2 A727V is likely neutral as measured by cell viability and downstream signaling via AKT comparable to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R2 G373R mutation is located in the SH2 1 domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in lobular carcinoma and endometrial carcinoma (PMID: 28481359, 28481359). In vitro studies with lymphoblastoid cell lines expressing this mutation demonstrated PIK3R2 G373R is activating as measured by increased tumorigenesis, cellular proliferation and PI3K signaling (PMID: 22729224). Notably, the germline G373R variant has been observed to occur mosaically, and megalencephaly and other disorders have been shown to occur despite this mosaicism (PMID: 26520804).

The PIK3R2 D557H mutation affects a highly conserved residue at the interface with PIK3CA. Mutations in PIK3R2 are associated with developmental brain disorders including megalencephaly-polymicrogyria-polydactyl-hydrocephalus (MPPH) and bilaterla perisylvian polymicrogyria (BPP) (PMID: 26520804). A single patient with MPPH and BPP harbored a de novo PIK3R2 D557H mutation, implicating this varaint as a contributing factor to the disease (PMID: 26860062).

The PIK3R2 S273C mutation is located in the RHO-GAP domain of the protein. This mutation has been observed in endometrial carcinomas (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated PIK3R2 S273C is likely neutral as measured by cell viability and downstream signaling via AKT comparable to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R2 N561D mutation is located in an unknown functional domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrial carcinoma (PMID: 21984976). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrated PIK3R2 N561D is activating as measured by increased PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling and IL-3-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R2 A36E mutation is located in the SH3 domain of the protein. This mutation has been observed in endometrial carcinomas (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated PIK3R2 A36E is likely neutral as measured by cell viability and downstream signaling via AKT comparable to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

PIK3R2 truncating mutations occur throughout the gene and typically result in loss of protein function. These mutations have been identified in patients with SHORT syndrome (PMID: 23810382). Expression of a PIK3R2 truncating mutation in lymphoblastoid cells demonstrated that these mutations are likely inactivating as measured by reduced downstream signaling compared to wildtype (PMID: 23810382).

The PIK3R2 A171V mutation is located in the RHO-GAP domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in endometrial cancer (PMID: 21984976). In vitro studies with Ba/F3 cells expressing this mutation demonstrate PIK3R2 A171V is activating as measured by increased PI3K-AKT-MTOR signaling and IL-3-independent proliferation compared to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

The PIK3R2 A727V mutation is located in the C-terminus of the protein. This mutation has been found in endometrial carcinomas (PMID: 21984976). Expression of this mutation in Ba/F3 cells demonstrated PIK3R2 A727V is likely neutral as measured by cell viability and downstream signaling via AKT comparable to wildtype (PMID: 21984976).

Genomic amplification of PIK3R2 increases the number of copies of PIK3R2 in the genome, and can lead to increased transcription of the gene. In turn, increased transcription of PIK3R2 may increase activation of the Pi3K signaling pathway and its associated downstream targets. Although the consequences of PIK3R2 amplification have not been thoroughly investigated across multiple cancer lineages, in glioblastoma multiforme, amplification of PIK3R2 was predicted to lead to an increase in phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5 trisphosphate and increased signaling via the AKT/mTOR (mammalian target of rapamycin) pathway (PMID: 25502460).

Truncating mutations in PPP6C occur throughout the gene and are predicted to lead to a truncated, non-functional protein. These mutations have been identified in melanoma (PMID: 33789117). In vitro studies with PPP6C-silenced 501mel cells demonstrate loss of PPP6C is inactivating as measured by aberrant ERK signaling from loss of negative regulatory function compared to wildtype (PMID: 33789117).

The PLCG2 L845F mutation is located within the SH3 domain of the PLCG2 autoregulatory region. This mutation was found in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia who relapsed following treatment with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor ibrutinib. Expression of this mutation in HEK293 and DT40 cells demonstrated that it is activating and resistant to treatment, as shown by sustained B-cell receptor signaling in the presence of ibrutinib compared to wildtype PLCG2 (PMID: 24869598).

The PLCG2 R665W mutation is located within the SH2 domain of the PLCG2 autoregulatory region. This mutation was found in patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) who relapsed following treatment with the tyrosine kinase inhibitor ibrutinib. Expression of this mutation in HEK293 and DT40 cells demonstrated that it is activating and resistant to treatment, as shown by sustained B-cell receptor signaling in the presence of ibrutinib compared to wildtype PLCG2 (PMID: 25972157, 24869598). In vitro studies of cells expressing PLCG2 R665W suggest that this mutation is sensitive to SYK and LYN kinase inhibition (PMID: 24869598).

The PPP6C S270L mutation is located in the metallophos domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 33789117). In vitro studies with HEK293 cells expressing this mutation demonstrate PPP6C S270L is inactivating as measured by increased degradation of PPP6C, decreased binding of PPP6C to the PP6C regulatory subunits and reduced catalytic activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 23729733).

Truncating mutations in the PPM1D gene cluster in the C-terminal portion of the protein in exon 6 and confer a gain-of-function activity. PPM1D truncating mutations result in several C-terminally truncated versions of the PPM1D protein and are found in patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms (PMID: 30304655). PPM1D negatively regulates many proteins by dephosphorylation, including the tumor suppressor TP53 (PMID: 25742468). HeLa cells transfected with the truncating PPM1D E525* mutation displayed increased protein stability (PMID: 23907125). In a separate study, the PPM1D truncating mutants, E472* and E540*, attenuated p53 and H2AX activation (DNA damage response mediators) following irradiation of 293T cells. Additionally, the HCT116 colorectal cell line harboring the PPM1D L450* mutation showed lower CHK2 and p53 phosphorylation levels and increased cell growth and colony formation; this was reversed when inverting the genotype to PPM1D wildtype (PMID: 24880341). In vivo studies with mice expressing a frameshift mutation in exon 6 of PPM1D demonstrate that truncating mutations in the last exon are activating as measured by increased development of acute myeloid leukemia after sequential exposure to ionizing radiation compared to wildtype mice (PMID: 37709843). Preclinical studies with PPM1D-mutant hematopoietic cells and mouse models show that PPM1D truncating mutations confer resistance to chemotherapeutic agents but are sensitive to an allosteric, small molecule inhibitor of PPM1D, GSK2830371 (PMID: 29954749, 37709843).

The PPP6C P186S mutation is located in the metallophos domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 33789117). In vitro studies with HEK293 cells expressing this mutation demonstrate PPP6C P186S is inactivating as measured by increased degradation of PPP6C, decreased binding of PPP6C to the PP6C regulatory subunits and reduced catalytic activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 23729733).

The PPP6C R264C mutation is located in the metallophos domain of the protein. This mutation has been identified in melanoma (PMID: 33789117). In vitro studies with HEK293 cells expressing this mutation demonstrate PPP6C R264C is inactivating as measured by increased degradation of PPP6C, decreased binding of PPP6C to the PP6C regulatory subunits and reduced catalytic activity compared to wildtype (PMID: 23729733).

The PREX2 E824* mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma. Expression of this mutation in melanocytes as well as in a transgenic model of melanoma demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activity, increased tumor growth, and decreased survival in xenograft and transgenic models compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578, 26884185).

The PREX2 G258V mutation is located in the plekstrin homology domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hepatocellular carcinoma. Expression of this mutation in a liver cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 30796242).

The PREX2 K278* mutation is located in the pleckstrin homology domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 22622578, 26884185). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes demonstrated that it was activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activity and decreased tumor-free survival in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578, 26884185).

The PREX2 Q1430* mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 22622578, 26884185). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased protein and pathway activity and decreased tumor-free survival in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578, 26884185).

PPM1D amplifications are predicted to result in increased PPM1D protein expression. PPM1D amplifications are likely oncogenic as increased expression of PPM1D in mantle cell lymphoma patients is correlated with higher expression of a proliferation gene expression signature and poorer prognosis (PMID: 27626308). Cells with increased PPM1D expression and wildtype p53 were sensitive to the PPM1D inhibitor, GSK2830371, as measured by decreased pathway activation and cell proliferation (PMID: 27626308, 26883108).

The PPP6C H114Y mutation alters a residue that is highly conserved among multiple protein phosphatases. Expression of the H114Y mutant protein resulted in decreased binding to the PP6C regulatory subunits and increased degradation of PPP6C. Catalytic activity of the H114Y mutant protein was significantly reduced as compared to that of wildytpe PPP6C. In addition, Aurora-A, the downstream target of PPP6C phosphatase activity, displayed increased phosphorylation and activity, further suggesting that the H114Y mutation resulted in decreased PPP6C catalytic activity. Cells expressing the H114Y mutant displayed increased genomic instability suggesting genomic instability as a mechanism for the oncogenic effects of the H114Y mutation (PMID: 23729733).

The PREX2 G844D mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 22622578, 26884185). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes demonstrated that it was activating as measured by decreased tumor-free survival in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes in another study showed no change in PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PMID: 26884185).

The PREX2 G106E mutation is located in the DBL homology domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 22622578, 26884185). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes demonstrated that it was neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding and no change in survival in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578, 26884185).

The PREX2 T868I mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26884185, 22622578). Expression of this mutation in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PIMD: 26884185).

The PREX2 V1441F mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26884185, 22622578). Expression of this mutation in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PIMD: 26884185).

The PREX2 A1376V mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26884185, 22622578). Expression of this mutation in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PIMD: 26884185).

The PREX2 E1346D mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hepatocellular carcinoma. Expression of this mutation in a liver cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 30796242).

The PREX2 S1113R mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hepatocellular carcinoma. Expression of this mutation in a liver cell line demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased protein stability, pathway activation, cell proliferation and migration compared to wildtype (PMID: 30796242).

The PREX2 P1145S mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26884185, 22622578). Expression of this mutation in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PIMD: 26884185).

The PREX2 P948S mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 22622578, 26884185). Expression of this mutation in melanocytes demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in PTEN binding and no change in survival in a xenograft model compared to wildtype (PMID: 22622578, 26884185).

The PREX2 L50V mutation is located in the DBL homology domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hepatocellular carcinoma. Expression of this mutation in a liver cell line demonstrated that it is likely activating as measured by increased protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 30796242).

The PREX2 K400* mutation is located in the dishevelled, Egl-10, and pleckstrin domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in hepatocellular carcinoma. Expression of this mutation in a liver cell line demonstrated that it is inactivating as measured by decreased protein stability compared to wildtype (PMID: 30796242).

The PREX2 T994A mutation is located in the inositol phosphatase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in melanoma (PMID: 26884185, 22622578). Expression of this mutation in a melanoma cell line demonstrated that it is likely neutral as measured by no change in protein GEF activity or PTEN binding compared to wildtype (PIMD: 26884185).

Truncating mutations in gene occur throughout the entire gene and are predicted to lead to loss of this protein. gene is a component of a multiprotein E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that is involved in Parkinson disease through a mechanism that leads to defects in mitophagy (PMID: 29995846, 31409571, 27593930). gene loss has been shown to lead to tumorigenesis through a mechanism that involves redox-mediated inactivation of PTEN by S-nitrosylation (PMID: 29209642, 28306514). Loss of gene has been reported in ovarian, breast and lung carcinomas and can occur through a variety of mechanisms including truncating mutations (PMID: 27593930).

The PTPRT R453C mutation lies within the fibronectin type-III repeats of the PTPRT protein. While expression of wildtype PTPRT in insect Sf9 cells has been shown to promote cellular aggregation, expression of the R453C mutant failed to induce cellular aggregation suggesting this mutation confesr loss of wildtype PTPRT activity (PMID: 20230342).

The PTPRT N510K mutation lies within the fibronectin type-III repeats of the PTPRT protein. While expression of wildtype PTPRT in insect Sf9 cells has been shown to promote cellular aggregation, expression of the N510K mutant failed to induce cellular aggregation suggesting this mutation confers loss of wildtype PTPRT activity (PMID: 20230342).

The PTPRT K218T mutation lies within the Immunoglobulin domain of PTPRT. While expression of wildtype PTPRT in insect Sf9 cells has been shown to promote cellular aggregation, expression of the K218T mutant failed to induce cellular aggregation suggesting this mutation confers loss of wildtype PTPRT activity (PMID: 18644975)

The PTPRT Y412F mutation lies within the fibronectin type-III repeats of the PTPRT protein. Cell line experiments of cell growth of PTPRT harboring a truncating mutation was associated with the loss of the inhibitory effect of PTPRT on cell growth (PMID: 15155950).

Analysis of The Cancer Genome Atlas data showed that hypermethylation of the promoter was observed in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC), in breast invasive carcinoma and in colon and lung adenocarcinoma. In HNSCC, hypermethylation of the promoter was associated with downregulation of PTPRT mRNA expression and hyperphopshorylation of its substrate STAT3. Treatment of HNSCC cells with hypermethylated PTPRT with a non specific DNA methyltransferase inhibitor (5-azacytidine), resulted in demethylation of the PTPRT promoter and subsequently induction of expression of PTPRT protein and dowregulation of phopshorylated STAT3 (PMID: 25982282). A second study analyzed the methylation of PTPRT in spradic colorectal cancers (CRC) and showed that hypermethylation of the promoter is significantly higher in the tumor cells versus normal tissue (PMID: 23096495). An additional study in human gastric carcinomas showed presence of hypermethylated CpG islands in the promoter and exon 1 of PTPRT gene (PMID: 25009298).

The RAD51C R193W mutation has not been functionally characterized. However, it was identified as a secondary mutation following treatment with the PARP-inhibitor, rucaparib, in a patient with high-grade ovarian carcinoma whose primary tumor harbored the RAD51C R193* truncating mutation. In this context, the H192delinsGG mutation restored the RAD51C open reading frame, potentially leading to PARP-inhibitor resistance (PMID: 28588062).

The RAD51C L138F mutation is located in the N-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and ovarian cancers (PMID: 20400964). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely inactivating, as evidenced by decreased binding to BRCA2 of the mutant compared to wildtype, as well as the inability to rescue sensitivity to mitomycin C and decreased RAD51C foci formation in RAD51C-mutated cells expressing the mutant compared to wildtype (PMID: 24141787, 20400964).

The RAD51C R193L mutation has not been functionally characterized. However, it was identified as a secondary mutation following treatment with the PARP-inhibitor, rucaparib, in a patient with high-grade ovarian carcinoma whose primary tumor harbored the RAD51C R193* truncating mutation. In this context, the R193L mutation restored the RAD51C open reading frame, potentially leading to PARP-inhibitor resistance (PMID: 28588062).

RAD51C is a tumor suppressor and truncating mutations in this gene are assumed to be oncogenic. Homozygous missense mutations in the RAD51C gene can cause Fanconi-anemia like disorders (PMID:20400963). Furthermore, multiple types of germline mutations in RAD51C establish it as a highly penetrant susceptibility gene for breast and ovarian cancer (PMID:21616938,20400964).

The RAD51C R258H mutation is located in the C-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in Fanconi anemia (PMID: 20400963). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely inactivating as evidenced by reduced binding to BRCA2 of the mutant compared to wildtype, as well as the inability to rescue sensitivity to mitomycin C and decreased RAD51C foci formation in RAD51C-mutated cells expressing the mutant compared to wildtype (PMID: 24141787, 20400963).

The RAD51C A126T mutation occurs in a conserved domain of the RAD51C protein. This mutation has been reported as a germline risk allele for breast cancer with moderate penetrance, but this notion is disproved by recent studies and its frequency in the general population (PMID: 21990120, 20400964, 26261251, [ExAC]). In separate in vitro assays, in chicken B cell, skin fibroblast and yeast cells, respectively, the mutation was demonstrated to have no effect on RAD51C function indicating that this mutation is neutral (PMID: 20400964, 21980511).

The RAD51C G264S is located in the Rad51 domain of the RAD51C protein. This mutation has been reported as a germline risk allele for breast cancer with moderate penetrance, but this notion is disproved by recent studies and its frequency in the general population (PMID: 21990120, 20400964, 26261251, [ExAC]). In separate in vitro assays, in chicken B cell and fibroblast, respectively, the mutation was demonstrated to have no effect on RAD51C function indicating that this mutation is neutral (PMID: 20400964).

The RAD51C H192delinsGG mutation has not been functionally characterized. However, it was identified as a secondary mutation following treatment with the PARP-inhibitor, rucaparib, in a patient with high-grade ovarian carcinoma whose primary tumor harbored the RAD51C R193* truncating mutation. In this context, the H192delinsGG mutation restored the RAD51C open reading frame, potentially leading to PARP-inhibitor resistance (PMID: 28588062).

The RAD51C D159N mutation is located in the N-terminal domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast and ovarian cancers (PMID: 20400964). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is likely inactivating as measured by decreased binding to BRCA2, decreased ability to rescue G2 arrest, increased cell death and increased chromatid breaks after exposure of RAD51C-deficient cells to DNA-damaging agents when the mutant is overexpressed compared to wildtype (PMID: 24141787, 22167183).

Truncating mutations in RAD51D lead to inactivation of protein function and germline mutations may confer a predisposition to ovarian cancer (PMID: 22986143,23372765). Cell line experiments have demonstrated that knockdown of RAD51D in breast cancer cells is associated with sensitivity to the PARP inhibitor olaparib (PMID: 21822267).

The RAD51D S207L mutation is located in the ATPase domain of the protein. This mutation has been found in ovarian and breast cancers (PMID: 22986143, 26845104, 26976419). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating, as measured by decreased formation of RAD51 foci at double-strand break sites, reduced levels of RAD51-XRCC2 co-immunoprecipitation and increased sensitivity to PARP inhibitors compared to wildtype (PMID: 28646019).

The RAD51D S257_R259delinsK mutation has not been functionally characterized. However, it was identified as a secondary mutation following treatment with the PARP-inhibitor, rucaparib, in a patient with high-grade ovarian carcinoma whose primary tumor harbored the RAD51D G258Sfs*50 truncating mutation. In this context, the S257_R259delinsK mutation restored the RAD51D open reading frame, potentially leading to PARP-inhibitor resistance (PMID: 28588062).

Truncating mutations in RECQL4 can occur anywhere in the gene and are predicted to disrupt its activity (PMID: 18716613). RECQL encodes a member of the RecQ DNA helicase family and has been shown to be involved in several types of DNA damage repair (PMID: 23842644). Germline truncating mutations in RECQL4 have been shown to be associated with Rothmund-Thomson (RTS), Balle-Gerold (BGS) and RAPADILINO syndromes, which are hereditary conditions characterized by skin and skeletal abnormalities (PMID: 12734318, 18716613, 15897384). Truncating mutations in RECQL4 have been identified in patients with osteogenic sarcomas and lymphomas as well as other carcinomas (PMID: 28481359, 12734318).

The RRAS2 G23V mutation is located in the P-loop of the protein. This mutation has been shown to lead to a constitutively active gene product, with a subsequent increase in PI3K pathway activity and tumorigenesis (PMID: 24826867).

The RRAS2 Q72L mutation was found to be activating when expressed in NIH3T3 cells, as measured by increased colony formation when compared to other library constructs used (PMID: 11850823). This mutation is analogous to other activating RAS mutations, such as Q61R (PMID: 26619011).

The RAD54L G325R mutation is located in the helicase motif (III) of the protein. This mutation has been found in breast cancer (PMID: 10362365). In vitro studies have demonstrated that this mutation is inactivating, as measured by reduced homologous recombination rates and increased sensitivity to DNA damaging agents compared to wildtype (PMID: 10362365, 15056673).

The RRAS2 G24D mutation is located in the P-loop of the protein and is analogous to codon 13 of KRAS/NRAS/HRAS (PMID: 26619011). Expression of this mutation in NIH3T3 cells and in vivo in a mouse model demonstrated that it is activating as measured by increased transformation in a focus formation assay and increased tumor formation in mice compared to wildtype (Abstract: Watanabe et al. Oral Med Pathol, 2006. https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/omp/11/4/11_4_121/_pdf/-char/en).

Truncating mutations in SH2B3 can occur throughout the entire gene and are predicted to lead to loss of its protein product (PMID: 29625055). SH2B3 encodes a member of the SH2B adaptor family of proteins, which are involved in growth factor and cytokine-mediated signaling (PMID: 26974155, 25776072). Through these mechanisms, SH2B3  has been shown to act as a key negative regulator of cytokine signaling and plays a critical role in hematopoiesis (PMID: 30254368). Mutations in SH2B3 have been implicated in the development of myeloproliferative neoplasms (PMID: 21922527, 28484264). Truncating mutations in SH2B3 have been identified in multiple malignancies including uterine, colorectal and several other carcinomas (PMID: 29625055).

Truncating mutations in SDHAF2 can occur anywhere throughout the gene and are predicted to lead to loss of its protein product (PMID: 29625055). SDHAF2 encodes an assembly factor of the Succinate Dehydrogenase (SDH) complex, an enzyme that is part of the Krebs cycle and complex II of the respiratory chain (PMID: 20226277). Loss of SDH expression has been shown to lead to succinate accumulation, which behaves as an oncometabolite to induce tumor formation (PMID: 31039394). Germline mutations in SDHAF2 have been associated with the development of paragangliomas through a mechanism that involves loss of SDH (PMID: 28384794, 28099933, 31687641). Truncating mutations in SDHAF2 have been identified in multiple malignancies including paragangliomas and several carcinomas (PMID: 28099933, 29625055).

The SH2B3 D231fs mutation is located in the PH domain of the protein. This mutation was identified as a homozygous germline mutation in familial acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Patient derived lymphoblastoid cells with homozygous D231fs mutations displayed a proliferative advantage over lymphoblastoid cells from a wildtype control. This proliferative advantage was inhibited by expression of the wildtype SH2B3. Mouse xenograft experiments show that the SH2B3 D23fs mutation accelerates NOTCH1-induced T-ALL (PMID: 23908464).

Expression of this mutation in HEK293T cells resulted in the inability of SMAD3 D408E to oligomerize with SMAD4, likely leading to decreased anti-proliferative TGFß-mediated transcription (PMID: 10092624).

The SH2B3 E208Q mutation is located in the PH domain of the protein. This mutation is found in patients with myeloproliferative neoplasms. Expression of this mutation in HEL cells, HEK293T cells and BaF3 cells stably expressing EPOR demonstrated that they are likely inactivating, as shown by slightly decreased downstream pathway inhibition and slightly increased colony formation compared to expression of wildtype SH2B3 (PMID: 23590807).
